papers.title: Feed-forward active magnetic shielding
papers.summary: Measurement of small magnetic fields requires shielding. For example, magnetoencephalography (MEG) measures small fields arising within the brain, in the presence of environmental fields several orders of magnitude larger. A common solution is passive shielding, but its cost, bulk and limited effectiveness motivate the alternative approach of active shielding, which comes in two flavours: feed-back and feed-forward. In feed-back shielding (the most common design), coils are driven from sensors that measure the corrected field. In feed-forward shielding (less common), coils are driven from sensors that measure the uncorrected field. The latter has the potential of providing better performance, but its implementation is hobbled by an inevitable coupling between coils and reference sensors. This paper describes an approach that employs a data-driven ``decoupling matrix" to suppress the coupling, enabling greater flexibility to achieve effective shielding across a wide frequency range. The method is evaluated by simulation, first using a simplified "flat world" in which the principle is clearly visualised, and then based on the more realistic geometry of a standard MEG system. Performance appears to be limited only by spatial sampling and numerical resolution. The method, which is data-driven and does not require geometric calculations, tight-tolerance fabrication, or manual calibration, is complementary with standard feed-back shielding methods. Active shielding is of particular interest in the context of a new generation of optically-pumped magnetometers (OPM), as the lower cost and reduced constraints of these new systems relative to SQUID-based systems provide an incentive to likewise reduce the cost and constraints of shielding.

papers.title: Coexistence of broadband conduction and amplitude-driven topological confinement in synthetic acoustic matter
papers.summary: Nonlinear and topological wave phenomena offer new opportunities for robust wave manipulation. Existing experimental platforms have largely focused on on-site (Kerr-like) nonlinearities within tight-binding frameworks, leaving the regime of programmable nonlinear inter-site coupling in far-field scattering systems essentially unexplored. Here we demonstrate a programmable acoustic metamaterial that exhibits amplitude-driven topological confinement of sound while simultaneously maintaining broadband linear transmission across the same frequency range. The system consists of an open acoustic waveguide coupled to a chain of actively controlled electroacoustic resonators enabling tunable nonlinear and nonlocal interactions. Using a classical wave-scattering model we show that increasing the excitation amplitude drives a robust topological interface mode localized deep within the structure, with the confinement strengthening continuously with drive rather than at a finite threshold. The predictions are verified experimentally using a fully programmable metacrystal composed of individually controlled acoustic resonators, enabling real-time manipulation of coupling parameters. The mode's topological origin is established by symmetry: it survives coupling disorder beyond 50% of nominal but collapses when a delay between adjacent couplings is introduced, effectively breaking the protecting chiral symmetry. These results establish a versatile platform for studying nonlinear topological wave physics and for designing adaptive acoustic metamaterials.

papers.title: Kernel Ridge Regression for conformer ensembles made easy with Structured Orthogonal Random Features
papers.summary: A computationally efficient protocol for machine learning in chemical space using Boltzmann ensembles of conformers as input is proposed; the method is based on rewriting Kernel Ridge Regression expressions in terms of Structured Orthogonal Random Features, yielding physics-motivated trigonometric neural networks. To evaluate the method's utility for materials discovery, we test it on experimental datasets of two quantities related to battery electrolyte design, namely oxidation potentials in acetonitrile and hydration energies, using several geometry- and orbital-based molecular representations to demonstrate the method's flexibility. Despite only using computationally cheap force field calculations for conformer generation and generating orbital representations with GFN2-xTB calculations, we observe systematic decrease of prediction errors with increased training set size in all cases, with experimental accuracy reached after training on hundreds of molecules.

papers.title: Unbeatable imitation of a friend
papers.summary: Imitation sometimes achieves success in multi-agent situations even though it is very simple. In repeated games, success of imitation has been characterized by unbeatability against other agents. Previous studies specified conditions under which imitation is unbeatable against co-players in repeated symmetric games, and clarified that the existence of unbeatable imitation is strongly related to the existence of payoff-controlling strategies, called zero-determinant strategies. However, these results were on the situations in which one repeated game is played by one group of players. It was pointed out that imitation of other players in the same group and imitation of other players in the same role in other groups generally result in different outcomes. Here, we investigate the existence condition of unbeatable imitation in the latter situations, described by two concurrent repeated games played by two different groups of players. We find that the existence condition of unbeatable imitation is stronger than the existence condition of unbeatable zero-determinant strategies, whereas both are very limited. Furthermore, we find that adding exploration can make an imitation strategy unbeatable even in games where imitation without exploration can be beaten. Our findings suggest a strong relation between unbeatable imitation and payoff control even in the two concurrent repeated game situations.

papers.title: Collective evolutionary dynamical-systems games: Emergent turn-taking under anonymous monitoring
papers.summary: Sustainable resource use in large societies requires institutions that define and enforce acceptable behaviour while keeping monitoring costs manageable. Here we show that such institutions can arise even when users observe only anonymised group-level information. Using the evolutionary dynamical-systems game framework, we model a common-pool resource management game. In the model, each player's harvesting decisions depend on the resource abundance, the player's wealth, and the group-average wealth. Strategies are encoded as two-parameter decision-making functions that mutate across generations. Evolutionary simulations reveal that players self-organise into clusters that alternate harvesting turns. A simple rule emerges, wait when wealthy, harvest when below average, which generates turn-taking patterns and robustness against selfish overharvesters. While the majority cluster tends to exploit the minority, moderate diversity in strategies allows "turn-taking of turns" between the majority and minority roles, improving efficiency, equity, and robustness. Moderate stochasticity in both resource dynamics and peer monitoring can enhance efficiency. The conditions for sustaining these institutions depend strongly on group size and demographic history. Gradual group expansion allows sustainability at substantially larger group sizes. These results provide a mechanistic account of the self-organisation of institutions under anonymous monitoring.

papers.title: Holistic Versus Fragmented Multiverses: Empirical Access via Causal and Grounding Signatures
papers.summary: Several objections have been raised against the scientificity of multiverse scenarios. This chapter defends the scientificity of certain multiverse scenarios by distinguishing fragmented from holistic multiverses. Concepts of multiverse used in physics are almost always holistic: they embed universes within a broader, unifying physical or metaphysical multiversal structure that can, in principle, leave empirical signatures inside the universes. I develop a classification of such signatures and show how it applies to a number of scenarios from quantum theory, cosmology, and string theory. The framework clarifies why objections such as the `this universe' objection and a newly articulated generalization, the epistemic isolation objection, fail against scientifically motivated multiverses.

papers.title: Der Stern von Bethlehem -- Einige Theorien und Hintergruende: Von der altorientalischen Astrologie ueber Kepler zu Newton
papers.summary: Many have have taken in hand to write a treatise on the Star of Bethlehem, particularly on Kepler's explanation as a stellar birth, triggered by Mars joining a great conjunction (a meeting of Jupiter and Saturn), as he observed it in October 1604. It is the aim of my short treatise to introduce, at a hopefully well digestible level, into underlying antiquity's concepts of physics, astrology, and astronomy around the time of Christ's birth and to demonstrate their essential developments up to the early modern period. In the latter, Kepler played a significant role. His contributions enabled him to calculate back to the year 7 BC with astonishing precision, locating a triple great conjunction in Pisces, which was then complemented by Mars. This is confirmed by both Babylonian tradition and modern astronomy. The following background provided may be specifically helpful for a more theologically oriented audience, also because the controversy surrounding "geocentric" and "heliocentric" world systems (Copernicus) is touched upon. And, because the overall context raises questions for theology, with which the epilogue concludes.

papers.title: Deposition rate and energy to substrate in chopped and standard HiPIMS: identifying optimal pulse parameters
papers.summary: High-Power Impulse Magnetron Sputtering (HiPIMS) delivers higher ionisation of the target material at the expense of lower deposition rates than conventional magnetron sputtering. A fine optimisation of the deposition conditions is crucial for specific applications. Chopped or multi-pulse HiPIMS (segmenting pulses into shorter micropulses) has been proposed to enhance the degree of ionisation of the film-forming flux fraction while maintaining the deposition rate. This study investigates how micropulse length and the delay time between segments influence energy flux, deposition rate, and the ionised flux fraction in both chopped and standard HiPIMS. These quantities are evaluated by passive thermal probe, biasable QCM and mass spectrometer measurements at the substrate position. Deposition-averaged and pulse-averaged power is kept constant for all conditions to facilitate meaningful comparison. Results indicate that chopping the HiPIMS pulse consistently leads to higher energy flux and total deposition rate compared to standard HiPIMS at the same total pulse length, primarily due to increased ion flux. In chopped HiPIMS, increasing the delay time between micropulses beyond 30 us simultaneously improved the deposition rate and the ionised flux fraction. In comparison, standard HiPIMS, operated at higher frequencies and shorter pulse lengths, demonstrated similar performance with even higher total energy fluxes, but this can be attributed to a higher fraction of process-gas ions in the flux to the substrate, rather than to an increased ionised flux fraction of the film-forming species.

papers.title: An integrated photonic millimeter-wave receiver with sub-ambient noise temperature
papers.summary: Growing demands for timing precision in positioning systems, and resolution in atmospheric sensing and automotive radar, have extended receiver frontends into the millimetre-wave and THz regimes. At these frequencies, the noise performance of field-effect transistors used in low-noise amplifiers degrades rapidly due to parasitic effects, limited carrier mobility, hot electrons, and shot noise. Parametric transducers that couple electromagnetic signals to optical fields can offer quantum-limited sensitivity at room temperature. Electro-optic materials can enable receivers that transduce radiofrequency signals into optical phase shifts. Yet to date, room-temperature receivers using electro-optical detection have not attained a noise figure comparable to the electronic amplifiers. Here we demonstrate a room-temperature cavity electro-optic-based millimetre-wave receiver on a lithium tantalate photonic integrated circuit, achieving an on-chip photon-number transduction efficiency of 10%. The equivalent input-referred receiver-added noise temperatures reach $110\,\mathrm{K}$ on-chip and $202^{+35}_{-33}\,\mathrm{K}$ for the full system at 60.5 GHz, with noise figure matching state-of-the-art V-band electronic low-noise amplifiers. We resolve the thermal noise in cavity electro-optic transducers, showing that the system is limited by thermal photon occupation ($\sim$100) in the millimetre-wave cavity and optical vacuum noise, with no measurable excess noise. Our work demonstrates that integrated photonics can reach state-of-the-art electronic receiver noise performance while offering high-radiofrequency-power survivability and compatibility with remote optical readout. This establishes cavity electro-optics as a low-noise, electromagnetic interference-resilient, chip-scale receiver frontend for millimetre-wave applications, enabling scalable analogue processing in the optical domain.

papers.title: Unlocking n-alk-1-ynes Conformers: Quantum "Trigger Finger" versus "Stiff Joint" Conformations
papers.summary: Molecular conformation in n-alk-1-ynes (CnA) is conventionally simplified to an all-planar structure. We report a comprehensive quantum chemical analysis revealing two near-isoenergetic rotamers at the acetylenic terminus: planar (C$_s$) and skewed (C$_1$). The high, symmetric rotational energy barrier ($\approx 150$\,meV) arises from unique steric relief near the $\mathrm{sp}$ center coupled with electronic stabilization of C$_1$. This creates a unique kinetic profile: a Quantum ``Trigger Finger'' ($\alpha$ rotation) that enforces an $\approx 50\%:\,50\%$ $\mathrm{C}_s/\mathrm{C}_1$ ensemble, sharply contrasting with the thermodynamically biased ``Stiff Joint'' ($\delta$ rotation) of the alkyl chain. This structural degeneracy necessitates ensemble averaging for spectroscopic data interpretation, while the slow interconversion permits kinetic trapping and intentional conformer enrichment during synthesis and molecular junction fabrication. Our work redefines the alkyne anchor, providing a blueprint for accurate interpretation of spectroscopic data and achieving conformational control in molecular electronics.

papers.title: Neural network approximation of regularized density functionals
papers.summary: We study neural-network approximation of density functionals in a Banach-space setting. Since the exact continuum functionals are discontinuous in the natural density topology, we apply $p$-Moreau-Yosida regularization. We construct finite-rank ReLU networks that preserve convexity and nonnegativity, lie below the regularized functional, and approximate it uniformly on compact sets. For energies obtained by minimization over compact density sets, we account exactly for the energy shift caused by regularization and bound the remaining error by the localization on these compact sets and network approximation errors. We apply this framework to canonical and grand-canonical density-functional theory at fixed particle number and fixed mean particle number, respectively. We obtain uniform energy convergence on norm-compact classes of external potentials, including molecular Coulomb potentials. We illustrate our results through numerical experiments on a simple model system.

papers.title: How Withheld Punishment Sustains Anti-Democratic Behavior in an Evolutionary Game
papers.summary: Democratic backsliding is often framed as a contest between defenders and disruptors of democratic institutions. That framing can miss a third response, withholding punishment from disruptors while penalizing defenders who confront them. We model the three responses as strategies in an evolutionary game, track their shares with replicator dynamics, and assume defenders beat disruptors head-to-head but have a payoff disadvantage among non-punishers even when disruptors are absent. If the third response cannot spread among disruptors, a payoff condition draws the population toward the classical May--Leonard heteroclinic cycle, a rock--paper--scissors succession in which disruption repeatedly becomes rare, then widespread. If that response can, a threshold on its payoff advantage over disruptors determines whether all three coexist or defenders alone vanish. In finite-population simulations, sustained resurgence requires reintroducing lost strategies. Our contribution is to show how two separately documented political tendencies, if combined, can sustain disruption despite defenders' head-to-head advantage over disruptors.

papers.title: Achieving angular-momentum conservation with physics-informed neural networks in computational relativistic spin hydrodynamics
papers.summary: We propose physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) as a numerical solver for relativistic spin hydrodynamics and demonstrate that the total angular momentum, i.e., the sum of orbital and spin angular momentum, is accurately conserved throughout the fluid evolution by imposing the conservation law directly in the loss function as a training target. This enables controlled numerical studies of the mutual conversion between spin and orbital angular momentum, a central feature of relativistic spin hydrodynamics driven by the rotational viscous effect. We present two physical scenarios with a rotating fluid confined in a cylindrical container: one case in which initial orbital angular momentum is converted into spin angular momentum in analogy with the Barnett effect, and the opposite case in which initial spin angular momentum is converted into orbital angular momentum in analogy with the Einstein-de Haas effect. We investigate these conversion processes governed by the rotational viscous effect by analyzing the spacetime profiles of thermal vorticity and spin potential. Our PINNs-based framework provides the first numerical evidence for spin-orbit angular momentum conversion with fully nonlinear computational relativistic spin hydrodynamics.

papers.title: Electric Field Gradients in Multiconfigurational Embedded-Cluster Calculations of Solids
papers.summary: The electric field gradients (EFGs) at the (non-spherical) nucleus contribute to atomic and molecular hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Electric field gradients (EFGs) at nuclei contribute to atomic hyperfine structure and govern Nuclear Quadrupole Resonance (NQR) and M\"ossbauer spectroscopy, providing a sensitive probe of local electronic structure and symmetry. EFGs can be obtained from electronic-structure calculations and inferred from spectroscopic measurements, linking theory and experiment. In this work, we use representative molecular and crystalline examples to examine selected factors that control calculated EFGs, with particular emphasis on multiconfigurational embedded-cluster calculations for solids. We analyze the sensitivity of EFGs to geometry and to computational choices including basis set, correlation treatment, and active-space construction. We also discuss differences in EFG tensor conventions adopted by commonly used quantum-chemistry codes and their implications for comparing computational results. Periodic calculations are used where appropriate as reference data for assessing the embedded-cluster description. Our results provide practical guidelines for the reliable computation and interpretation of EFGs as descriptors of the electronic structure and local chemical environment.

papers.title: Skillful Thunderstorm Forecasts Learned Directly from Observations
papers.summary: Nowcasting the evolution of severe convective storms over the first few hours after observations are collected is critical for issuing timely, accurate warnings. Forecast accuracy is hindered because the variables that matter most, such as rain, hail, and lightning, are imperfectly represented by numerical model physics and are difficult to initialize correctly. Here we introduce StormScope, a computationally efficient generative forecasting system that learns storm-scale evolution directly from satellite, radar, and lightning observations over the continental United States with no numerical model used for training or initialization. StormScope produces coherent, physically plausible storm trajectories with well-calibrated uncertainty. Across more than 900 forecasts, it greatly exceeds the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's state-of-the-art forthcoming operational numerical modeling system in both deterministic and probabilistic skill through the 0-2-h nowcasting window. StormScope's skill for strong radar echoes exceeds the operational state of the art by approximately 75% and 45% at lead times of 30 min and 2 h, a relative improvement several times larger than machine learning has delivered for global medium-range forecasting. Crucially, it also anticipates storms that develop after forecast initialization, establishing its utility beyond extrapolation of existing radar echoes. It likewise surpasses a leading AI nowcasting model for intense precipitation. Together, these results establish learning directly from observations as a route toward skillful, well-calibrated storm-scale forecasts that is unconstrained by the initialization and microphysics bottlenecks limiting numerical models and their emulators.

papers.title: Newtonian and Relativistic Particle Mechanics from Local Energy Conservation: A Symmetry-Selected Force-Energy Framework
papers.summary: We develop a formulation of particle mechanics in which the functional relation between force and kinetic energy is derived directly from the instantaneous (pointwise along the trajectory) conservation of mechanical energy $E$, rather than postulated through Newton's second law or a variational principle. Starting from the condition $\dot{E}=0$, we derive a generalized force law that does not assume a specific kinetic-energy function, momentum-velocity relation, or equation of motion. The resulting inertial response naturally decomposes into a component parallel to the acceleration, responsible for changes in kinetic energy, and a transverse component that preserves energy while altering the direction of motion. Imposing rotational equivariance constrains the geometric structure of the force law, while the relativity principle between inertial reference frames further restricts its admissible realizations. In strictly one-dimensional motion, inertial frame equivalence, supplemented by a set of five structural properties, implies invariance of the total force under inertial boosts; together with local energy conservation, this uniquely fixes the functional form of kinetic energy and momentum. Galilean invariance selects the Newtonian expressions, whereas Lorentz invariance yields the relativistic ones. The framework unifies conservative and non-conservative (yet non-dissipative, e.g., the magnetic Lorentz force) dynamics at the single-particle level and clarifies the precise conditions under which energy-based and variational formulations of mechanics are dynamically equivalent. Newtonian and relativistic mechanics thus emerge as symmetry-selected realizations of a common energy-conserving force-energy structure. The analysis further shows that the standard Lagrangian form $L=T-V$ is consistent with, and implicitly presupposes, Galilean relativity.

papers.title: A Computational Model for Flexoelectricity-Driven Contact Electrification
papers.summary: Recent theoretical studies show that nanoscale contact on dielectric substrates can induce flexoelectric polarization large enough to drive electron transfer. This has been supported by experimental evidence, indicating that contact electrification is inherently a coupled electromechanical phenomenon. In this work, we develop a computational model for flexoelectricity-driven contact electrification that integrates finite-deformation flexoelectricity with contact mechanics and physically motivated charge transfer. A tunneling transparency function is introduced to regulate the interfacial channel based on the WKB approximation, capturing the irreversible charge trapping during unloading. Three contact scenarios are investigated with specific hypotheses for charge transfer: unbiased metal-dielectric contact driven by surface polarization, biased contact restricted to carriers of a single polarity, and dielectric-dielectric contact where surface states with finite capacity limit the transferable charge. The model is compared with atomic force microscopy measurements on PMMA and PDAP substrates under both biased and unbiased conditions.For contact between identical dielectric materials, we show that geometric asymmetry in surface curvature is sufficient to induce charge separation, with polarity reversal occurring at a critical surface wavenumber. Three-dimensional simulations on random rough surfaces reproduce the mosaic charge distributions observed experimentally, confirming that contact-induced local strain gradient heterogeneity can generate spatially non-uniform charge patterns without introducing any material inhomogeneity.

papers.title: Streamwise periodic solver to simulate turbulent flow in finned channels with uniform isothermal walls
papers.summary: Assessment of the thermo-hydraulic performance of heat exchangers using computational fluid dynamics is a challenging task. The intricate geometries of a heat exchanger require a fine discretization of the flow passage, which consequently leads to high computational costs. A streamwise periodic flow model can significantly reduce this cost, particularly for heat exchangers featuring repeating structures. This manuscript presents the streamwise-periodic turbulent source terms for flows in channels with isothermal walls, along with the implementation of the corresponding periodic flow solver in the open-source CFD-Suite, SU2. The accuracy of the implemented solver was verified by comparing its predictions against those of a full fin array simulation for the test case of offset circular fins. The results show that the streamwise periodic flow solver accurately reproduces the solutions of the full array simulation under both laminar and turbulent flow conditions.

papers.title: Watch an AI Weather Model Learn (and Overshoot) Tropical Cyclones
papers.summary: In a changing climate, artificial intelligence (AI) weather models have the potential to provide cheaper, faster, and more accurate forecasts of high-impact weather events. To realize this potential and gauge trustworthiness, there is a need for more research on how models learn extreme events and how that learning might be improved. Here, we investigate how a Spherical Fourier Neural Operator (SFNO) learns tropical cyclones (TCs) by saving every checkpoint from training and analyzing storm-specific metrics. We find that a subset of storms show early TC intensity forecast skill that degrades into systematic overprediction in the second half of training. Moisture perturbation experiments show a causal relationship between anomalously moist environments and this skill degradation. This work provides a first example of leveraging task-specific training dynamics to further our understanding of how AI weather models learn extreme events.

papers.title: COACH: Toward the performance limit of traditional hybrid density functionals for molecular chemistry
papers.summary: Density functional theory (DFT) offers an exceptional balance between accuracy and efficiency, but practical density functional approximations face an unavoidable trade-off among simplicity, accuracy, and transferability. Here we present a systematic functional-development protocol that combines constraint enforcement, flexible functional forms, and modern optimization within a predefined application domain and functional class. Applying this strategy to the range-separated hybrid (RSH) meta-GGA framework, we obtain the carefully optimized and appropriately constrained hybrid (COACH) functional. Across broad molecular benchmarks, COACH improves both accuracy and transferability relative to leading RSH meta-GGAs, including \(\omega\)B97M-V, while retaining the computational practicality of its rung. These results suggest that COACH comes closer to the performance limit of traditional hybrid meta-GGA functionals for general molecular ground-state chemistry. Further substantial progress will likely require richer nonlocal or orbital-dependent information than is available from semilocal density ingredients combined with simple exact-exchange mixing.

papers.title: On Sub-Sevenfold Symmetries in LH2 Stacked Ring Scaffolds: A Quantum Optical Perspective
papers.summary: For highly efficient light-harvesting, purple photosynthetic bacteria rely on light-harvesting 2 (LH2) complexes featuring ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold rotational symmetries; however, sub-sevenfold scaffolds have not yet been observed in nature. To investigate this absence, we utilize a closed coupled-dipole model that neglects dissipative effects, which remains valid for a temporal window shorter than the interlayer excitation energy transfer time (on the picosecond scale) in an LH2 scaffold. We examine collective eigenmodes across $C_n$ stacked model ring geometries for $n=9,8,7,6$. Our results demonstrate that the minimum energy separation between specific collective bands occurs at the angular-momentum modes $m=\pm 1$ for known geometries, effectively predicting the photoactive absorption wavelengths of the lower bacteriochlorophyll (BChl) ring. Specifically, we predict peaks at 851, 848, and 825 nm for ninefold, eightfold, and sevenfold symmetries, respectively, which agree well with experimental observations. Applying this analysis to a hypothetical sixfold geometry, we predict a significant blue shift in the photoactive wavelength of the lower BChl ring, suggesting inefficient harvesting of the available solar spectrum and offering a quantum optical perspective on the evolutionary absence of sub-sevenfold scaffolds in LH2 complexes. Our study demonstrates that quantum cooperative models can elucidate specific aspects of biological LH systems.

papers.title: Noise-resilient nanophotonic gyroscope with sub-prad phase resolution
papers.summary: Optical gyroscopes based on the Sagnac effect are the cornerstone of precision orientation and navigation. However, their bulky form factors prevent deployment in emerging mobile and autonomous systems. On nanophotonic platforms, the Sagnac signal plummets under aggressive miniaturization. Consequently, the signal is easily swamped by refractive-index fluctuations, rendering navigation-grade sensitivity within just a few square millimeters a notoriously elusive goal. Here, we demonstrate a noise-resilient nanophotonic optical gyroscope by exploiting a two-chain decoupling architecture to effectively isolate the rotation signal from channel noise. Implemented on a 3 mm^2 passive silicon-nitride chip, the proof-of-concept device achieves a bias instability of 0.79 deg/h and an angle random walk of 0.0014 deg/\sqrt{h}, representing improvements of 4 and 6 orders of magnitude, respectively, over a representative nanophotonic gyroscope with the same enclosed sensing area (ref. 1). In the broader context of integrated optical gyroscopes, our approach bridges the long-standing size-performance gap by two to three orders of magnitude, moving chip-scale devices into a previously inaccessible regime and pointing toward navigation-relevant precision for monolithic microsystems. This architecture further enables an estimated input-equivalent phase resolution of 0.17 prad with general applicability, establishing a foundational framework for the next generation of robust, monolithically integrated photonic sensing systems.

papers.title: A Thin Sheet Volume Integral Equation Solver for Simulation of Bianisotropic Metasurfaces
papers.summary: A thin-sheet (TS) volume integral equation (VIE) formulation incorporating generalized sheet transition conditions (GSTCs) is presented for the simulation of three-dimensional (3D) bianisotropic metasurfaces. The metasurface is represented as an equivalent thin sheet, with its constitutive tensors derived from the GSTC susceptibility tensors. Invoking the thin-sheet approximation, the governing VIEs are reduced to surface integral equations (SIEs), in which tangential and normal flux density components are treated as distinct sets of unknowns and discretized using Rao-Wilton-Glisson and pulse basis functions, respectively. In contrast to conventional GSTC approaches based on conventional SIEs, which represent only tangential fields, the proposed framework rigorously enforces the bianisotropic GSTCs, including normal field interactions, while retaining the flux-based VIE character of the formulation. Numerical examples, including a comparison with an SIE-GSTC solver that neglects the normal susceptibility components, demonstrate the accuracy and robustness of the proposed TS-VIE-GSTC solver for polarization rotation on planar and curved sheets, perfect reflection, beam steering with spatially varying susceptibilities, multi-directional attenuation, and oblique phase-shift transformation.

papers.title: Biting fly vision and zebra stripes
papers.summary: The function of the zebras striped coat has been discussed since Darwin and Wallace. Increasing amount of comparative and experimental evidence supports the hypothesis that the stripes mainly serve as protection against visually orienting biting Diptera, in particular tabanids (horse flies), glossinids (tsetse flies), and culicids (mosquitoes). The proposed ways this protection works include polarotactic disruption and silhouette break-up, as well as motion based illusions in motion based detectors of the insect visual system. In this work a complementary purely optical mechanism is presented to explain why the zebra's stripe pattern provides a measurable advantage in warding off biting flies. We have quantified the optical illusion caused by the interaction between the zebra's striped coat and the fly's compound eye with a linear, shift-invariant Fourier model based on published optical data of the diurnal Culicidae. The model predicts that, within an approach range of about 1-5 m, the interaction of the stripe pattern with the ommatidial sampling produces parasitic spatial frequencies that are absent from the physical stimulus. These frequencies fall within the range most important for host fixation and controlling their landing. A post-retinal motion-detector shows that these parasitic frequencies create misleading motion signals. The magnitude of this parasitic energy predicts the specific loss of the radial-expansion (looming) cue that gates landing, linking the optical disturbance quantitatively to the motion computation that controls the fly's final approach. By rigorously modeling visual processes and quantifying disturbances, this study makes a decisive contribution to clarifying the role of zebra stripes in defense against biting flies.

papers.title: From Symmetry and Continuity to the Lorentz Transformation
papers.summary: We derive the Lorentz transformation from spacetime symmetries and continuity, without assuming the invariance of the speed of light. Spacetime homogeneity yields an additive coordinate map; continuity along four linearly independent inertial worldlines, together with additivity, establishes linearity throughout spacetime. Spatial isotropy and the assumed continuous local one-parameter group structure of collinear boosts yield velocity reciprocity and determine a generalized Lorentz-type family parameterized by $\kappa$. The velocity law and the empirical identification of its invariant speed with the coordinate speed of light in vacuum select the Lorentzian branch, fixing $\kappa=-1/c^2$ and recovering the Lorentz transformation.

papers.title: Absolute Experimental Measurement of Intrinsic Helicity in Elementary Plasmonic Nanostructures
papers.summary: Helicity is a universal quantity describing the internal rotation of an object or a field. Whether it characterizes fundamental properties such as the spin of elementary particles or leads to practical consequences such as the toxicity or harmlessness of chiral molecules, defining and measuring it is essential. However, this remains ambiguous in the case of chiral photonic systems such as plasmonic nanoparticles or photonic metasurfaces, where contrary to common knowledge, the observation of circularly polarized dependent optical properties is not a relevant measure for the helicity. We demonstrate experimentally and theoretically that the helicity can be rigorously defined and measured in a nanoplasmonics system emitting circularly polarized light after excitation in the near-field by a focused electron beam. In the case of a model system composed of two plasmonic dipoles (Born-Kuhn systems), we show that the helicity of photonic modes takes on a very intuitive form and can be simply measured by symmetrizing the geometry of excitation and detection. The method could be extended to a variety of chiral photonic systems, whose locally enhanced properties make them promising for the engineering of local chirality.

papers.title: Semi-analytical representation of the Gaunt-modified Landau-Lifshitz equation in a plane wave
papers.summary: We analyze electron dynamics in a plane electromagnetic wave using the Landau-Lifshitz equation with a quantum radiation reaction correction modelled by a Gaunt factor. In this geometry, the quantum parameter $\chi$ depends solely on the lightfront momentum, allowing the modified equation of motion to retain the integrable structure of the classical problem. We derive a semi-analytical solution for the energy evolution and the four-velocity, which reduces to the known classical result in the appropriate limit. The results provide an analytical and deterministic description of semiclassical radiation reaction in plane-wave fields.

papers.title: Boundary crossings as a minimal mechanism for global connectivity in structured landscapes
papers.summary: Global connectivity in complex systems often emerges from local interactions, yet it remains unclear whether sophisticated agent strategies are required for such reorganisation. Here we identify a minimal mechanism by which heterogeneous mobility can generate system-wide connectivity when agents move within a structured multi-attractor landscape. In an agent-based model, a small fraction of higher-mobility agents explores the environment while the majority remains locally constrained. Configurational transitions are strongly localised at inter-attractor boundaries, where local crossing events accumulate over time to produce an expanding transition network and a percolation-like shift from fragmented to globally connected regimes. The core phenomenon persists under pure random-walk dynamics, showing that neither optimisation nor goal-directed behaviour is necessary. Interface-sensitive exploration nevertheless increases the transition rate by approximately four- to fivefold per exploratory movement relative to the random-walk baseline, thereby accelerating network integration. A novelty term produces only a small and non-uniform additional rate increase and no consistent improvement in unique-edge production. By contrast, when landscape structure is removed, transition-network connectivity arises through unconstrained spatial mixing, eliminating the boundary-mediated interpretation of the process. These results identify a minimal mechanism through which simple stochastic movement and spatial constraints generate large-scale connectivity. Interfaces between basins emerge as critical mediators linking local dynamics to global organisation, with potential implications for systems in which movement occurs across structured environments.

papers.title: All-electron Dynamical Bethe-Salpeter Equation for Extended Systems with Atom-centered Orbital Basis
papers.summary: Solving Bethe-Salpeter equation (BSE) for the two-particle Green's function is the most widely used approach for taking into account the particle-hole (exciton) interaction in electronic excitation in the context of the many-body theory based on Green's function. In BSE calculations, the static approximation to the screened Coulomb interaction kernel is commonly employed. However, when the excitonic character is significant as typically indicated by a large exciton binding energy, dynamical screening effects become non-negligible, rendering the static approximation questionable. Because of the large computational cost due to the dense Brillouin zone integration necessary for convergence, solving the dynamical BSE for extended systems remains a significant challenge, especially when combined with GW calculation for the calculation of quasi-particle energies. In this work, we formulate the plane-wave based effective dielectric function method [Zhang, et al., Phys. Rev. B 107, 235205 (2023)] for the dynamical BSE calculation using atom-centered orbitals as basis functions. We implement this approach in our recently developed all-electron numerical atom-centered orbital (NAO) implementation of BSE@GW [Zhou, et. al. J. Chem. Theory Comput. 21, 291 (2025)] for extended systems. We validate our all-electron NAO-based implementation of the dynamical BSE method, and we then discuss its realistic application to molecular crystal of naphthalene by performing the dynamical BSE@G0W0 calculation.

papers.title: Virtual-Array Operational Modal Analysis of Rolling Tires Using a Single Tire Cavity Accelerometer
papers.summary: The dynamics of the rolling tire govern structure-borne road noise below 500 Hz. Laser Doppler vibrometry (LDV) is the established laboratory reference for measuring rolling-tire modes. This paper presents a complementary approach that uses a single wireless tire cavity accelerometer (TCA) mounted on the inner liner and a once-per-revolution encoder on the drum of a tire-on-drum rig fitted with a cleat. Because the drum-to-tire diameter ratio (2.74) is non-integer, successive cleat impacts encounter the TCA at different circumferential positions. The TCA's contact-patch signature locates the sensor at each impact within approximately $1^\circ$, and grouping the impact responses by angular position synthesizes a 36-element virtual array from a single 128 s run. Covariance-driven stochastic subspace identification (SSI-COV) is applied using a consensus rule across multiple parameter settings, bootstrap resampling over impacts, and a correction for window-induced damping; the complete signal-processing chain is verified on synthetic data with known modes. For a slick 195/65R15 tire rolling at 30 km/h under a 1334 N load, ten modes between 46 and 193 Hz are robustly identified, exhibiting circumferential wavenumbers from 1 to 5, damping ratios of 2.1--4.2%, and strongly complex mode shapes, with three additional modes identified tentatively. The extracted modes follow the wavenumber ladder of a stationary modal test of the same tire. Requiring no optical access and capturing the full virtual array in a single run, the proposed method is well suited to treaded tires and on-road testing, at the expense of in-tire sensor installation.

papers.title: Improvement of Heat-Treated Niobium Surface by In-situ Plasma Treatment Applied to Superconducting RF Resonator
papers.summary: A specific heat treatment at 300 C, named medium-temperature baking (Mid-T baking) is applied to superconducting radio-frequency (SRF) accelerating cavities to improve the quality factor (Qo) at medium accelerating fields (10 to 20 MV/m). This treatment is very successful when done properly as it can reduce by almost a factor of two the power dissipations in this field range. However, surface contamination can lead to the degradation of Qo instead. Plasma-based surface treatment provides an effective approach to eliminate contaminants from the Niobium surface. In this study an insitu plasma cleaning process with argon containing 10 % O2 was performed to remove hydrocarbons from Niobium surface. The treatment was applied before and after a heat treatment at 500 C under ultra-high vacuum conditions (Mid-T baking). Changes in chemical speciation and oxide layer alteration induced by plasma processing were analyzed using insitu X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) and exsitu scanning electron microscopy (SEM). The results show that plasma treatment modifies the composition of Niobium oxides, converting a Nb2O5 layer into NbO2. Furthermore, a plasma treatment before Mid-T baking helps reduce unstable oxides such as NbxO and significantly increases the proportion of metallic Niobium at the surface. The Niobium sample treated by plasma prior to Mid-T baking showed a 53 % reduction in carbide formation. Moreover, the C1s component attributed to NbC bonds shifts toward lower binding energy, indicating the formation of a more metallic NbC phase. Whereas without plasma treatment, the higher binding energy component observed after Mid T baking is consistent with Nb2C.

papers.title: Impedance of multilayer cylindrical structures with a material-filled beam region
papers.summary: Beam-coupling impedances in material media are relevant for ionization-cooling channels of a future muon collider, where the beam propagates in matter rather than vacuum. We extend the cylindrical field-matching formalism for multilayer structures to the case of a material-filled beam region surrounded by external layers with arbitrary electromagnetic properties. Relative to the vacuum formulation, the usual factor $1/\gamma^2$ is replaced by the material-dependent factor $F=1/\varepsilon_1-\mu_1\beta^2$, and the radial propagation constant is modified accordingly. Analytical expressions are obtained for the monopolar longitudinal and dipolar transverse impedances, with the surrounding structure encoded through reflection coefficients determined by field matching. The formalism reduces to the known vacuum and perfectly conducting limits in the appropriate cases. Representative calculations are presented for absorber-relevant configurations, illustrating the dependence on the material properties of both the beam region and the surrounding layers. In particular, a finite beam-region conductivity can generate a real impedance component and reverse the sign of the imaginary space-charge impedance, while sufficiently high permittivity can give rise to resonant structures associated with oscillatory radial fields. The effect of finite-conductivity surroundings is also examined, showing the approach towards the perfectly conducting limit as the external conductivity is increased. The applicability of the infinite-length approximation is also discussed by comparison with finite-length mode-matching results.

papers.title: Detachment dynamics and disturbance rejection in the TCV X-Point Target divertor
papers.summary: The X-Point Target (XPT) is an alternative divertor configuration with a secondary X-point in the divertor leg. We investigate its detachment dynamics and disturbance rejection capacity on the TCV tokamak, comparing it with a long-legged single-null (SN) divertor. We employ a system identification approach using multi-sine perturbations to D$_2$ fuelling in Ohmic L-mode scenarios and to N$_2$ seeding and electron cyclotron resonance heating (ECRH) power in auxiliary-heated L-mode scenarios, using the CIII emission front position as a proxy for the detached state evolution. For D$_2$ fuelling perturbations at 4-31 Hz, the gain of the front response at the secondary X-point is at least a factor of 3 lower than upstream of it, where the response is similar to that of the SN. This indicates that the reduced detachment sensitivity of the secondary X-point in an XPT configuration previously observed in quasi-steady state experiments, extends to control-relevant timescales as an enhanced disturbance rejection capacity. In auxiliary-heated scenarios, the CIII front in the XPT remains nearly stationary near the secondary X-point under N$_2$ seeding and ECRH power perturbations, whereas the CIII front in SN discharges responds strongly. However, due to complex SOL profiles in the region close to the secondary X-point of the XPT configuration, this reduction in CIII front response may not imply disturbance rejection of the detached state as a whole. The enhanced disturbance rejection at the secondary X-point could provide a passive buffer against disturbances, simplifying the task of exhaust controllers to maintain the detached state throughout a discharge cycle.

papers.title: Consistent Initial States with Constant Circuit Depth for Quantum Computational Chemistry
papers.summary: Variational quantum eigensolvers have been extensively studied, yet there are still no methods that offer black-box applicability with consistent performance. Separable pair approximations promise to be candidates for such methods: they compile to shallow constant-depth quantum circuits with linear gate count and parameter dependence and circumvent most bottlenecks of variational quantum algorithms through their classical simulability. At the same time, they seamlessly integrate into prominent more general circuit designs and subspace strategies. So far, their capability as a consistent method has only been indicated and demonstrations have been restricted to manually designed model systems. In this work, we extensively evaluate the consistency of SPA states for hydrogen chains, alkanes, and small molecules within an orbital-optimized VQE framework. Our benchmarks demonstrate consistent approximations with classical complexity comparable to Hartree-Fock. While SPA can serve as a useful low-cost standalone approximation, its restriction to the seniority-zero subspace makes it best suited as a scalable, chemically consistent initial state for more expressive correlation treatments when high quantitative accuracy is required. Our open-source implementation within the \textsc{tequila} framework allows convenient use of the algorithms as a standalone method or as a subpart of more extensive procedures.

papers.title: Comments on the paper "Eliminating beam-induced depolarizing effects in the hydrogen jet target for high-precision proton beam polarimetry at the Electron-Ion Collider"
papers.summary: A critical review of the methodology used in F. Rathmann et al., Phys. Rev. Accel. Beams 29, 021001 (2026), to evaluate beam-induced depolarization of the Atomic Polarized Hydrogen Gas Jet (HJET) target at the Electron--Ion Collider (EIC) is presented. It is shown that several key assumptions underlying that analysis -- including the introduction of a photon emission threshold, the application of Fermi's Golden Rule to coherent hyperfine transitions, the interpretation of power broadening as a physical linewidth increase, and the treatment of spatial magnetic fields -- are either incorrect or internally inconsistent. As a consequence, the predicted large depolarization effects are demonstrated to be artifacts of the adopted methodology rather than genuine physical phenomena. A consistent quantum-mechanical treatment based on the time-dependent Schr\"odinger equation shows that beam-induced depolarization probabilities at the EIC are negligibly small.

papers.title: Two Photon excitation microscopy of individual Single-Walled Carbon Nanotubes
papers.summary: Two-photon fluorescence imaging achieves deep-tissue penetration through long excitation wavelengths and nonlinear excitation confinement. The 1700 nm transparency window is particularly attractive, as it optimally balances tissue scattering and absorption. However, efficient fluorophores for two-photon excitation in this window remain limited. Moreover the weak near-infrared emission of individual emitters, and the low photon detection efficiency, has so far precluded single-particle imaging. Here, we characterize the two-photon excitation properties of chirality-sorted pristine and quantum color center-functionalized single-walled carbon nanotubes under 1700 nm excitation. By measuring and comparing their two-photon action cross-sections, we identify quantum color center-functionalized (6,5) nanotubes emitting at 1140 nm, as the most promising emitter, with an exceptionally large cross-section of (57 \pm 2).103 GM. Leveraging these favorable photophysical properties, we image individual nanotubes under 1700 nm excitation, to our knowledge the first demonstration of single-particle imaging at this wavelength. These results establish quantum color center-functionalized (6,5) nanotube as a strong candidate for long-wavelength two-photon imaging and lay the groundwork for deep-tissue single-particle imaging.

papers.title: Computational Fluid Dynamics and Discrete Dipole Approximation Applied to Predict Airborne Viruses Disinfection by Ultraviolet Irradiation
papers.summary: Ultraviolet (UV) inactivation of airborne viruses involves coupled multiphysics and multiscale processes, yet UV scattering within virus-laden saliva droplets is commonly neglected. Here, for the first time we combine computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and the discrete dipole approximation (DDA) to investigate the influence of droplet-scale UV scattering on airborne virus inactivation. A benchmark CFD-DDA case study is developed and demonstrated that infected saliva droplets can exhibit highly non-uniform UV scattering under representative flow and irradiance conditions. This non-uniformity can substantially affect the predicted number of surviving viral copies, $N_s$ , indicating that UV scattering should be considered when modeling UV-based airborne disinfection systems. We systematically investigate the effect on $N_s$ by varying: the initially emitted saliva droplets diameter distribution, their number ($n(t = 0) = 10^3$ or $10^4$), volumetric airflow rate ($Q_v$ = 100, 150, or 200 $m^3/h$), droplet-wall interaction (stick vs escape), and coronavirus UV susceptibility constant (Z = 0.018 or 0.377 $m^2$/J). The simulations consider initially infected saliva droplets containing $7.4 \times 10^8$ RNA copies/mL, with a viral capsid diameter of $d_{cap}$ = 100 nm, at an air temperature of 21 {\deg}C and relative humidity of 65%. UV irradiation is represented by a 10 W cylindrical UV-lamp (34.3 mW/$cm^2$). The DDA results further enable development of an extended virus-inactivation model based on the classical Chick-Watson law that accounts for UV scattering in both spherical and nonspherical infected droplets. The results highlight the importance of resolving local UV-droplet interactions in airborne virus disinfection models and demonstrate the potential of the coupled CFD-DDA approach for improving the design and performance of UV-based airborne disinfection systems.

papers.title: Ultrashort pulsed laser atmospheric filament properties and microwave radiation inferred from S-band guided wave interaction and self-emission
papers.summary: The electrical conductivity $\sigma$ of the plasma filament left behind by an ultrashort pulsed laser (USPL) optical pulse after it is geometrically then self-focused in air via the Kerr effect is measured by attenuation of a 3.2 GHz TE$_{10}$ mode within an S-band waveguide through which the filament passes, taking into account the characteristic radius $R$ of the filament, as determined by fast camera visible light imaging. Models of the major air constituents' ionization rate $W_{i}$ vs. local laser intensity $I$, and of electron temperature $T$ and mean axial electron momentum $\left\langle p_{{z}}\right\rangle $ vs. peak laser intensity $I_{0}$ are then used to infer a hypothetical steady state filament's $I_{0}$, $T$, major species particle densities, and assumed axially invariant current time integral $Q$ and current decay rate $\nu$ after pulse passage. $Q$ is independently measured via the filament's self-emission signal in the waveguide for comparison. The theoretical far field microwave radiation pattern due to the actual axial variation in $Q=Q\left( z\right) $ is compared favorably to published measurements. A much lower upper bound on $\nu$ is inferred once such radiation is taken into account. Results are presented along a $30$~cm long filament at a broad range of atmospheric pressures.

papers.title: GraphCast Skill and Systematic Biases in Indian Summer Monsoon Forecasts: Evaluation Against ERA5 and IMERG
papers.summary: The Indian Summer Monsoon (ISM) is one of the most dynamically complex phenomena in the global climate system, yet its accurate prediction remains challenging for both physics-based and data-driven models. This study presents a systematic climatological evaluation of Google's GraphCast, a machine-learning global weather prediction system, against ERA-5 reanalysis and IMERG satellite precipitation for the boreal summer season (June-September, JJAS) over 2021-2024. We analyze deterministic GraphCast forecasts initialized at 00 UTC across 6-hourly steps to assess +24h, +48h, and +72h performance over the full ISM domain. The evaluation covers the climatological mean state (spatial rainfall, surface temperature, low-level winds), rainfall intensity distributions, thermodynamic drivers (tropospheric temperature gradient, DTT; apparent heat source and moisture sink, Q1 and Q2), monsoon dynamics (vertical wind shear, meridional structure), and variability across intraseasonal, synoptic, and spectral scales. GraphCast reproduces the spatial pattern and annual cycle of monsoon rainfall with high fidelity at short leads, showing a near-zero domain-averaged rainfall bias over the core monsoon zone (-0.7 to -1.2 mm/day) and high daily temporal correlation with IMERG (0.89-0.92). However, temporal variance is moderately suppressed across timescales (power-spectrum variance ratio ~0.63), and the intensity distribution systematically underrepresents extreme events and the 95th percentile. GraphCast closely captures the vertical structure and seasonal evolution of Q1 and Q2, but degrades in northward-propagating intraseasonal variability. Overall, GraphCast shows a moderate underrepresentation of rainfall intensity and variance rather than a wet bias or variance collapse, providing benchmark diagnostics for AI weather models.

papers.title: Generalization of Rayleigh's high-frequency theory for the 2D Helmholtz equation in a half-space subject to a radiation condition at infinity and a Dirichlet condition on a 1D periodically-uneven boundary
papers.summary: The 2D Helmholtz equation, radiation condition and Dirichlet boundary condition, are the translation, in mathematical terms, of (at least) three physical 2D problems for the prediction of the total scalar wavefield on one side of an impenetrable 1D periodically uneven boundary when: a) a plane TE electromagnetic wave propagating in the vacuum strikes the boundary the other side of which is occupied by a perfectly-conducting medium, b) a plane SH elastic elastic wave strikes a rigid boundary, c) a plane acoustic wave strikes a pressure-release boundary. The first attempt to solve such problems in a non-heuristic manner was made by Lord Rayleigh (in his book, 'The Theory of Sound' which appeared in 1896). My task will be to revisit Rayleigh's theory of diffraction by a sinusoidal-shaped, impenetrable boundary, and more specifically, his perturbation method for obtaining a mathematically-explicit solution to the diffraction problem in the high-frequency regime. In so doing, I shall correct and generalize Rayleigh's method to obtain solutions for arbitrary angles of incidence as well as for 1D periodic impenetrable boundaries of quite-general shape.

papers.title: Computational studies of giant edge islands and unpaired X-points in HSX and W7-X by manipulating coil currents
papers.summary: We present magnetic configurations in the Helically Symmetric eXperiment (HSX) and Wendelstein 7-X (W7-X), in which the edge magnetic structure exhibits island chains which are spatially larger than the previously reported configurations. These ``giant" island chains (with rotational transform $\iota=4/3$ or $4/4$ for HSX and $\iota=5/6$, $5/5$ or $5/4$ for W7-X) are obtained by reducing the coil current in main coil 6 for HSX and non-planar coil 5 for W7-X (i.e. the coil nearest the up-down symmetric cross-section $\phi=36^\circ$ for W7-X and $\phi=45^\circ$ for HSX). This appears a sufficient (but not necessary) condition for giant islands. The giant islands create X-point legs which transport plasma to the plasma-facing components (PFCs). In the most extreme cases, the island O-points leave the domain of the field line map and the divertor legs of the remaining ``unpaired" X-points do not close around the island. We show for W7-X, via the construction of quadratic flux-minimising surfaces, that these island size trends can mostly be interpreted as changes in magnitude of a resonant perturbation on a changing resonant ``unperturbed" magnetic surface. We use the anisotropic heat diffusion code EMC3-Lite to find ``giant island" W7-X configurations which are promising for PFC heat loads. These configurations significantly degrade the neoclassical transport performance but allow exploration of novel divertor regimes; for example, we show that the internal island pitch can be increased. This leads to favourable downstream/upstream plasma density ratios according to simple models; an attractive finding which motivates further investigation.

papers.title: Spin-Consistency Constraints in Noncollinear Tensor TDA
papers.summary: TDDFT for open-shell systems, whether spin-conserving or spin-flip, has long suffered from spin contamination. This problem arises because the single-excitation space built upon a single Kohn-Sham determinant is not spin-complete. Adopting spin tensor reference states therefore offers an elegant and promising route to resolving this issue. In this work, we revisit the tensor TDDFT equations within the Tamm-Dancoff approximation (TDA) from a noncollinear perspective. We show that, for S = 1/2 reference states, the internal consistency of the spin tensor formulation can, with the aid of the zero-excitation-energy theorem, be recast as a set of constraints that the exchange-correlation kernel must satisfy. Standard noncollinear functionals, however, generally fail to meet these constraints. To address this, we propose a kernel reconstruction scheme that is independent of the specific functional form and free of empirical parameters. This scheme enforces the required constraints, restoring internal consistency in the full spin tensor structure, with spin adaptation following as a natural consequence. Furthermore, when extended to tensor reference states with other values of S, such as S = 1 for the oxygen molecule, the scheme eliminates the so-called artifact states, namely solutions with severely underestimated excitation energies. In addition, the scheme allows the target states that ROKS reference states aim to describe to be expressed and computed, at the TDA level, within the same unified framework as other states, a capability that spin-adapted spin-conserving TDDFT has so far lacked.

papers.title: A Geometry-Adaptive Mesh Refinement Framework for Immersed Boundary Methods on Hybrid Unstructured Meshes
papers.summary: In this work, we describe a new preprocessing tool for geometry-adaptive mesh refinement on hybrid unstructured meshes with a target application on immersed boundary methods. The tool has as input an unstructured, hybrid, and conforming mesh generated by an external mesh generation software, and the main goal is to refine this mesh around immersed geometries in such a way that the CFD solver using the immersed boundary method can simulate flow problems in an accurate and efficient manner. The input background mesh can be made of different types of elements, like tetrahedra, hexahedra, prisms, and pyramids, which, unlike Cartesian meshes, permit for a more flexible mesh. Hybrid unstructured meshes enable one to use the immersed boundary technology in a new class of flow problems where the full geometry is decomposed into a fixed geometry part and a changing geometry part. A body-fitted mesh is generated for the fixed geometry while for the changing one is used the immersed boundary method. We simulate several flow problems to test the new meshes, including subsonic flow past a cylinder and subsonic flow past an NACA0012 airfoil, both using finite volume and discontinuous Galerkin methods and solving the Navier-Stokes equations. As an industrial example of our mesh generation, we consider the simulation of a multi-element airfoil: in this case, a mesh generation software generates an unstructured conforming background mesh for the slat and main airfoil, while the flap is placed as immersed geometry in this body-fitted mesh. As accurate and efficient results are sought, this mesh is refined around the flap and then the subsonic flow at high-lift flow conditions is simulated with a finite volume method coupled with an immersed boundary method and using the Reynolds-averaged Navier-Stokes equations.

papers.title: Sub-sonic compressible magnetohydrodynamic turbulence I. Alfv\'enic and fast-magnetosonic injection, amplitude dependence, and compressibility effects
papers.summary: We investigate how sub-sonic compressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence properties that are relevant for cosmic-ray (CR) transport in the Galaxy are affected by the nature and amplitude of initial fluctuations, and by the plasma compressibility $\beta$. We perform 3D simulations of decaying compressible ideal-MHD turbulence at $1024^3$ resolution with the PLUTO code. The level of density fluctuations in fully developed turbulence is insensitive to whether this state is reached starting from Alfv\'enic or fast-magnetosonic perturbations. Fast-magnetosonic injection is characterized by an early phase of rapid shock dissipation, followed by a turbulence-dominated decay with a rate comparable to that of the Alfv\'enic case. The contribution of fast-magnetosonic fluctuations in fully developed turbulence remains relevant only when the initial injection consists exclusively of fast modes. Large-amplitude turbulence ($\delta B/B_0>1$) is characterized by a nearly isotropic Kolmogorov or Iroshnikov-Kraichnan spectrum for Alfv\'enic or fast-magnetosonic injection, respectively. At low amplitudes ($\delta B/B_0\ll1$), both initial Alfv\'enic and mixed-wave perturbations lead to strongly anisotropic turbulence with spectra $\propto k_\perp^{-5/3}$ and $\propto k_z^{-2}$ (becoming steeper at $\beta\gg1$), whereas fast-magnetosonic perturbations produce a turbulent state populated by shocks with a nearly isotropic $k^{-2}$ spectrum. Magnetic-field curvature and mirror structures are strongly sensitive to fluctuation amplitude and plasma $\beta$. The predicted -2.5 power-law scaling emerges only in the large-amplitude regime at high $\beta$. This work highlights that features of sub-sonic compressible MHD turbulence that may affect CR transport are sensitive to large-scale conditions and to the plasma $\beta$. Their effect on CR diffusion and field-line random walk is the object of Paper II.

papers.title: The Equations of Reduced Magnetohydrodynamics in Dipole Coordinates
papers.summary: The equations of reduced magnetohydrodynamics (RMHD) isolate the Alfv\'enic energy transfer and turbulence dynamics from MHD in a computationally tractable way. In this study, we derive the equations of RMHD for a low $\beta$ plasma in a dipole coordinate system aligned with an inhomogeneous background that is general enough to represent the Earth's magnetosphere using a multiscale analysis and the Kreiss theorem. The most important effect beyond homogeneous RMHD is the propensity for background Alfv\'en speed gradients to drive nonlinear wave effects. This work has immediate application to the magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling problem in the Earth's magnetosphere, where the Alfv\'en speed varies by an order of magnitude over a short distance. We estimate the turbulent energy transfer driven by this. In Earth's magneotsphere, a substantial portion of energy ($>20\%$) could be transferred in this way along auroral field lines. A revised field aligned current density mapping technique to account for this energy loss mechanism is proposed to replace using $j_\parallel/B_0$ being constant along the field line. We also predict the existence of a ``saturation current density,'' where there is a maximum $j_\parallel$ that exist before driving a nonlinear cascade. At Earth, this value is $\sim 5\; \mu \text{A}/\text{m}^2$ at the ionosphere, which corresponds to the maximum observed value by ground magnetometers. Furthermore, this study makes use of a novel methodology, a computer algebra system, in performing algebraic work under complicated coordinate systems. We hope this approach serves as a template for performing reproducible and verifiable multiscale perturbation analysis under arbitrarily complex geometries.

papers.title: Explainable AI for Geoscientific Regression: Evaluating Sensitivity and Attribution Methods with the Lorenz-63 System and Applications
papers.summary: As artificial intelligence (AI) moves from research prototypes to operational tools in Earth system science, trust in its predictions becomes increasingly important. Explainable AI (XAI) offers insight into how AI models make predictions. However, many influential XAI methods were developed or popularised for classification, and their interpretation for regression, which dominates geoscience, is less well established. A central obstacle is the lack of ground truth for judging explanations. We show that, for a dynamical system with known governing equations, matched references can be built directly from the physics. We extend established sensitivity methods to provide physical references for both sensitivity and attribution, separately for methods with implicit and explicit baselines, all computed from the governing equations independently of the network. Applied to an AI emulator of the Lorenz-63 system, these references show that method families answer distinct questions rather than approximating one ``true'' explanation. The emulator's sensitivities and attributions can depart most from their physical references where it forecasts best, so predictive skill is not a substitute for the physical realism of what a model has learned. We then review XAI applications to Earth system regression, organised by method family, extending to issues an idealised system cannot address: computational scalability, strongly correlated high-dimensional predictors, and reliance on expert judgement where no physical reference exists. We also discuss how an XAI method can be mathematically valid yet only partially relevant to a given stakeholder group. We close with future directions and practical recommendations for responsible XAI use in geoscientific modelling and forecasting.

papers.title: Reconstructing the generalized Barrow holographic dark energy with physics-informed neural networks
papers.summary: Barrow holographic dark energy connects cosmic acceleration with possible quantum-gravitational deformations of horizon entropy, encoded in the Barrow exponent $\Delta$. If such effects are scale dependent, however, there is no fundamental reason for $\Delta$ to remain constant throughout cosmic history. In this work we reconstruct $\Delta(z)$ directly from observations, without assuming any particular functional form, using the Cosmo-PINN physics-informed neural-network framework. The generalized Barrow holographic evolution equation is incorporated into the training, while PantheonPlus supernovae, DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations and cosmic chronometers constrain the reconstruction. We find a mild and smooth redshift evolution, with the posterior mean favoring negative $\Delta$ and this tendency becoming stronger when the Cepheid calibration is included. Nevertheless, $\Delta=0$ and constant negative values remain compatible with current uncertainties. The reconstructed cosmology yields a viable late-time evolution, with $w_{\rm DE}$ close to $-1$ and the expected transition to accelerated expansion. Our results demonstrate that cosmological observations can directly probe the functional behavior of a quantity entering the underlying entropy law itself.

papers.title: Early warning signals for synchronization transitions from partial observations
papers.summary: Anticipating the onset of collective synchronization is important in many networked systems, yet observing every oscillator is often impractical. We investigate whether synchronization transitions can be detected from a small set of monitored, or sentinel, nodes. Using a stochastic Kuramoto model on networks, we numerically compare three early warning signals: the local order parameter, its temporal variance, and the variance of individual oscillator phases after removing their mean rotational trends. We also compare sentinel-selection strategies based on node dynamics, degree, and random sampling. We show that, under partial observation, the local order parameter and the variance of detrended phases provide substantially stronger warning signals than the variance of the local order parameter. Selecting nodes according to their dynamical behavior near the transition consistently improves performance over other sentinel-selection methods. With only $\lfloor\ln N\rfloor$ dynamically selected sentinels, two success indicators approach the performance obtained by observing all $N$ nodes. These results demonstrate that synchronization transitions can be anticipated from sparse observations when the warning signal and monitored nodes are chosen appropriately.

papers.title: Internal heating in rapidly rotating convection is not a shortcut to geostrophic turbulence
papers.summary: Convective turbulence in planets and stars is often driven by internal heating. This forcing mechanism has also been proposed as a means of accessing the diffusion-free scalings of the geostrophic turbulence (GT) regime at modest forcing. We test this with the asymptotically reduced quasi-geostrophic model, which is formally valid in the limit of vanishing Ekman number, $Ek \rightarrow 0$, and retains the Prandtl number as an independent parameter. We find no such shortcut: the Nusselt and Reynolds numbers are no closer to their diffusion-free predictions than in the boundary-heated case; the predicted $Pr^{-1/2}$ collapse fails over the range surveyed; and the prefactor depends on the form of the heating. Our no-slip/stress-free cases track the radiatively driven simulations of Hadjerci, Bouillaut, Miquel & Gallet (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 998, 2024, A9) case by case. Those simulations span only the narrow range of forcing over which the compensated Nusselt number is near its maximum within their geostrophic-turbulence criterion; across the wider range accessible to the reduced model it rises to that maximum and then falls by more than an order of magnitude while the flow remains rotationally constrained. We argue that bulk transport scalings are incomplete diagnostics of GT, whereas the saturation of the interior mean temperature gradient and of the vertical velocity kurtosis remain reliable indicators.

papers.title: Dynamic Alignment or Angular Persistence?
papers.summary: Dynamic alignment in magnetohydrodynamic turbulence is commonly inferred from the decrease of an amplitude-weighted average of the mutual angle between Els\"asser increments toward smaller separations. That decrease, however, need not imply that the increments themselves rotate toward alignment: large-angle fluctuations can simply lose more amplitude than small-angle ones. We therefore study the joint evolution of increment amplitude and mutual angle using finite-step conditional transition probabilities. In forced incompressible full MHD and in balanced strong-guide-field reduced MHD, we find that, at fixed initial angle, large-amplitude Els\"asser-increment pairs undergo smaller angular changes than small-amplitude pairs, including when they begin at large angles. We call this amplitude-dependent angular persistence. Normalized amplitude moments increase toward smaller separation, while stronger amplitude weighting produces progressively smaller angular averages and stronger scale dependence, linking apparent alignment to the intermittent large-amplitude tail. In RMHD, a source-state decomposition of the Politano-Pouquet third-order moment shows that initially large-angle, high-amplitude populations contribute with the sign associated with transfer toward smaller perpendicular scales despite their comparatively small angular changes. Time-resolved full-MHD data reproduce the same amplitude ordering, and the local Els\"asser advective term closely tracks the conditional dependence of both angular and amplitude changes on the initial state. These results show that the conventional dynamic-alignment diagnostic reflects the joint statistical evolution of amplitude and angle and, by itself, is not evidence for a cascade-wide dynamical rotation toward alignment.

papers.title: Odd-viscosity-induced instability in shear flows
papers.summary: Odd viscosity is a nondissipative component of the viscosity tensor that arises in fluids with broken time-reversal symmetry. We show that, despite being energy-conserving, odd viscosity can qualitatively alter hydrodynamic stability by generating exponentially growing modes that are absent in conventional fluids. For plane Poiseuille flow, we derive the odd-viscous generalization of the Orr--Sommerfeld--Squire equations and find a new instability that first emerges for streamwise-uniform modes and extends to oblique modes. The instability exploits the non-normality of the linearized Navier--Stokes operator: conventional fluids support transiently growing disturbances through the lift-up mechanism, while odd viscosity closes a feedback loop between wall-normal velocity and vorticity, converting these disturbances into self-sustaining exponentially growing modes. This mechanism lowers the linear instability threshold by nearly two orders of magnitude, from $\mathrm{Re}_c \approx 5772$ to $\mathrm{Re}_c \approx 62$. More generally, we show that an energy-conserving coupling can destabilize a linearly stable system by sustaining the growth of otherwise transiently growing disturbances. Such a coupling thus triggers energy growth without directly supplying energy, by enabling continuous energy extraction from the background state. This establishes a mechanism for controlling stability in non-normal systems without direct energy dissipation or injection.
