papers.title: Features of Charged Lepton Flavor Violation in an $A_4$ Symmetric Neutrino Mass Model
papers.summary: Neutrino flavour oscillations imply that there must be charged lepton flavour violation (CLFV) also. Different neutrino mass models predict different patterns of CLFV decays. Neutrino mass generation through standard see-saw mechanisms leads to the prediction that the branching ratios of meson CLFV decays will always be smaller than the corresponding radiative CLFV decays. In this work, we analyse an interesting neutrino mass model, based on $A_4$ symmetry, in which the symmetry and the symmetry-breaking pattern lead the neutrino mixing matrix to be of tri-bimaximal (TBM) form. In this model, we find that the meson CLFV decay amplitudes are not correlated to the corresponding radiative CLFV amplitudes, unlike in the case of see-saw models. The branching ratios of radiative CLFV decays are predicted to be negligibly small in this model, but those of the meson CLFV decays can be large enough to be observable in the near future.

papers.title: BCS superconductivity in the presence of wave dark matter
papers.summary: As particle physics and condensed matter physics continue to expand their boundaries, emerging intersections between the two fields suggest well-motivated frontiers for physics models. In particular, dark matter, which is cosmologically predicted to form the background to our ordinary matter, can affect the physics of materials in a fundamental sense. In this work, we investigate the scenario in which relic ultralight wave dark matter alters the superconductor Hamiltonian via a sinusoidal source term. The Yukawa interaction with the scalar dark matter changes the effective electron mass, inducing periodic perturbations of macroscopic observables such as the superconducting order parameter, whose size could be important in future experiments. We provide here the actual calculations for this scenario on the superconducting resonators, calculating the modulation size depending on the dark matter parameters.

papers.title: Thermal Leptogenesis in $SO(10)\times U(1)_A$ SUSY GUT
papers.summary: We investigate thermal leptogenesis within a supersymmetric grand unified theory (SUSY GUT) based on the $SO(10) \times U(1)_A$ symmetry, where both the doublet--triplet splitting problem and the unrealistic Yukawa relations are resolved under the natural assumption that all symmetry-allowed interactions appear with $\mathcal{O}(1)$ coefficients. In this framework, the structures of the Dirac neutrino Yukawa couplings and right-handed neutrino masses are determined entirely by the symmetry. The baryon asymmetry of the Universe is computed taking into account the flavor effects, Higgs asymmetry contributions, and the impact of the second-lightest right-handed neutrino. While the predicted asymmetry is too small when all $\mathcal{O}(1)$ coefficients of the Dirac neutrino Yukawa couplings are set to unity, a moderate enhancement factor $r_1 \sim 5.4$ for the lightest right-handed neutrino mass reproduces the observed baryon asymmetry without spoiling low-energy neutrino data. This corresponds to a suppressed lightest neutrino mass, $m_{\nu_1} \sim (1/r_1) \times (\text{symmetry-determined value})$, typically $m_{\nu_1} \sim 4.5 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{eV}$. We further explore cases where the $\mathcal{O}(1)$ coefficients of the Dirac neutrino Yukawa couplings are $\pm 1$, and find that roughly half of them successfully generate the observed baryon asymmetry for $r_1\leq 11$. Moreover, the others yield results of the correct order of magnitude, although they do not generate the observed Baryon asymmetry. These findings demonstrate that thermal leptogenesis is realized in this $SO(10)\times U(1)_A$ SUSY GUT, establishing a link between the observed baryon asymmetry and predictions for the lightest neutrino mass.

papers.title: Jet quenching and its substructure dependence due to color decoherence
papers.summary: Motivated by color coherence and decoherence effects in the QCD medium, we propose a theoretical framework that combines vacuum-like emissions and medium-induced radiation to study jet quenching and its dependence on jet cone sizes and substructure. In our approach, a jet produced at a hard scale $Q$ first undergoes vacuum-like evolution, as described by the well-established generating-function method in the double logarithmic approximation. These vacuum-like emissions generate subjets at an infrared momentum scale $Q_0$. Each subjet then experiences medium-induced energy loss as described by the BDMPS-Z formalism. By modeling the QCD bulk medium using OSU (2+1)-dimensional viscous hydrodynamics and treating $Q_0$ together with the jet-quenching parameters at the initial proper time of the hydrodynamic evolution as free parameters, our approach provides a very good description of the inclusive jet modification factor $R_{AA}$ for large-radius jets and its dependence on jet substructure in 0-10% PbPb collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}} = 5.02~\rm{TeV}$, as measured by the ATLAS experiment.

papers.title: Probing Cosmic-Ray-Boosted and Supernova-Sourced Sub-GeV Dark Matter with Paleo-Detectors
papers.summary: Astrophysical dark matter particles with masses well below GeV-scale can be difficult to detect using conventional nuclear recoil experiments due to their low velocities in our Milky Way halo. Elastic scattering with high-energy cosmic rays or thermal production inside core-collapse supernovae can accelerate sub-GeV DM to (semi-)relativistic velocities, producing nuclear recoil energies above the keV threshold that paleo-detectors can record over geological timescales. Using olivine as the target with 100$\,$g$\cdot$Gyr exposure, we compute track length distributions from such (semi-)relativistic dark matter fluxes, incorporating all major backgrounds (neutrinos, uranium-chain neutrons, thorium recoils) with a statistical analysis on an Asimov dataset. We derive 95 C.L. projected sensitivity of paleo-detectors to the DM-nucleon cross section for dark matter masses between a few MeV and hundreds of MeV. Our results show that paleo-detectors are able to probe large parameter regions that are not covered by current and near-future experiments designed to detect dark matter and neutrinos. In particular, paleo-detectors offer a unique ability to record the dark matter flux from Galactic supernova events over geological times. Such cumulative exposure enables sensitivity gains of a few orders of magnitude compared to conventional experiments.

papers.title: Detectability of Magnetar-Induced Vacuum Birefringence with IXPE and eXTP
papers.summary: We analyze the prospects of quantitatively detecting vacuum birefringence from magnetars using the IXPE and eXTP experiments. We adopt a realistic spatially-varying magnetic field profile for magnetars and use the one-loop refractive indices, without expanding in $B/B_{\rm c}$, to calculate the differential time delay and accumulated phase between the two photon polarization eigenmodes. Including the extended magnetosphere enhances the time delay by a factor of 1.2--1.7 relative to a constant-field estimate and can yield delays approaching the microsecond scale for the strongest catalogued magnetar fields. We also study the evolution of the polarization state in a varying projected magnetic field using the Stokes-vector precession equation, derive the corresponding adiabaticity condition and polarization-limiting radius, and recover the fixed-eigenaxis expressions used in our catalog analysis as a controlled limit. We calculate the Stokes parameters for all known magnetars and investigate their observability with IXPE and eXTP, including the effects of instrumental response and energy averaging. We find that both experiments can be sensitive to magnetar vacuum birefringence under favorable conditions, with 1RXS J170849.0$-$400910 being the most promising candidates. A quantitative prediction for an individual magnetar, however, additionally requires a source-specific treatment of the emission mechanism, viewing geometry, plasma environment, and magnetospheric scattering, which we do not tackle in this study.

papers.title: EEXICC: An event generator for doubly heavy baryon production at $e^+e^-$ colliders
papers.summary: We present EEXICC, a Monte Carlo event generator designed to simulate the production of doubly heavy baryons ($\Xi_{cc}$, $\Xi_{bc}$, and $\Xi_{bb}$) via $e^+e^-$ annihilation. Based on nonrelativistic QCD effective theory, the generator calculates the process $e^{+}+e^{-}\rightarrow \Xi_{QQ'}+\bar{Q}'+\bar{Q}$ using an improved trace technique at the amplitude level, which greatly improves numerical efficiency compared with traditional squared-amplitude methods. EEXICC uses a modular Fortran implementation for hard-process generation and a C++ interface to the bundled PYTHIA 8.317 library, enabling convenient integration into complete event simulation workflows. The program supports both weighted and unweighted event generation, and its numerical reliability has been verified against existing theoretical results. EEXICC provides a flexible and robust tool for studying the properties of doubly heavy baryons at future high-luminosity and high-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders such as the CEPC and FCC-ee.

papers.title: Solar axions from nuclear transitions

papers.title: Muon-induced di-tau production as a probe of new physics
papers.summary: The muon trident process, which involves coherent scattering to produce tau pairs, is a powerful tool for constraining dark sectors. We propose to explore this channel using future high-energy muon beams with the dedicated active-target detector, High-Energy Muon Electronic Research Apparatus (HEMERA). The detector would complement muon beam-dump searches by resolving prompt signatures and could operate from preparatory facilities involving an individual muon beam of the full Muon Collider. We illustrate its capabilities for a leptophilic scalar with Yukawa-like couplings that can mediate thermal dark matter production. With $10^{18}$ incident TeV-scale muons, even a compact 10 kg silicon-based HEMERA will extend current $B$-factory and $(g-2)_\mu$ bounds by over an order of magnitude in coupling strength. In the leptophilic thermal dark matter paradigm, this search offers a way to probe dark sector targets beyond the neutrino floor of dark matter direct detection. This provides an additional compelling motivation for the development of high-energy muon beam infrastructure.

papers.title: Chiral-odd structure of the $N \to \Delta$ transition: transverse multipoles from QCD light-cone sum rules
papers.summary: The matrix element of the tensor current between the nucleon and the $\Delta(1232)$ is described by six form factors, which organize into transverse multipoles of rank zero to three. The rank-three term, an octupole, has no counterpart in the diagonal tensor matrix elements of the nucleon or in the electromagnetic $N \to \Delta$ transition. We study the isovector chiral-odd transition within QCD light-cone sum rules, constructing the sum rules from light-cone projections of the correlation function rather than from individual Lorentz structures and removing the contributions of spin-$1/2$ states of both parities explicitly. At leading and next-to-leading power in the light-cone expansion the spin-$1/2$-free sum rules form an overdetermined system that determines four combinations of the form factors, among them the transverse dipole, quadrupole and octupole; the monopole and the longitudinal form factor $F_1$ are not accessible at this level. Conventional sum rules built on single Lorentz structures that measure the same combination of form factors differ by up to a factor of two while being equally stable in the Borel parameter, and we show that these structures receive no contribution of leading or next-to-leading power. With the $\Delta$ coupling and the continuum threshold taken from the $\Delta$ two-point sum rule and two sets of nucleon distribution amplitudes, we obtain the quadrupole for $1 \leq Q^2 \leq 6$~GeV$^2$ and the octupole for $Q^2 \gtrsim 2$~GeV$^2$, with Borel and threshold variations of at most about ten percent, and the dipole, whose magnitude depends strongly on the distribution amplitudes. The model of the distribution amplitudes is the dominant source of uncertainty, and the results do not determine an extrapolation to $Q^2 = 0$.

papers.title: Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Ray Boosted Relic Neutrinos
papers.summary:
Ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs) can boost relic neutrinos to high energies through Standard Model (SM) neutral-current interactions, providing an indirect probe of the cosmic neutrino background (C$
u$B). In this work, we perform a systematic study of the diffuse UHECR-boosted C$
u$B flux including elastic neutrino--nucleon scattering (ES), coherent elastic neutrino--nucleus scattering (COH), incoherent neutrino--nucleus scattering (INCOH), baryon-resonance production (RES), and deep inelastic scattering (DIS). For the UHECR flux, we use mixed-composition spectra obtained from the UHECR propagation code PriNCe and from the H3a and H4a implementations of the Hillas model, together with SFR, QSO, and GRB source evolution models. We find a clear hierarchy of scattering channels as a function of boosted neutrino energy. The coherent scattering dominates at low-energy neutrino flux for heavy nuclear components, while ES and INCOH become important once individual nucleons are resolved. The RES channel gives a non-negligible contribution in the high-energy region, and DIS appears only at the highest energies and is most visible for the H4a case. Using current IceCube and Pierre Auger Observatory data, we obtain upper limits on the C$
u$B overdensity. Our results show that reliable predictions of the UHECR-boosted C$
u$B signal require a combined treatment of the relevant SM scattering channels, UHECR composition, source evolution, and the neutrino mass spectrum.

papers.title: Decay constants of the two-pole $D_0^*(2300)$
papers.summary: The nature of the scalar charmed meson $D_0^*(2300)$ remains one of the most intriguing questions in hadron spectroscopy. A prominent interpretation is a two-pole structure generated by the coupled channels $D\pi$, $D\eta$, $D_s\bar K$, and $D\eta'$, in which the lower pole couples mainly to $D\pi$ and the higher pole to $D_s\bar K$. Following this picture, we calculate the decay constants of these two poles using the effective Lagrangian approach. The resulting values, $f_{D_0^*}^{(\mathrm{lower})}=68.46^{+0.93}_{-1.25}\,\mathrm{MeV}$ and $f_{D_0^*}^{(\mathrm{higher})}=90.51^{+5.91}_{-11.64}\,\mathrm{MeV}$, are substantially smaller than those predicted by conventional $c\bar q$ excited-state scenarios. This difference suggests that decay constants can serve as a sensitive probe to discriminate between different internal structures of the $D_0^*(2300)$. As a phenomenological application, we further predict the branching fractions for the Cabibbo-favored decays $B_s \to D_s D_0^*$, $\Lambda_b \to \Lambda_c D_0^*$, and $\Xi_b \to \Xi_c D_0^*$ within the factorization approach. These predictions provide crucial tests to validate the two-pole interpretation of the $D_0^*(2300)$.

papers.title: Lepton-Number Violation in Higgs Effective Field Theory: Complete Operator Basis and Type-II Seesaw Matching
papers.summary: We construct a complete and nonredundant basis of lepton-number-violating (LNV) operators in the Higgs effective field theory (HEFT) through $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$, including their full flavor multiplicities. Using a complex dressed spurion that encodes the $B-L$ charge, we classify the $\Delta L=2$ and $\Delta L=4$ sectors, including baryon-number-violating operators, and independently validate the counting using Hilbert-series methods. As a concrete application, we present the first complete tree-level matching of the type-II seesaw model onto HEFT through $\mathcal{O}(p^4)$, covering the bosonic, lepton-number-conserving, and LNV sectors. Using the nonlinear field representation and primary-HEFT power counting, we retain the full dependence of the matching coefficients on the independent scalar masses, the neutral-scalar mixing, and the doublet and triplet vacuum expectation values. We compare our results with the corresponding real-triplet matching and a broken-phase effective field theory. We further discuss implications for LNV processes, Higgs physics, and electroweak observables.

papers.title: Physics of the QCD Trace Anomaly and Renormalization in a Reducible Basis
papers.summary: The QCD trace anomaly is a well-established textbook result in quantum field theory with several prominent features: (1) it arises from the quantum breaking of scale symmetry at ultraviolet (UV) scales, yet its full renormalized expression is independent of the particular UV regulator used, whether lattice or dimensional regularization; (2) although nominally of order $\alpha_s$, it is free of renormalization-scheme ambiguity; and (3) it is free of UV divergences and therefore scale independent. We show that renormalization in a reducible operator basis introduces additional convention dependence in its separation into quark and gluon parts, which do not share the properties of the whole anomaly itself. An irreducible decomposition instead keeps the trace anomaly as a single, convention-free component, and gives transparent physical meanings to anomaly-related nucleon physics, including the nucleon mass structure and internal forces.

papers.title: Fully charmed tetraquarks on the Lattice with controlled errors
papers.summary: We introduce the lattice quark potential model (LQPM), which discretizes the nonrelativistic quark potential model on a periodic cubic lattice and diagonalizes the resulting many-body Hamiltonian exactly. Unlike variational approaches, which provide only upper bounds on the energy, LQPM removes this variational bias, and its remaining finite-volume uncertainty is removed by extrapolation. Formulated directly in coordinate space, the method is indifferent to the specific form of the potential and accommodates arbitrary interactions, such as including three-body forces and spin-orbit and tensor couplings, that are difficult to treat in conventional few-body approaches. As a benchmark, the charmonium and $\Omega_{ccc}$ spectra are reproduced within a few MeV of experiment. For the fully charmed tetraquark $cc\bar{c}\bar{c}$, we obtain three resonances $J^P = 0^+, 1^+,$ and $2^+$ ground states above the $\eta_c \eta_c$, $\eta_c J/\psi$, $J/\psi J/\psi$ thresholds, respectively. Our results establish exact lattice diagonalization as a controlled, systematically improvable, and broadly applicable route to multiquark spectroscopy, providing a quantitative benchmark for the strong interaction and valuable guidance for future experimental searches for exotic hadrons.

papers.summary: The Roy equations for the $S$ and $P$ waves are solved for pion masses below the physical value in the region between threshold and $s_A=0.84\GeV^2$. The analysis is based on the assumption that the phenomenological input above $s_A$ can be used essentially unchanged. Moreover, for $M_\pi \le M_{\pi,\mathrm{phys}}$, the chiral perturbation theory predictions for the two $S$-wave scattering lengths provide a very reliable additional input to the Roy equations. The outcome is an accurate description of the $S$ and $P$ partial waves as the light-quark masses decrease towards the chiral limit. As a test of the approach, we evaluate the first few threshold parameters of the $S$, $P$, and $D$ waves via Wanders' sum rules and find excellent agreement with chiral perturbation theory across the entire range $0 \le M_\pi \le M_{\pi,\mathrm{phys}}$. We further solve the Roy equations for pion masses above the physical value (up to $240\MeV$) and show that the resulting solutions agree well with existing lattice data at $M_\pi=239\MeV$. The present work paves the way for analyses of lattice data that fully incorporate the constraints of analyticity, unitarity, and crossing symmetry, and provides the basis for an accurate study of the dependence of the $\sigma$ and $\rho$ resonances on the light-quark masses, both of which will be addressed in future work.

papers.title: Measuring $V_{cb}$ at electron-proton colliders
papers.summary: We study the prospects for an independent determination of $V_{cb}$ from bottom-tagged charged-current deep-inelastic scattering at future electron-proton colliders: the EIC, LHeC, and FCC-eh. The transition $e^- c \to \nu_e b$ probes $|V_{cb}|^2$ through a process with different theoretical and experimental uncertainties from semileptonic $B$ decays. We fit ratios of $b$-tagged charged-current event counts over flavour-inclusive ones in kinematic bins, including correlated parton-distribution and flavour-tag calibration uncertainties, and floating the other CKM parameters. With projected parton distributions and tagging performance motivated by existing studies, we find a potential relative sensitivity in $|V_{cb}|$ of about $0.8\%$ at the LHeC with $1\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$ of integrated luminosity and $0.7\%$ at FCC-eh with $2\,\rm{ab}^{-1}$. The corresponding EIC sensitivity is instead at the level of $20 - 30 \%$, depending on the configuration. The LHeC could thus provide a high-energy determination competitive with low-energy ones, but with substantially different dominant systematic uncertainties, on the timescale of its proposed operation between the HL-LHC and FCC-ee. We identify precise flavour-tag calibration and control of the kinematic response as the main requirements for realising this potential sensitivity.

papers.title: Two-variable longitudinal distribution of the $\Lambda_b$ in a three-quark light-front model
papers.summary: We determine a normalized two-variable longitudinal distribution of the $\Lambda_b=(ud)b$ baryon from a covariant three-quark light-front wave function. The scalar $ud$ channel is selected with the good-component structure $C\gamma_5\gamma^+$ and the two independent transverse momenta are integrated without introducing an elementary diquark. The resulting model-scale valence distribution $\Psi_2^{\rm LF}(x_u,x_d)$ retains both the heavy-light and internal-light momentum scales of the parent wave function. It is symmetric under $x_u\leftrightarrow x_d$, is concentrated where both light-quark fractions are small and separates the total light-pair momentum from its internal sharing. For the central parameter set we find $\langle x_u\rangle=\langle x_d\rangle=0.130$, $\langle x_b\rangle=0.739$, $\langle\zeta^2\rangle=0.153$, and $\langle\zeta^4\rangle=0.055$, where $\zeta=(x_u-x_d)/(x_u+x_d)$. Parameter variations give $\langle x_u\rangle=0.130^{+0.007}_{-0.007}$, $\langle x_b\rangle=0.739^{+0.014}_{-0.014}$, $\langle\zeta^2\rangle=0.153^{+0.014}_{-0.016}$, and $\langle\zeta^4\rangle=0.055^{+0.009}_{-0.009}$. The heavy-light momentum partition is controlled mainly by $\beta_{b,ud}$ and $m_b$, whereas the internal $u$--$d$ sharing is most sensitive to $\beta_{ud}$. The result provides a compact finite-mass benchmark for three-quark longitudinal structure, with distinct observables for heavy-light momentum sharing and correlations inside the light pair.

papers.title: Causal-horizon scaling of prompt X(3872) formation lengths
papers.summary: A causal-horizon ensemble relates changes in prompt production to spatial correlations involved in forming $\X$. Each horizon represents the spatial coherence range of an early-field pulse. For weak phase fluctuations and overlap widths small compared with the mean horizon, ensemble averaging makes the fractional loss of formation probability proportional to the Gaussian source-state overlap width. Extending this dependence as an effective law at finite attenuation, we compare three states to eliminate the common field coefficient. A common-slope fit to matched LHCb prompt $\X/\Ps$ and $\Ps/\Jp$ ratios at 13 TeV gives conditional formation scales. With a common Gaussian source, common field coupling, fixed relative production baselines and a direct-$\Jp$ reference, the central fit requires a source root-mean-square width above about 0.60 fm and an $\X$ effective Gaussian RMS separation of at least about 1.25 fm. The same assumptions require at least a factor of about 4.5 increase in the $\X$ formation probability relative to its no-field value between 4--6 and 12--14 GeV/$c$ in $2<y<3$. Calculations with finite feed-down and a nodal reference assess the length calibration. A matched three-state activity measurement tests the same spatial slope without an additional activity-dependent parameter.

papers.title: Gravitational Dark Matter Production in Einstein-Cartan Theory
papers.summary: Introducing torsion into General Relativity leads to new four-point interactions for fermions. These are universal and must also affect any fermion dark matter. We improve existing calculations of dark matter production through the Einstein-Cartan theory four-fermion interaction by also considering the s-channel graviton exchange as another contributing process. The effect on both the total cross section as well as the momentum-dependent Boltzmann equation collision term is calculated and discussed. We also introduce the Holst term, which generally modifies the four-fermion interaction coupling constant as well as introduces two new four-fermion interactions, and discuss and compute its effect on the total produced dark matter abundance.

papers.title: Holographic Approaches to Hadron Structure
papers.summary: We give an introduction to and an overview of holographic approaches to QCD and hadron structure. After an introduction to the string-theoretic foundations of holographic QCD, we review the predictions of top-down and bottom-up models for the phenomenology of mesons, baryons, and glueballs. We focus on the top-down model following from probe flavor branes in the Witten model of low-energy Yang-Mills theory and, in the more phenomenological approach of bottom-up models, mostly on minimal models based on five-dimensional anti-de Sitter space, which also implement global symmetries and their anomalies consistently, but allow the high-energy behavior to better match real QCD.

papers.title: Proton GTMDs and Wigner Distributions in the Chiral Quark Soliton Model: Orbital Angular Momentum and Spin-Orbit Correlation with Sea Quarks
papers.summary: We calculate the leading-twist vector and axial-vector quark generalized transverse-momentum-dependent distributions (GTMDs) of the proton in the chiral quark soliton model, including both the discrete valence level and the regularized Dirac sea. We consider the isosinglet and isotriplet combinations of GTMDs at zero and nonzero skewness. At zero skewness, we construct Wigner distributions and resolve the orbital angular momentum (OAM) and spin-orbit correlation (SOC) densities in transverse position and momentum space, separately for quarks and antiquarks. This provides a phase-space picture of the sea-quark and sea-antiquark contributions, displaying OAM aligned with the proton spin and anti-aligned with the partons' own spin.

papers.title: Updated $\Sigma_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures
papers.summary: In order to study the new $\Sigma_{c}$ baryons observed by the LHCb collaboration recently, we update the previously predicted $\Sigma_{c}$ excitation spectrum by extending the excited states up to the highly excited $2P$- and $1F$-wave states. The calculation is performed in the framework of the relativized quark model and Gaussian expansion method by considering the mixing effect. The radially and orbitally excited states in the calculation are determined by the truncation convention proposed in this work and the mechanism of the heavy-quark dominance. The contribution of each Hamiltonian term to the energy levels is precisely calculated by using the two-step Gaussian expansion method. Then, the concerned $\Sigma_{c}$ states are obtained and the $\Sigma_{c}$ excitation spectrum including the $2P$- and $1F$-wave fine structures is established. Based on these, several important topics are discussed and analyzed, including the root-mean-square radii, off-diagonal matrix elements, mixing effect, fine structures and assignments of the newly observed $\Sigma_{c}(2800)^{0}$, $\Sigma_{c}(2900)^{0}$ and $\Sigma_{c}(3200)^{0}$ states. Meanwhile, it is found that the approximate decoupling phenomenon emerges in different $nL$-wave groups. This implies the reasonability of the truncation convention and is of great significance for further improving the calculation scheme for all the baryon spectra. Moreover, it is demonstrated that in the very high-lying $nL$-wave groups such as the $1F$-wave group, the energy level gaps become small even degenerate, and each of the baryon states has a big radius and therefore a loosely bound structure. In addition, by examining the experimental and calculated data, we suggest more precise experiments to search for more $\Sigma_{c}$ baryon states in the predicted $1P$- and $2P$-wave fine structures whose central energies are around 2822 and 3210 MeV, respectively.

papers.title: Covariance and the use of the Schrodinger equation in quantum field theory
papers.summary: The Schrodinger equation is not covariant. Nevertheless, quantum field theory is often formulated using the Schrodinger equation to describe the time evolution of the system, which is equivalent to using Feynman path integrals. It is well known that scattering theory gives covariant results provided that the interaction vanishes in the asymptotic limit of $t \rightarrow \pm \infty$, but there are other situations of interest that do not satisfy those conditions. As an example, the Aharonov-Bohm effect is derived here using second-quantized field theory to describe all the electrons as well as the electromagnetic field, which allows the effects of retarded vector potentials to be calculated in a straightforward way using the Feynman propagator. The results are in agreement with the usual expression for the Aharonov-Bohm effect when the retardation of the electromagnetic field is negligible, but they predict a fractional phase shift, a lack of covariance, and violations of causality when retardation effects are significant. These results suggest that quantum field theory based on the Schrodinger equation or Feynman path integrals is incomplete in the sense that it cannot give a correct description of all observable phenomena.

papers.title: Constraining high-energy neutrinos from tidal disruption events with IceCube high-energy starting events
papers.summary: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) have been proposed as candidate sources of high-energy neutrinos. Successful and choked jets, as well as the accretion disk, corona, wind, and outflow regions in a TDE have been examined and shown to produce TeV - PeV neutrinos. In this work, we use the IceCube 12.5 year high energy starting events (HESE) dataset and perform a maximum likelihood analysis to investigate the spatial and temporal correlations between HESE dataset and a selected sample of 89 TDEs. Our results indicate that the currently observed data do not show any significant correlation and hence is consistent with the background only hypothesis. Using this result, we place constraints on the fraction of TDEs harboring intrinsic jets ($f_{\rm jet}$) and the corresponding isotropic-equivalent cosmic ray (CR) energy ($\mathcal{E}_{\rm CR}$). We note that even with limited statistics, we can constrain the parameter space as $\mathcal{E}_{\rm CR} \lesssim 3 \times 10^{53}$ erg for $f_{\rm jet} \gtrsim 0.6$ at more than 90% C.L. Finally, we discuss the theoretical implications of our results and the limits on the all-sky diffuse neutrino flux from TDEs. With more observational data in the electromagnetic band for TDEs and neutrino observations from IceCube and KM3NeT, our analysis can be used to place stringent constraints on physical parameters associated with TDEs.

papers.title: New axion bounds derived from the 100-parsec Gaia DR3 white dwarf luminosity function
papers.summary: The axion, a well-motivated hypothetical particle arising in extensions of the Standard Model, can be produced copiously within the hot, compact cores of white dwarf stars. The shape of the white dwarf luminosity function (WDLF) is a powerful tool for constraining theoretical particles that would imply an additional cooling channel in white dwarfs. In this work, and for the first time, we use the 100-parsec Gaia DR3 white dwarf sample and compare it with theoretical predictions. We have simulated synthetic populations of white dwarfs using a population synthesis code based on Monte Carlo techniques, incorporating realistic observational errors, and based on state-of-the-art white dwarf models that incorporate the anomalous cooling caused by the presence of axions. Axion bremsstrahlung emission rates were implemented using the latest theoretical calculations. We find that, for the brightest white dwarfs in the sample ($M_{\mathrm{Bol}} < 10$), the $\chi^2$ statistic is largely insensitive to the assumed stellar formation rate (SFR), which is typically the dominant uncertainty in modeling the Galactic-disk WDLF. The resulting $\chi^2$ analysis disfavors a sizable additional cooling contribution. This conclusion contrasts with earlier studies in which axion-electron couplings in the range $0.7 \times 10^{-13} < g_{ae} < 2.1 \times 10^{-13}$ provided mildly improved fits to the Galactic-disk WDLF. We attribute the discrepancy to simplifying assumptions in previous modeling and to the substantially improved observational quality of the 100-pc Gaia DR3 sample. We obtain the upper limit $g_{ae} < 1.68 \times 10^{-13}$ ($95\%$ C.L.), which is among the strongest available.

papers.title: Assessing the robustness of amortized simulation-based inference to transient noise in gravitational-wave ringdowns
papers.summary: Gravitational waves (GW) emitted by binary systems allow us to perform precision tests of general relativity in the strong field regime. Ringdown signals allow for probing black hole mass and spin with high precision in GW astronomy. With improvements in current and next-generation GW detectors, developing likelihood-free parameter inference methods is crucial. This is especially important when facing challenges such as non-standard noise, partial data, or incomplete signal models that prevent the use of analytical likelihood functions. In this work, we propose an amortized simulation-based inference strategy to estimate ringdown parameters directly. Specifically, our method is based on amortized neural posterior estimation, which trains a neural density estimator of the posterior for all data segments within the prior range. The results show that our trained amortized network achieves valid confidence coverage and yields posteriors in agreement with established Markov-chain methods at moderate signal-to-noise ratios. At higher signal-to-noise ratios, the recovered posteriors agree with the Markov-chain results in location, although the amplitude posterior is broader. The network provides inference speeds that are orders of magnitude faster. Furthermore, we evaluate the robustness of the method against transient noise contamination. Our results indicate that the timing of glitch injection significantly affects estimation bias, in particular when the glitch contaminates the early, high-amplitude portion of the signal. This study not only provides an efficient and statistically validated inference framework under the tested conditions for ringdown analysis but also lays a foundation for developing robust data-processing pipelines for future GW astronomy in realistic noise environments.

papers.title: Neutrino and electromagnetic signatures from Superluminous Supernovae: a case study for SN 2017egm
papers.summary: Superluminous supernovae (SLSNe) are rare transients that are $\sim 10 - 100$ times more luminous than ordinary stellar explosions, reaching peak optical luminosities $\sim 10^{44} - 10^{45}$ erg s$^{-1}$. The energy source powering SLSNe remains uncertain. In this work, we explore the multi-wavelength and multi-messenger signatures of the scenario in which SLSNe are powered by a newly born millisecond magnetar. We model the dynamical evolution and emission from the coupled system comprised of the magnetar, wind, nebula, and supernova ejecta, consistently evaluating the pair multiplicity of the wind and nebula regions, and the bulk wind Lorentz factor governing the $e^+ - e^-$ injection spectra in the nebula. We compute the thermal and non-thermal electromagnetic signatures, neutrino signatures, and investigate their detection prospects. For SN 2017egm, the nearest observed SLSNe, our prediction for high-energy gamma rays matches the recent detection by Fermi LAT. For neutrinos, using SN 2017egm a canonical SLSNe, we find that in the era of the Vera C. Rubin Observatory, a stacking analysis with upcoming neutrino observatories can lead to $3\sigma$ detection significance of neutrino events from a population of SLSNe within a decade of operation.

papers.title: Quark Number Susceptibilities and Conserved Charge Fluctuations in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD with M\"obius domain-wall fermions (MDWF)
papers.summary: We calculate second- and selected fourth-order conserved-charge fluctuations in $(2+1)$-flavor QCD using M\"obius domain-wall fermions (MDWF) along a line of constant physics. Gauge ensembles were generated for two light-to-strange quark-mass ratios, $m_l/m_s=1/10$ and $1/27.4$, corresponding to heavier-than-physical and physical pion masses, respectively. For $m_l/m_s=1/10$, calculations were carried out on lattices with temporal extents $N_\tau=12$ and $16$, enabling an assessment of lattice-spacing effects at heavier pion mass. For $m_l/m_s=1/27.4$, calculations were performed at $N_\tau=12$, allowing us to study the light-quark-mass dependence down to the physical point. Below the pseudocritical temperature, second-order electric-charge, strangeness, and off-diagonal conserved-charge fluctuations are consistent with QMHRG2020 hadron resonance gas calculations. Across the crossover region, these observables rise rapidly and tend toward their Stefan--Boltzmann limits. Selected fourth-order cumulants were also computed at the physical pion mass. Although these observables are statistically more demanding, several channels with controlled uncertainties permit a first comparison with hadron resonance gas calculations.

papers.title: High resolution Lyman-{\alpha} forest constraints on dark matter-neutrino scattering
papers.summary: We present new constraints on models of dark matter interacting with neutrino, based on high-resolution Lyman-$\alpha$ forest data. We perform a suite of full hydrodynamical simulations of these models, spanning a range of interaction strengths and thermal histories. We train an emulator on the simulation results. A Monte Carlo Markov Chain analysis yields an upper limit on the interaction strength of $u_{\nu\chi} \leq1.5\times10^{-8}$ (95% C.L.), which is the strongest direct bound to date on such interactions. Our results exclude previous hints of non-zero interactions presented in the literature. We furthermore compare our results to those obtained by mapping warm dark matter constraints to other models with suppressed small-scale structure, and find that these methods would overestimate the constraining power for this model.

papers.title: Quantum Correlations Between Two Giant Dipole Resonances in Ultra-Peripheral Collisions
papers.summary: Mutual Coulomb dissociation in ultra-peripheral heavy-ion collisions is dominated by Giant Dipole Resonance (GDR) excitation, whose subsequent decays produce forward neutrons. Standard descriptions treat the two GDRs excited in opposite nuclei as statistically independent, leading primarily to a quadrupolar azimuthal correlation determined by the common photon-polarization axis. In this work, we investigate the possibility that the two GDRs are instead prepared with a correlated quantum phase during the overlap of the electromagnetic pulses. We develop a phase-sensitive GDR decay model and implement it in a modified version of the \texttt{$n_{0}^{0}n$} Monte Carlo generator, allowing a quantitative comparison among three competing mechanisms: the weak dipolar modulation from electromagnetic recoil, the quadrupolar correlation from independent polarized GDR decays, and the phase-sensitive dipolar modulation associated with the proposed phase-lock scenario. For neutron pairs with small relative emission-time differences, the correlated-phase scenario produces a pronounced first-harmonic modulation in the two-neutron relative-azimuth distribution. Averaging over all relative emission times substantially reduces this modulation. Within the adopted energy-dependent angular model, the time-selected dipolar coefficient increases in magnitude with pair-mean neutron kinetic energy. These results identify neutron relative-azimuth correlations and their energy dependence as experimentally accessible observables for probing quantum phase correlations between the two GDR excitations. Such phase-sensitive correlations could also provide a basis for future tests of quantum entanglement between spatially separated GDR excitations at RHIC and the LHC.

papers.title: Search for $\mathrm{GeV}$-scale axion-like particles in PbPb collisions
papers.summary: A search is performed for the production of axion-like particles with masses in the range 3-10 GeV using PbPb collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of $0.228~\mathrm{nb}^{-1}$ and a nucleon-nucleon centre-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s_{\mathrm{NN}}}=5.02$ TeV. This is the first search for axion-like particles produced exclusively by two photons ($\gamma\gamma\to a\to\gamma\gamma$) in the forward direction. It extends sensitivity to previously unexplored regions of the parameter space, probing axion-like particle masses and couplings down to 3.0 GeV and $3.2\times10^{-4}~\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$, respectively. This result provides the most stringent limits to date on the production of axion-like particles from exclusive photon-photon fusion processes with masses between 3 and 5 GeV.

papers.title: Evidence for the decay $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ and improved measurements of the decay $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$
papers.summary: The first single-experiment evidence for the rare decay $B^0 \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ and the world's most precise measurements of the $B^0_s \to \mu^+ \mu^-$ branching fraction and effective lifetime are reported. The results are obtained using Run 3 proton-proton collision data corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 18 fb$^{-1}$ recorded with the LHCb Upgrade I detector at a centre-of-mass energy of $13.6$ TeV between 2024 and 2025. Their combination with the Run 1 and Run 2 LHCb results further improves the precision. All measurements are found to be in agreement with the Standard Model expectations.

papers.title: Heavy Quarkonium Physics: An Experimental Review at Tevatron, LHC, and e+e- Colliders
papers.summary: We review recent experimental advances in heavy quarkonium physics at the Tevatron, e+e- colliders (Belle, BaBar, Belle II, BESIII, and LEP), and the LHC (ALICE, ATLAS, CMS, and LHCb), including Run 2 and early Run 3 results. Differential cross sections and polarization measurements of charmonium (Jpsi, Psi(2S)) and bottomonium (Upsilon(nS)) test perturbative and non-perturbative QCD within the Non-Relativistic QCD (NRQCD) framework and probe symmetry relations among spin and orbital configurations. CDF and D0 established production baselines and exposed polarization tensions with early NRQCD predictions. Complementary e+e- measurements provide precise spectroscopy, branching fractions, radiative and hadronic transitions, and observations of exotic quarkonium-like states, constraining non-perturbative dynamics. LHC measurements extend production and polarization studies across broad kinematic ranges. Spectroscopic advances include fully-heavy tetraquark candidates, exotic structures in Jpsi Jpsi and Jpsi Psi(2S) reported by LHCb, and studies of toponium (ttbar) quasi-bound states. Sequential bottomonium suppression in PbPb collisions probes the quark-gluon plasma, while pPb measurements constrain cold nuclear matter effects. Multi-quarkonium production explores multi-parton interactions and exotic-hadron structure. Together, these results establish heavy quarkonium as a laboratory for QCD and a probe for physics beyond the Standard Model, while highlighting unresolved theoretical challenges. Future programs at the LHC, Belle II, and BESIII promise greater precision and new discoveries.

papers.title: Measurement of the $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ element of the CKM matrix using $\mathrm{t\bar{t}}$ events in pp collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A measurement of the magnitude of the Cabibbo$-$Kobayashi$-$Maskawa matrix element $V_\mathrm{cb}$ is presented using top quark pair events produced in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV. The data correspond to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$ collected by the CMS experiment at the LHC. The measurement targets the lepton+jets final state, where one W boson decays leptonically and the other hadronically. The value of $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ is extracted from the branching fraction of the W $\to$ cb decay. To identify this rare signal amid the dominant W $\to$ ud and W $\to$ cs backgrounds, a multivariate discriminant based primarily on the b jet tagging information of the jets assigned to the hadronic W boson decay is used. The measured value is $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ = [4.59$^{+0.44}_{-0.48}$ (stat) $^{0.64}_{-0.76}$ (syst)] $\times$ 10$^{-2}$. This measurement provides a complementary determination of $\lvert V_\mathrm{cb}\rvert$ at the electroweak scale, independent of the nonperturbative quantum chromodynamics inputs used in measurements based on semileptonic B meson decays.

papers.title: World average charged-current inclusive neutrino cross section from 6 to 200 GeV
papers.summary:
The methods of the Particle Data Group are applied to produce a world average inclusive, charged-current, muon neutrino cross section energy-dependence slope $\sigma/E_
u$ . For the energy range $30 < E_
u < 200$, values obtained are (0.677 $\pm$ 0.013) and (0.335 $\pm$ 0.007) $	imes 10^{-38}$ cm$^2$/GeV for neutrino and anti-neutrino, respectively. These values are practically identical to those in common use. This paper expands the experiments whose data are used and describes the evolution of measurements leading to the result. Next, the value for $\sigma/E_
u$ is obtained for the low energy extensions by experiments that used the low-$
u$ method to anchor to the high energy result. In the range $6 < E_
u < 30$ GeV, values of (0.698 $\pm$ 0.018) and (0.316 $\pm$ 0.012) $	imes 10^{-38}$ cm$^2$/GeV are obtained. These are higher than the high energy average for neutrino and lower for anti-neutrino, but consistent at the edge of the uncertainty estimates. An interpretation of the evolution of the inclusive cross section, nuclear effects, and isoscalar corrections is provided in the context of the Bodek Yang 2000 model and two configurations of the GENIE neutrino event generators. These cross sections underpin foundational neutrino quantities such as structure functions, electroweak parameter measurements, and oscillation parameter determinations.

papers.title: CELEBI: Design and Realization of a Reproducible Physics Analysis Framework
papers.summary: Reproducibility in modern physics analysis requires more than preserving source code or workflow descriptions. Analyses evolve through changes in code, configurations, parameters, input datasets, and dependencies, requiring a coherent representation of both the analysis and the provenance of its results. We present Celebi, a framework for organizing and preserving evolving physics analyses while keeping analysis definitions lightweight and separate from generated data products. Celebi maintains analysis definitions and preserved states in an Analysis Repository, while execution and generated results are managed separately through a Production Factory. The middleware layer, Yuki, connects preserved analysis states to execution infrastructure by constructing executable Snakemake workflows and dispatching them to supported runners, keeping the analysis representation independent of execution backends. This paper presents three main design concepts. First, the workflow architecture provides a modular representation of analysis components and their dependencies. Second, a structured file organization realizes this model in a human-readable form, separating reusable algorithms, task-specific configurations, parameters, documentation, and dependencies into well-defined objects. Third, the impression mechanism preserves immutable states of these objects and their dependencies, assigning persistent identities to specific analysis configurations and linking generated results unambiguously to their originating states. Together, these concepts establish a coherent representation of evolving physics analyses, supporting reproducibility, provenance tracking, collaboration, and long-term preservation.

papers.title: CELEBI: Towards Reproducible and FAIR Physics Analysis
papers.summary: Modern physics analyses evolve continuously as datasets, selections, parameters, software environments, and analysis strategies are updated. Over the lifetime of an analysis, this evolution can make it difficult to determine the conditions under which an earlier result was produced or to transfer the analysis reliably between collaborators. We present Celebi, an analysis-management framework that maintains a persistent connection between evolving analysis materials and their generated results. Celebi organizes reusable algorithms, tasks, and their dependencies into a structured workflow, preserves selected states as immutable impressions, and associates retained results with the states responsible for their production. This organization supports analysis modification, systematic variations, collaboration, and review while the working analysis continues to evolve. Celebi supports controlled rerunning of preserved analysis states. When results remain retained, they can be inspected and compared together with their corresponding states. By capturing provenance during everyday analysis development, Celebi reduces the need to reconstruct analysis history retrospectively and provides a practical foundation for more transparent and reusable physics analysis.

papers.title: Search for supersymmetric particle pair production in final states with two oppositely charged leptons and large missing transverse momentum in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV
papers.summary: A search is presented for direct production of pairs of supersymmetric particles in final states with a pair of oppositely charged leptons (electrons or muons) and missing transverse momentum. The analysis uses proton-proton collision data at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 138 fb$^{-1}$, recorded with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC. The observed data do not exhibit any excess over the standard model predictions. Constraints are derived on chargino, top squark, and slepton pair production in the context of simplified models with $R$-parity conservation. In these models, the neutralino is taken to be the lightest supersymmetric particle. For chargino production, an exclusion region in the chargino-neutralino mass plane is determined, which extends to chargino masses of 1120 GeV and neutralino masses of 490 GeV. For mass splittings between the lighter top squark and the neutralino ranging from the W boson mass to the top quark mass, top squark masses up to 500$-$540 GeV are excluded. Slepton masses are excluded up to 700 GeV for a massless neutralino.

papers.title: Experimental Searches for Muon to Electron Conversion in Nuclei
papers.summary: Charged lepton flavor violation (CLFV) provides a highly sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model. This experimental review discusses $\mu^{-} \to e^{-}$ conversion in nuclei, which is a muon CLFV process characterized by a clean monoenergetic-electron signature and the ability to exploit large samples of stopped muons. It describes the physics motivation, basic experimental principles, key background sources, and search strategies, as well as the status and prospects of past and next-generation experiments such as COMET and Mu2e. Future experimental concepts may extend the sensitivity even further. If a signal is observed, comparisons among results obtained with different target nuclei and with those from complementary searches for other muon CLFV decay modes will be essential for identifying the underlying interaction.

papers.title: Search for dark photon dark matter near $\mathbf{1\,meV}$ using a superconducting mixer
papers.summary: We demonstrate the use of a superconducting mixer for direct searches for dark photon dark matter (DPDM) in the meV mass range. DPDM couples to the ordinary electromagnetic field through kinetic mixing with a coupling constant $\chi$ and can convert into ordinary photons at the surface of a metal plate. For DPDM masses of 1 meV, the conversion photons have frequencies of around 240 GHz. At such frequencies, superconducting mixers enable low-noise spectroscopic measurements. We performed a direct search for DPDM in the mass range 1.0047578-1.0047598 meV, corresponding to the frequency range 242.94935-242.94983 GHz, using approximately one hour of data obtained with a cryogenic millimeter-wave receiver based on a superconducting mixer. No significant excess was found, and we set upper limits of $\chi < (1.6\text{-}1.9)\times10^{-9}$ at the 95% confidence level. These limits are comparable to existing constraints from solar dark photons. By applying this method, we plan to extend the search to the wider mass range of 0.7-1.1 meV, corresponding to 170-260 GHz, with improved sensitivity.

papers.title: Study of the up-down asymmetry in $B^+\to K^+\pi^+\pi^-\gamma$ using $K_1(1270)$ amplitudes constrained by semileptonic $D$ Decays
papers.summary: Using $K_1(1270)\to K\pi\pi$ amplitude models constrained by the charmed-meson semileptonic decays $D^{+(0)}\to K^-\pi^+\pi^{0(-)} e^+\nu_e$, we present a model-dependent estimate of the up-down asymmetry observed in $B^+\to K^+\pi^+\pi^-\gamma$ in the mass region $M_{K^+\pi^+\pi^-}\in[1.1,1.3]$~GeV/$c^2$. Estimates based on an isolated $K_1(1270)$ show significant model dependence, but systematically lie below the measured asymmetry $\bar{\mathcal{H}}_{\mathrm{ud}}=(0.092\pm0.023)$ when assuming $\lambda_\gamma=1$. We also explore interference with the $K_1(1400)$ tail and find that it can appreciably reduce the tension.

papers.title: Two-peak gravitational wave spectra from supercooled two-field phase transitions
papers.summary: We study the gravitational wave (GW) spectrum generated by supercooled first-order phase transitions in two-field conformal models. We construct three representative toy models that capture the essential features of these models, derive analytical criteria for the existence of two-step transitions, and show how the two-field dynamics generate a genuine two-peak GW spectrum. We identify regions of parameter space in which two-peak GW spectra are observable at LISA and the Einstein Telescope. By way of illustration, we apply our analysis to a realistic conformal dark SU(3) model.

papers.title: Probing the charm-quark dead cone effect in heavy ion collisions
papers.summary: The first experimental study of the dead-cone effect for the charm quark in heavy ion collisions is presented. The analysis is based on a sample of lead-lead (PbPb) collisions at a center-of-mass energy per nucleon pair of 5.02 TeV, recorded by the CMS experiment at the CERN LHC in 2018 and corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 1.7 nb$^{-1}$. The studied observable is the angular distribution of hard, collinear intrajet emissions that are selected with the late-$k_\mathrm{T}$ grooming algorithm. The analysis is performed using inclusive jets and a sample of jets containing prompt D$^0$ mesons. The angular distribution of late-$k_\mathrm{T}$ emissions in PbPb collisions is found to be shifted towards larger angles in D$^0$ jets relative to inclusive jets, indicating a suppression of collinear splittings for D$^0$ jets. This shift, which is expected from the dead-cone effect, is consistent with a similar observation made in proton-proton collisions. The new measurement disfavors hypotheses that predict a filling of the charm-quark dead cone by medium-induced radiation in heavy ion collisions.

papers.title: Light nucleus and hypernucleus production at RHIC and LHC energies: a comparative study of phenomenological models
papers.summary: This document summarizes the work of the EMMI Rapid Reaction Task Force on ``Understanding light (anti)nuclei production at RHIC and LHC'', which took place at GSI on 8--12 April 2024. The meeting brought together experimentalists and theorists to discuss the current understanding of light-nuclei and hypernuclei production in high-energy hadronic collisions, with particular emphasis on statistical hadronization, coalescence, kinetic, and transport approaches. The discussions addressed the experimental status and the ability of different theoretical descriptions to reproduce the available measurements, as well as the connections between nuclear production, femtoscopic correlations, source sizes, nuclear wave functions, and the formation dynamics of loosely bound states. This document reviews the main experimental and theoretical developments presented during the RRTF, summarizes the key questions that emerged from the discussions, and identifies observables and future measurements that may help discriminate among different production mechanisms.

papers.title: First evidence of the decay $B^+\to\pi^+ e^+ e^-$
papers.summary: The first evidence for the decay $B^+\to\pi^+ e^+ e^-$ is reported using proton-proton collision data recorded by the LHCb experiment at centre-of-mass energies of 7, 8 and 13 TeV, corresponding to an integrated luminosity of 9 fb$^{-1}$. A signal excess with a significance of 3.2$\sigma$ is observed and the branching fraction is measured to be $\cal{BR}(B^+\to\pi^+ e^+ e^-) = (2.4\,{}^{+0.9}_{-0.8} \,{}^{+0.4}_{-0.2}) \times 10^{-8}$, where the first set of uncertainties is statistical and the second is systematic. The result is consistent with the Standard Model expectation.

papers.title: Search for pair production of additional neutral scalars within the Inert Doublet Model in a final state with two electrons or two muons in proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV and 13.6 TeV
papers.summary: A first dedicated search for pair production of new scalars predicted by the Inert Doublet Model is performed using proton-proton collisions. Data were collected with the CMS detector at the CERN LHC at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13 TeV and 13.6 TeV, corresponding to integrated luminosities of 138 fb$^{-1}$ and 35 fb$^{-1}$, respectively. Within this model, four additional scalar bosons (H, A, H$^+$, and H$^-$) are predicted. Through an additional discrete symmetry, the lightest new scalar, H, is stable, rendering it a viable dark matter candidate. These candidates can originate from quark-antiquark annihilation producing an offshell Z boson that decays to a pair of the new scalars. The target final state consists of exactly two opposite-charge same-flavour leptons (electrons or muons), with missing transverse momentum due to the stable neutral scalars, and very little hadronic activity. A parameterised neural network is used to separate the signal from the standard model background. No significant excess of events is observed. Exclusion limits at 95% confidence level are set on the production cross section of the two new neutral scalars, H and A, expressed in terms of their masses, $m_\mathrm{H}$ and $m_\mathrm{A}$, in the $m_\mathrm{H}$ vs. $m_\mathrm{A} - m_\mathrm{H}$ plane. The observed (expected) exclusion region reaches $m_\mathrm{H}$ = 108 (106) GeV for $m_\mathrm{A} - m_\mathrm{H}$ = 78 (76) GeV and at $m_\mathrm{H}$ = 70 GeV, covers the range of $m_\mathrm{A} - m_\mathrm{H}$ = 40$-$90 (35$-$90) GeV.

papers.title: First measurements of vector boson scattering in W$^\pm$W$^{\pm}$ and WZ production in all-leptonic final states at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV
papers.summary:
The production cross sections of W$^\pm$W$^{\pm}$ and WZ boson pairs in association with two jets in proton-proton collisions are measured at $\sqrt{s}$ = 13.6 TeV. The data sample corresponds to an integrated luminosity of 171 fb$^{-1}$, collected with the CMS detector during 2022$-$2024. The measurements are performed in the leptonic decay modes: W$^{\pm}$Z $	o$ $\ell^\pm
u\ell^{\prime\pm}\ell^{\prime\mp}$ and W$^\pm$W$^{\pm}$ $	o$ $\ell^\pm
u\ell^{\prime\pm}
u$, where $\ell, \ell'$ = e or $\mu$. The electroweak productions of W$^\pm$W$^{\pm}$ and WZ bosons are each observed with a significance greater than five standard deviations from the background-only hypothesis. Differential fiducial cross sections as functions of several observables are also measured.

papers.title: Neutral kaon mass measurement with the CMD-3 detector at VEPP-2000
papers.summary: Using more than 600 thousand $K_{S}^{0}\to\pi^{+}\pi^{-}$ decays from the $e^{+}e^{-}\to\phi(1020)\to K_{S}^{0}K_{L}^{0}$ reaction, the neutral kaon mass has been measured with the CMD-3 detector at the VEPP-2000 collider. Using the beam energies control by the back-scattering laser light photons, and a calibration to the world average $\phi$-meson mass, the neutral kaon mass is determind to be m($K^0$) = 497.587 $\pm$ 0.004(stat.) $\pm$ 0.008(syst.) $\pm$ 0.009(calibr.) \mevcc, where the first uncertainty is statistical, the second is systematic, and the third is the uncertainty from the energy calibration.

papers.title: First double-differential measurement of pionless charged-current muon neutrino interactions using kinematic imbalance observables on carbon and oxygen with the T2K experiment
papers.summary: We report the first measurement of muon-neutrino charged-current cross section as a function of kinematic imbalance (KI) observables on oxygen with no pions and at least one proton in the final state, using the T2K ND280 detector. The cross section is extracted simultaneously for carbon and oxygen targets and double-differentially as a function of several KI observables, providing new insight into the modeling of nuclear effects. This joint measurement offers direct sensitivity to the correlations between two targets, a key ingredient for reducing systematic uncertainties in neutrino oscillation experiments that employ multiple target nuclei, such as T2K and Hyper-Kamiokande. Comparisons with predictions from widely used neutrino event generators show that none of the models fully describe the data across all regions of measured phase space. These results highlight possible directions where improvements in neutrino-nucleus interaction modeling are needed for current and future neutrino oscillation experiments.

papers.title: Signal selection and model-independent extraction of pionless charged-current muon neutrino cross section using double-differential kinematic imbalance observables on carbon and oxygen with the T2K experiment
papers.summary: We present the first joint measurement of muon neutrino CC$0\pi Np$ interactions on carbon and oxygen targets, in two double-differential kinematic imbalance (KI) observable spaces, $\delta p_{T}$-$\delta \alpha_{T}$ and $p_{N}$-$\cos\theta_{\mu}$. The measurement employs the ND280 detector of the T2K experiment and includes a detailed description of the event selection used to define signal and control regions, the evaluation of systematic uncertainties, and the signal extraction procedure, together with validation studies supporting a robust cross-section measurement. The results of this analysis indicate that current neutrino-nucleus interaction models do not adequately describe the data, and demonstrate the strong discriminating power of KI observables. This measurement highlights the need for improved theoretical nuclear modeling within neutrino interaction generators to achieve increased precision in neutrino oscillation measurements.

papers.title: Evidence of the $e^+ e^-\to f_1(1285)$ reaction with the CMD-3 detector at VEPP-2000
papers.summary: A search for the $e^+ e^-\to f_1(1285)$ reaction is performed with the CMD-3 detector at the VEPP-2000 collider. Data from a scan in the center-of-mass energy range Ec.m.=1.20--1.36 GeV with 109.1 pb$^{-1}$ of the integrated luminosity is used. A dedicated 51.7 pb$^{-1}$ have been collected at the $f_1(1285)$ resonance peak energy Ec.m.=1282 MeV, where $26.5 \pm 7.4$ events have been found in the $e^+ e^-\to\eta\pi^0\pi^0$ reaction. No indication of the signal is observed in the scan data. We interpret the result as a statistical 4.5$\sigma$ evidence of the C-even resonance production in the $e^+ e^-\to f_1(1285)\to\eta\pi^0\pi^0$ reaction via the two-photon interaction. The production cross section is found to be $\sigma(e^+ e^-\to f_1) = 0.074 \pm 0.021 \pm 0.010$ nb, and the corresponding branching fraction to the $e^+ e^-$ pair is $B(f_1(1285)\to e^+e^-) = (8.3 \pm 2.3 \pm 1.1)\times 10^{-9}$.

papers.title: Recent results in $b \rightarrow s\,\ell\ell$ transitions at LHCb
papers.summary: Rare decays of $B$ hadrons, such as $b\rightarrow s\ell \ell$ processes, provide great avenues to search for the influence of new physics (NP). They are highly suppressed in the Standard Model (SM) and therefore sensitive to NP contributions. In recent years, experimental measurements have shown tension with SM predictions. It is still up for debate whether these stem from genuine NP or an incomplete understanding of the theory. These proceedings focus on the recent efforts of the LHCb collaboration to advance this field. Some of the results covered show that tensions in these processes, like in $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0}\, \mu^+ \mu^-$, still persist upon higher precision. Others aim to shed some light on the theoretical picture through amplitude analyses of decays like $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0}\, \mu^+ \mu^-$ and $B^+ \rightarrow K^+ \, \mu^+ \mu^-$. We also present two innovative measurements: the branching fraction of $B^0 \rightarrow K^+ \pi^- \mu^+ \mu^-$ at large dihadron mass; and the first hadron collider measurement of the lepton flavour universality ratio of $B^0 \rightarrow K^{*0} \, \ell^+\ell^-$ at high $q^2$ (dilepton mass squared).

papers.title: Generalizable Equivariant Diffusion Models for Non-Abelian Lattice Gauge Theory: Analytical Foundations and Numerical Scaling Tests
papers.summary: Gauge-equivariant diffusion models can be used to generate ensembles of field configurations in non-abelian lattice gauge theories. Previously, we demonstrated the feasibility of modeling these theories by combining L-CNN-based diffusion models with the Metropolis-adjusted annealed Langevin algorithm (MAALA). Here we focus on the underlying analytical framework. In particular, we present a rigorous derivation of the reverse-time stochastic differential equation on the group manifold, discuss the gauge invariance of the denoising loss function, and provide extensive numerical benchmarks regarding the scaling behavior with respect to the lattice volume and the inverse coupling $\beta$. Full analytical expressions for arbitrarily sized Wilson loops and the topological charge susceptibility during the forward process are given as well.

papers.title: Full edge control of bulk energy gap in armchair graphene nanoribbons
papers.summary: In solid-state physics, the ability to open and tune an electronic energy gap provides a direct route to controlling charge transport and accessing distinct electronic phases. In solids with physical boundaries, a bulk energy gap formed exclusively by extended bulk states is conventionally expected to be governed primarily by the interior bulk region, with only a minor contribution from the boundaries. Here we show that, in stark contrast to this conventional expectation, the bulk gap of armchair graphene nanoribbons in the $N_w=3p+2$ family with $p\in\mathbb{Z}\ge 0$ can be fully controlled through the hoppings solely at the boundaries. This full boundary control originates from an exact cancellation between the gap contributions of long-range hoppings along and across the ribbon in the bulk region. It persists in the presence of Hubbard interactions and holds irrespective of ribbon width in this family. Our findings establish boundary dynamics as an unexpectedly powerful means of manipulating bulk electronic properties, enabling width-preserving engineering of one-dimensional (1D) band structures and topological phases, with potential applications in qubits, artificial quantum spin chains, topological quantum dots and other quantum devices.

papers.title: Beyond Point Photo-$z$ Estimates: Normalizing Flows for Tomographic $N(z)$ Reconstruction with DESI DR1
papers.summary: Accurate calibration of tomographic redshift distributions, $N(z)$ is essential for cosmological analysis of weak lensing data. We investigate conditional normalizing flows (NFs) and compare their performance with random forest (RF) and quantile random forest (QRF) models. We consider DESI galaxy and quasar targets from DESI DR1 spectroscopic data and with the photometry from Legacy Surveys DR10. We train on 1.1 million sources and test on 2.0 million sources in a non-overlapping sky region ($01.6$. By introducing distribution-level metrics like Wasserstein distance and JS divergence, we find that stacking NF posterior PDFs provides more accurate tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction than QRF, particularly at high redshifts. For $z_{\rm median}>2.5$, the NF achieves a smaller absolute mean-redshift bias ($0.060\pm0.031$ versus $0.318$) and higher probability overlap ($0.905\pm0.008$ versus $0.787$) than QRF. We apply redshift-dependent post-hoc PDF calibration derived from a held-out validation sample. After calibration, the absolute mean-redshift biases in four bins spanning $0.2<z_{\rm median}<1.0$ range from $0.0016$ to $0.0019$, with central values below referring benchmark $0.002(1+z)$. In the highest-redshift bin, calibration further reduces the bias to $0.016\pm0.011$. Our results demonstrate the potential of NF PDFs for tomographic $N(z)$ reconstruction while highlighting challenges in transferring models across galaxy populations.

papers.title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamics at z=1.7: Resolved tSZ and X-ray analysis of CL J0459.6-4946
papers.summary: Measurements of the entropy and temperature distribution of the intracluster medium (ICM) of local clusters have proven pivotal for the study of cluster astrophysics. Here, we extend these measurements to $z=1.7$ with a resolved analysis of the ICM in ACT/SPT-CL J0459.6-4946. By combining high-resolution thermal Sunyaev-Zeldovich measurements using new, deep ALMA Band 1 and 3 observations, with archival X-ray data, we conclude that the cluster has (i) an ICM with a flat and relatively high ($\approx 200$ keV cm$^2$) entropy distribution out to $\approx 0.3\,r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, (ii) a hot core ($T_{\mathrm{e}} \simeq 14$ keV) with a declining temperature profile, (iii) a short effective path length along the line of sight of $l_{\mathrm{eff}} \simeq (0.75 \pm 0.05) \times r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$, and (iv) a clumpiness factor $C = \langle n_{\mathrm{e}}^2 \rangle / \langle n_{\mathrm{e}} \rangle^2 \simeq 1.17 \pm 0.05$ within $r_{500,\mathrm{c}}$. Its dynamic nature and high redshift suggest that the cluster is still thermalising its ICM, consistent with a relatively large hydrostatic mass bias of $b = 1 - M_{500,\mathrm{c,HE}}/M_{500,\mathrm{c,WL}} = 0.27^{+0.32}_{-0.67}$ that we measure with respect to the weak lensing mass. Furthermore, a region with low entropy and high density to the south of the cluster centre is observed in the X-rays yet absent in the Compton-$y$ map, indicating pressure equilibrium; we interpret this as a sloshing cold front -- the first such detection at high redshifts. This case study demonstrates that $\approx 3$h-long ALMA observations, combined with comparatively "short" X-ray exposures ($\approx 122$ ks), can fully characterise the ICM at high redshift, opening a path towards the thermodynamics of young and distant galaxy clusters for larger samples.

papers.title: Wide-field search for submicrosecond optical and gamma transients as manifestation of primordial black holes evaporation with the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array
papers.summary: We demonstrated in our papers [Panov, 2021; Panov,2025), that the TAIGA-HiSCORE Cherenkov array physics, originally designed for research in cosmic rays and ultra-high-energy gamma-ray astronomy, can also be used for wide-field searches for very rare submicrosecond optical transients of astrophysical origin. The papers \cite{PANOV-2021,PANOV-2025} presented the results of the first four seasons of optical transient searches (2018--2022) and the resulting upper limits on the flux of corresponding events. The present paper presents data processing from two new seasons of optical transient searches (2022--2024). This paper further develops a method for searching for narrow spatiotemporal groups of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays (above 100\,TeV). Since the evaporation of relic black holes can be accompanied by both by the emission of a short light pulse and by a flash of ultra-high-energy gamma-rays, a multimessenger technique for searching for black hole evaporation was in fact implemented in this work, where two different methods are implemented within a single instrument. The search for narrow spatiotemporal groups of gamma-rays was carried out in time windows of 1000\,$\mu$s, 100\,$\mu$s, and 6\,$\mu$s. Since narrow groups of gamma were not detected, the upper limit on their frequency were obtained as $10^{-3}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$. The upper limit on the number of submicrosecond optical transients have also been updated: $10^{-4}\mathrm{erg/s/cm}^2$ as $5\cdot10^{-4}\,\mathrm{ster}^{-1}\mathrm{h}^{-1}$.

papers.title: First-principles calculations of far-wing absorption in He-broadened CO2 infrared spectra
papers.summary: We report theoretical predictions and modeling of the far-wing absorption of CO2 broadened by He over a wide temperature range (200-1000 K), which are relevant for exoplanet atmosphere studies. Accurate modeling of He-broadened CO2 absorption is essential for opacity calculations used to characterize the composition, structure, and climate of exoplanet atmospheres. In particular, the strong CO2 band at 4.3 mum has been clearly identified in the spectra of several exoplanets observed with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). Requantized classical molecular dynamics simulations were first performed to predict absorption in the far wings of the 4.3 mum band of CO2. The resulting predictions show excellent agreement with available experimental data at room temperature. The theoretical predictions and measured data were then used to parameterize an impact energy-corrected sudden model, which allowed us to accurately reproduce the far-wing absorption of He-broadened CO2 in several infrared spectral regions over the (200-1000) K temperature range. Finally, for applications to exoplanet atmosphere opacity calculations, we derived temperature-dependent chi-factor corrections that account for the sub-Lorentzian behavior of the far wing of the major infrared bands of CO2.

papers.title: Developing Environments: Formation and Quenching at Cosmic Noon Traced by the Large-scale Distribution of Gas and Galaxies
papers.summary: Environmental density correlates with galaxy properties in the local Universe, but how and when these trends emerge is unclear: at cosmic noon, large-scale structures are still assembling and galaxies quench rapidly for debated reasons. We study how the formation and quenching histories of massive galaxies at $1.71$), mostly in massive quiescent galaxies showing both. About 65\% of the sample follows a correlation between the tracers; two outlier regions stand out. A galaxy-rich, gas-poor region ($\delta_\#>2$, $\delta_{HI}1$), within 60 cMpc of the densest Hyperion cores, hosts rapidly quenched galaxies with a high incidence of AGN and outflows. This \emph{developing environment}, distinct from both mature protoclusters and the field, likely traces massive halos still assembling. Galaxy counts alone cannot capture the environment at cosmic noon: jointly mapping galaxies and cool gas is crucial to understand how environment regulates gas accretion, star formation, and quenching.

papers.title: EMBER: A Little Red Dot Candidate at $z_{\rm spec}=10.36$ in the Seed Black Hole Era
papers.summary: Little red dots (LRDs) are a newly discovered population that may trace rapidly growing black holes (BHs) and provide a link between seed BHs and luminous active galactic nuclei (AGNs). However, no LRD had previously been spectroscopically confirmed at $z>10$, leaving this earliest phase observationally unexplored. Using JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy from the EMBER program, we measure a spectroscopic redshift of $z_{\rm spec}=10.361^{+0.003}_{-0.002}$ for \target, the highest-redshift LRD candidate known to date. The redshift is constrained by a prominent Ly$\alpha$ break and multiple tentative emission lines, including C\,{\sc iv}\,$\lambda\lambda1549,1551$ and [O\,{\sc iii}]\,$\lambda4363$ detected at $S/N=3.9$ and $3.6$, respectively. Its extreme NIRCam-MIRI color of $m_{\rm F444W}-m_{\rm F770W}=1.82\pm0.1$, characteristic V-shaped continuum with a turnover near the Balmer limit, and continuum slopes of $\beta_{\rm UV}=-2.26^{+0.11}_{-0.11}$ and $\beta_{\rm opt}=1.17^{+0.74}_{-0.70}$ all support its LRD nature. A possible iron complex at $\lambda_{\rm rest}\sim0.24$--$0.25\,{\rm \mu m}$ and a possibly high $\log\left([{\rm O\,III]\,\lambda4363/\rm H\gamma}\right)=0.17^{+0.24}_{-0.22}$ further support an AGN-like interpretation, as seen in previously known LRDs. Tentative detection of Ly$\alpha$ emission may indicate enhanced Ly$\alpha$ transmission at $z\sim10$. Our findings extend the observational frontier of BH growth into the seed-BH formation era, and upcoming MIRI spectroscopy will further establish the physical nature of the source.
