papers.title: MARTA: A "little" black hole hidden in a clumpy, metal-poor galaxy at z~3.8
papers.summary: JWST has extended the search for accreting black holes into the high-redshift, low-mass regime. We report a low-mass black hole candidate in MARTA 3887, a clumpy, metal-poor galaxy at $z=3.7694$, combining deep JWST/NIRSpec spectroscopy, HST and JWST imaging, and archival VLT/MUSE data. We detect a broad H$\alpha$ component with $L_{\rm H\alpha,b}=2.35\times10^{41}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and FWHM $=1270^{+260}_{-250}$ km s$^{-1}$, with no [O III] counterpart of comparable width. Under a broad-line-region interpretation, virial calibrations give $\log(M_{\rm BH}/M_\odot)=6.52^{+0.18}_{-0.23}$ and $\lambda_{\rm Edd}=0.07$, or up to 0.38 for alternative calibrations. The host comprises at least three compact clumps, with $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=8.16^{+0.09}_{-0.10}$. If stellar photoionization dominates the narrow lines, the gas is highly ionized and metal poor, with $12+\log({\rm O/H})=7.68\pm0.04$ ($\simeq0.10\,Z_\odot$). The inferred $M_{\rm BH}/M_\star=2.3\%$ lies about 2 dex above the extrapolated local relation, suggesting that black-hole growth has outpaced the assembly of the observed host. If growth began only when the first 10% of the observed stellar mass had formed ($t_{10}=92$ Myr ago), a $10^2\,M_\odot$ seed would require a lifetime-mean Eddington ratio $\simeq5.7$; earlier growth or a more massive, e.g. direct-collapse, seed would allow sub-Eddington mean accretion. MUSE reveals extended Ly$\alpha$ emission ($\simeq6.5$-6.9 proper kpc), offset by $+64^{+10}_{-8}$ km s$^{-1}$ from systemic, with a provisional escape fraction of $\simeq0.44$. Together with a Mg II doublet ratio close to the optically thin limit and a high [O III]/[O II] ratio, this makes MARTA 3887 a laboratory to study black-hole growth, stellar assembly, and ionizing-photon escape jointly.

papers.title: A Supermagnified Little Red Dot with a Resolved Host
papers.summary: Little red dots (LRDs) are an intriguing new class of sources in the early universe discovered by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) characterized by V-shaped spectra and extremely compact sizes. Their underlying mechanisms still remain the subject of ongoing debate. We present JWST observations of a gravitationally lensed LRD nicknamed "Best Friend" at $z_{\rm spec} = 8.297\pm0.002$. Its high magnification factor of $\mu = 36^{+8}_{-12}$ makes it the highest magnified LRD reported to date and unveils both the resolved structure of its host and a central engine less than 7 pc in size. The spectrum of the central engine, in which broad lines are not detected, possibly owing to the limited S/N and spectral resolution, is better interpreted as black hole activity rather than a dense star cluster. The latter cannot be fully excluded, but if true, the resulting lower limit on stellar density would be $>1.25^{+0.4}_{-0.3}\cdot10^6 \mathrm{M_{\odot}/pc}^2$, which is around 2 orders of magnitude higher than stellar densities of typical clusters at high-z. By performing a spatially resolved analysis of NIRCam photometry and NIRSpec/PRISM spectroscopy, we find that the host stellar mass is $\log(M_\star/M_{\odot}) = 7.3^{+0.2}_{-0.8}$. Best Friend demonstrates the power of lensing to reveal the morphologies of LRDs.

papers.title: Intranight optical monitoring of eight quasars with superluminal jets and low optical polarization: Probing the mechanism of rapid flux variability
papers.summary: Intranight optical variability (INOV) of blazars whose emission arises predominantly from a relativistic jet, has been widely linked to a combination of two key observational diagnostics: the fractional optical polarization ($P_{opt}$) and the Doppler boost arising from relativistic beaming of the jet's emission. To discern which of these two factors plays the dominant role, we investigate INOV of a well-defined representative sample of 8 flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs, which are `low-synchrotron-peaked' blazars) whose jets exhibit a low degree of polarization ($P_{opt}$ 5\%$) is found to be zero, applying the normally used $F_{\eta}$ test, and $\sim 7\%$ using the more powerful `enhanced $F$-test'. The small DC, despite the strong Doppler boost expected from the observed high superluminality, shows that strong INOV is much rarer among LPSQs, compared to high-polarization quasars, for which DC $(\psi > 5\%$) is found to be around 30%, even using the $F_{\eta}$ test. This provides the first compelling evidence that optical polarization is the primary diagnostic of INOV, while relativistic beaming plays a supportive role. Possible implications for the proposed mechanisms for INOV are pointed out.

papers.title: Dust-induced reversal of the optical wavelength dependence of spiral-arm pitch angles
papers.summary: The classical density-wave scenario predicts a blue-to-red age--colour gradient across the spiral arms of disc galaxies as a consequence of shock-induced star formation. However, observations of spiral-arm pitch angles at different wavelengths sometimes suggest the opposite trend, namely a red-to-blue ``colour jump''. The origin of this apparent contradiction remains unclear. In this work, we investigate the effects of dust attenuation on post-shock stellar emission, together with the streamline motions of gas and stellar populations. We find that dust attenuation in regions with relatively high optical depths, $\hat{\tau}_{V} \gtrsim 0.2$, can produce an apparent red-to-blue spatial sequence, with respect to the shock location, by reversing the relative positions of the flux maxima of stellar populations observed in different bands. Moreover, streamline motions confine post-shock stellar populations near the spiral arms for longer than in a circular-orbit model, thereby modifying the spatial distribution of the emitted light. We conclude that the apparent red-to-blue colour jump does not necessarily contradict the classical density-wave scenario. Instead, it can arise from the same post-shock stellar populations that intrinsically produce a blue-to-red age--colour gradient if their emission is modified by dust attenuation.

papers.title: The MAGPI Survey: the evolution of galaxy spin-filament alignments since z~0.3
papers.summary: We present measurements of galaxy spin-filament alignments at 0.20<z<0.42 using the MAGPI Survey, exploiting resolved stellar and ionised gas kinematics to reconstruct 3D spin axes. Cosmic filaments are identified using a stellar mass-matched constant-number-density population from the GAMA, MAGPI Redshift Survey and DESI datasets. We detect a flipping of the statistical alignment signal at z~0.3 as a function of M*: low-mass galaxies preferentially exhibit spins parallel to the direction of their host filaments, while high-mass galaxies tend towards perpendicular orientations. The transition mass is measured to be log(M{*,t}/Msun)~10.8, approximately 0.6 dex higher than the value for the SAMI Galaxy Survey at z~0.05. Bootstrap analysis gives 99.5% confidence that the transition mass is higher for MAGPI than SAMI. At fixed stellar mass MAGPI galaxies exhibit stronger parallel alignments than their SAMI counterparts, suggesting evolution of spin-filament alignments over the past ~3 Gyr. The gaseous component in MAGPI galaxies is more closely aligned with filaments than the stellar component, relative to a M*-matched SAMI sample. This indicates a stronger coupling between ionised gas and the large-scale structure at z~0.3, consistent with coherent gas accretion onto filaments remaining efficient at higher M*. At z~0 we detect a transition toward perpendicular alignments at lower M*, while the gas and stellar components exhibit similar alignments relative to filaments, likely due to the cumulative effects of mergers and secular evolution.

papers.title: A VLT/CRIRES+ study of helium 1.083$\mu$m absorption features towards the inner Orion Nebula
papers.summary: JWST NIRCam F115W observations towards the inner Orion Nebula revealed a diverse array of previously unknown dark features. The most likely cause was absorption or suppressed emission of the helium 1.083$\mu$m triplet which lies in that filter. We have obtained VLT/CRIRES+ high-resolution spectrographic observations over a selection of different dark targets, confirming that the features are indeed explained by a reduction in the flux of the helium 1.083$\mu$m triplet, a reduction that is fairly uniform across the line. The Orion Nebula is a blister HII region, with a dense, bright ionised layer on the far side from the observer near the Orion A molecular cloud and lower density gas elsewhere. Using a simple radiative transfer model, we show that dark features arise when emission from the dense layer is absorbed by intermediate density helium (e.g. in clumps, globules, or winds from objects like proplyds) on the near side of the dense layer.

papers.title: Probing the geometry and outflows of the accreting millisecond pulsar SAX J1808.4-3658 with multi-band polarimetry
papers.summary: We present VLT/FORS2 R- and I-band imaging polarimetry of the accreting millisecond X-ray pulsar SAXJ1808.4-3658 during its 2025 outburst, coordinated with the first X-ray polarimetric observations of this source with IXPE. We detect significant optical linear polarisation at every epoch (polarisation degree P~0.3-1.5%, angle Phi ~ 8-48{\deg}), consistent with the only prior optical polarimetric campaign of this source, obtained during a previous outburst. The average optical polarisation angle is offset by ~16-24{\deg} from the IXPE angle of the persistent X-ray emission, which pulse-profile modelling shows to trace the spin axis. A fast-timing sequence reveals the optical polarisation angle swinging by up to ~40{\deg} within minutes, disfavouring scattering in the disc. A colour-magnitude diagram and the dependence of the optical polarisation on the red colour excess over the disc emission, which we attribute to the jet, instead point to a jet origin during the main outburst, consistent with contemporaneous radio detections. The offset, with the same mean optical angle as in the previous outburst, can arise from emission near a wide jet base, where the Doppler-boosted side of the cone dominates. At the onset of the reflaring stage the optical polarisation degree is highest and its angle coincides with the IXPE one, while the disc likely dominates the optical flux. We discuss a polarisation flare of the fading jet, scattering in an outflow, and synchrotron emission at the disc-magnetosphere boundary as possible origins, tentatively favouring the last.

papers.title: Euclid Quick Data Release (Q1). Mass-to-light ratio of elliptical galaxies: constraints from strong lensing
papers.summary: Mass is among the most fundamental properties describing a galaxy. The relation between the luminosity and the total mass of a galaxy contains information on the efficiency of the star formation process and on the distribution of dark matter. We used strong gravitational lensing data from the Euclid Quick Data Release 1 (Q1) to constrain the total mass enclosed within an aperture of $5\,h^{-1}$kpc, $M_5$, of elliptical galaxies. Our analysis is based on a sample of 95 lenses, which we built by ensuring that their selection function is reproducible. This enabled us to correct our inference for selection effects. The average $\log_{10}{(M_5\,h\,M_\odot^{-1})}$ for a galaxy with an $r$-band luminosity of $10^{10.7}L_{\odot}\,h^{-2}$ at $z=0.5$ is $11.30\pm0.02$. The mass $M_5$ scales with luminosity to the power $\beta_\mathrm{L}=0.71\pm0.07$, and decreases with increasing redshift at fixed luminosity. Assuming a scenario in which galaxies grow by mergers and stellar populations evolve passively, these correlations imply that $M_5$ increases with time for individual galaxies. These measurements provide a useful benchmark for testing models of galaxy structure and evolution that make predictions on the distribution of total mass on the scales of $5\,h^{-1}$kpc.

papers.title: Shear Mapping in Python (SMPy): Modular, Extensible, and Accessible Dark Matter Mapping
papers.summary: Understanding the Universe's large-scale distribution of dark matter is a central objective in the era of precision cosmology. A key technique for the study of dark matter is weak gravitational lensing: a phenomenon where light from distant galaxies is sheared as it passes through the gravitational field of a massive object, like a galaxy cluster. This shear, which manifests as a slight (weak) distortion of shapes over thousands of galaxies, allows astrophysicists to infer the distribution of total matter, including both luminous and dark matter. Obtaining a mass distribution from a catalog of galaxy shears involves reconstructing the convergence ($\kappa$), the projected surface mass density divided by the critical surface density for the lens-source system. The Shear Mapping in Python (SMPy) package provides a standardized, well-documented, and open-source solution for creating convergence maps from weak lensing galaxy shear measurements. SMPy implements three mapping methods: the classic Kaiser-Squires inversion, aperture mass mapping, and, to our knowledge, the first publicly available implementation of the full KS+ algorithm, which corrects for missing data, field borders, and reduced shear. SMPy was initially developed to support the Superpressure Balloon-borne Imaging Telescope (SuperBIT) and has since evolved into a general-purpose tool suitable for analyzing the weak lensing data from cosmological surveys.

papers.title: Slowly rotating white dwarfs in f (R, T ) = R + 2{\lambda}T gravity: structure and stationary tidal response
papers.summary: We calculate the structure and stationary tidal response of cold carbon fluid white dwarfs in $f(R,T)=R+2\lambda T$ gravity through second order in uniform rotation. Equilibria are compared at fixed baryon number, with angular momentum also conserved during each aligned electric quadrupolar tidal perturbation. Negative coupling increases radii and dimensional tidal deformabilities over the common mass range. For the baryon sequence studied, background readjustment accounts for 95.8--97.5\% of the rotational enhancement at 40\% of each model's Kepler reference frequency. The explicit mixed rotational tidal contribution is positive and numerically resolved, but subdominant. At that spin, the enhancement relative to each coupling's static model decreases from 107.4\% in general relativity to 14.2\% at the most negative coupling, despite its larger absolute deformability. This reduction reflects less relative background expansion and a different Love-number variation.

papers.title: The L1157 filament as traced in HNCO by the LMT
papers.summary: Context. The L1157 outflow is a prototype of chemically active outflows where to look for molecular species linked to complex chemistry. Aims. With the aim of imaging the large (parsec) scale structure of key prebiotic molecules, we have mapped the whole blue-lobe of the L1157 outflow with the Large Millimeter Telescope (LMT), proving the potential of this facility to detect weak and extended molecular emission. Methods. Isocyanic acid, HNCO, an important precursor of complex chemistry, was chosen to be observed in its (4_0,4-3_0-3) transition at 87.925 GHz with the SEQUOIA focal-plane array, covering an area of 3x3 arcmin2 centered at the position of the main shock L1157-B1, which included a large portion of the vicinity of the protostellar region. Results. The HNCO emission was detected not only from the outflow but it also was found tracing a structure of about 0.3 pc in length, corresponding to the filament from which the protostellar system was born. Conclusions. The HNCO molecule was found to be a tracer of the densest part of filaments in molecular clouds, and given its importance in the formation of more complex molecules, its presence in the cold, quiescent filamentary gas indicates that the building blocks of complex chemistry are already well established in stages prior to protostellar warming or shocks. By allowing the detection of structures related with the filament, these observations proved the LMT potentialities to map weak and extended components in molecular clouds.

papers.title: CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stacking Search (CHAMPSS): Power Spectrum Injections and Survey Sensitivity
papers.summary: Artificial signal injection into real data is a key tool in time-domain radio astronomy, with particular import to the study of pulsars and Fast Radio Bursts (FRBs). Many surveys inject into the time series to probe observational biases impacting the detection of radio transients. In the case of the CHIME All-sky Multiday Pulsar Stack Search (CHAMPSS), the computational demands of both hardware and software time series injections force an alternative approach. We present methods for injecting artificial pulsar signals into the Fourier power spectrum. The injection process detailed here is computationally negligible compared to the overhead of the CHAMPSS search pipeline. We use injections to probe the in-system biases of the CHAMPSS survey. CHAMPSS is most sensitive to pulsars with frequencies on the order of 0.1 - 100 Hz and fluxes > 1 mJy. Our injections show weak overall sensitivity dependence on other factors such as dispersion measure (DM), duty cycle, and sky coordinates, but complex non-monotonic interactions between all parameters. Our findings suggest that frequency-dependent noise, especially low-frequency or "red" noise, and sampling limitations at higher frequencies are the dominant extrinsic factors decreasing CHAMPSS' sensitivity to pulsars.

papers.title: Modeling CO Line Luminosity with FIRE simulations: II. Comparison With Observations, CO Luminosity Functions and Redshift Evolution
papers.summary: We present predictions for the CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) luminosities of 765, 850, 887 and 915 galaxies at z=0, 1, 2 and 3, respectively, drawn from the Feedback in Realistic Environments (FIRE-2) simulations and post-processed with SKIRT radiative transfer and CLOUDY line emission calculations. We compare our CO line luminosity predictions with existing observations. At z=0, our predictions reproduce the observed scatter and mean relation between star formation rate (SFR) and CO(1-0) luminosity for both massive star-forming galaxies and low-metallicity dwarf galaxies. We also reproduce the observed superlinear power-law slope between CO(1-0) luminosity and metallicity. At z=1, our CO(2-1) predictions scatter to much lower luminosities than observed, which likely reflects the limited sensitivity of current surveys. At fixed SFR, our CO(1-0) luminosities decrease by roughly an order of magnitude per unit increase in redshift. This decline is likely driven by the decrease in metallicity with increasing redshift, since FIRE-2 galaxies with comparable SFR and metallicity produce similar CO(1-0) luminosities regardless of redshift. At fixed stellar mass, the predicted luminosities show no redshift dependence. These results show that our FIRE-2 predictions reproduce the observed scaling relations between CO(1-0) luminosity and galaxy properties wherever the observed galaxies are robustly detected. This gives us confidence in our predictions for the regime where no observational data exist, and suggests that our luminosity predictions can be used to build predictive models for CO line intensity mapping experiments.

papers.title: HD 210058 b and BD+37 4838 b: A precessing eccentric hot Jupiter and a misaligned substellar companion around two A-type stars
papers.summary: The number of A- and F-type stars known to host exoplanets is relatively low, as is the number of planets with measured spin-orbit angle, which is the angle between the planet's orbital axis and the star's rotational axis. Expanding the sample of such systems is important for constraining the formation and migration mechanisms of close-in giant planets around early-type stars. We aim to measure the sky-projected spin-orbit angles of HD~210058b (TOI-1355b) and BD+37~4838b (TOI-1414b), two objects still listed as candidate exoplanets, and to assess the planetary nature of these systems. Both of their host stars are fast rotators. We analyzed TESS photometry together with transit time-series of HARPS-N spectra. For both objects, we created cross-correlation functions from the spectra to analyze Doppler tomography and detect and model the Doppler shadow, while we also used the photometric observations to refine a number of previously poorly constrained photometric and spectroscopic parameters of both the host stars and the companions. When possible, we used the derived results to constrain the companion masses. We verified the planetary and substellar nature for both objects respectively. We report HD~210058~b to be a giant hot Jupiter with a mass of 10 M_Jup, residing on a slightly misaligned orbit with the sky-projected spin-orbit angle {\lambda}=-32 -6 +4 deg. Archival photometry reveals continuously changing inclination and impact parameter, pointing to a nodal precession with period of 860 yr, and giving availability of only about six upcoming years for any further transit observations. The second target, BD+37~4838~b, orbits a hybrid {\gamma}~Dor-{\delta}~Sct pulsator on a misaligned orbit with {\lambda}=56.9 +1.4 -2.3 deg. Since we could not reliably recover its mass, we only report an upper limit of approx. 24.3 M_Jup, leaving the possible planetary nature of this object unresolved.

papers.title: A multiprobe $\Lambda$CDM consistency analysis with gravitational-wave standard sirens
papers.summary: Multi-messenger cosmology offers an independent path to stress-test the $\Lambda$CDM model as gravitational wave (GW) catalogs grow in size. We present the first multiprobe assessment of $\Lambda$CDM tensions incorporating GW standard sirens: LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA Collaboration (LVK) fifth Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog (GWTC-5.0) standard sirens are combined with Dark Energy Survey (DES) Year 6 weak lensing and galaxy clustering (3$\times$2pt), baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO), and type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia), together with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) BAO, and confronted with primary cosmic microwave background (CMB) measurements from Planck, the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT), and the South Pole Telescope (SPT). All probes are analyzed under homogeneous priors and combined via normalizing flows, and we quantify the $S_8$ discrepancy and $H_0$ tension with respect to CMB. Adding standard sirens to the 3$\times$2pt analysis improves the constraints in the $\Omega_m$-$S_8$ plane by $\sim$30%, while constraining $H_0$ to 6.2%. We present cosmological constraints from the low-redshift probes including standard sirens, yielding $S_8 = 0.793 \pm 0.010$, $\Omega_m = 0.308^{+0.007}_{-0.006}$, and $H_0 = 69.4^{+4.1}_{-4.4}$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$. At current GW sensitivity, however, both the $S_8$ discrepancy and the $H_0$ tension remain essentially unchanged. Our analysis nonetheless delivers the first assessment of $\Lambda$CDM tensions computed with standard sirens included among the probes, and establishes them as a mature cosmological probe -- ready to be combined on equal footing with established datasets in forthcoming surveys such as the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), Euclid, and Roman.

papers.title: A temporally clustered gravitational wave pair and a Type IIb supernova
papers.summary: Compact object mergers are generally expected long after the stellar collapse that forms their remnants. Here we report two marginal gravitational wave (GW) candidates, S190910d and S190910h, separated by 7.1 hr, whose three-dimensional localizations overlap at the position and distance of the Type IIb supernova SN 2019rsq. The GW pair lies in the extreme tail of the joint distribution of temporal separation and localization overlap, with a pairwise null probability of $7.6 \times 10^{-5}$ under our Monte Carlo null test. Independent re-analyses recover both as signal-like candidates. Under a common-origin hypothesis, S190910h remains consistent with a low-mass compact binary with source-frame masses near $2.5 + 1.3\,M_\odot$, whereas S190910d favours a strongly asymmetric $\sim 34 + 3\,M_\odot$ system whose observed amplitude is compatible with the supernova distance. SN 2019rsq is a rapidly evolving stripped-envelope Type IIb explosion whose light curve is consistent with stellar collapse occurring near the GW activity. Although the supernova coincidence alone is not statistically rare, its timing and physical properties provide a stellar collapse anchor for the unusual GW pair. A fragmenting collapsar disk provides a plausible framework that can accommodate the component masses, hour-scale delays and supernova properties, raising the possibility that multiple compact object mergers can accompany a single stellar collapse episode.

papers.title: Double White Dwarfs with Circumbinary Disks: Evolution, Population Properties, and Gravitational Wave Signatures
papers.summary: Double white dwarfs (DWDs) are important multi-messenger sources and powerful probes of binary interaction physics. Close DWDs formed through isolated binary evolution are expected to have negligible eccentricities. However, recent observations have revealed that some eclipsing DWDs exhibit eccentricities of order $10^{-3}$ or larger. In this work, we investigate the interaction between a circumbinary disk (CBD) and the central DWD, where the CBD is assumed to form from a recent common-envelope (CE) ejection. Our models are the first to include CBD-DWD interaction in DWD population synthesis and to constrain disk parameters such as disk mass and lifetime. Our population models predict a correlation between the eccentricity distribution and the orbital period distribution of DWDs, which can be tested by future observations. Furthermore, we discuss the influence of CBD on the gravitational-wave (GW) signal. The CBD-DWD interaction can shrink the orbit and excite eccentricity, extending the time for which the system is individually resolvable by a future space-borne GW detector. Our results suggest that CBD interaction should be accounted for in population synthesis of Galactic DWD GW sources and the stochastic GW foreground.

papers.title: Gravitational Capture of Large Interstellar Planetesimals by Collapsing Prestellar Cores
papers.summary: We investigate the capture of free-floating planetesimals by the time-varying gravitational potential of a collapsing prestellar core. We use one-dimensional collapse models to estimate the volume of space from which planetesimals are captured. We combine this calculation with an estimate of the size distribution and velocity dispersion of the free-floating planetesimal population to determine the largest planetesimal that is typically captured, as well as the total mass of all planetesimals captured by a given protostar. We consider two cases: one in which the free-floating planetesimal population comes from the birth cluster of the star, and one in which the planetesimals are captured from the Galactic population of free-floating planetesimals. We find that the details of the collapse matter substantially, with the predicted diameter of the largest captured body from the Galactic population ranging from $2.8$ km to $6.4$ km depending on collapse model, and the largest body from our model birth cluster environment ranging from $70$ km to $1200$ km, for assumed velocity dispersions ranging from 0.7 to 8.5 km/s. The total solid mass captured by this mechanism does not exceed 0.07 Earth masses in all cases. We discuss the effect of these captured objects on the planet formation process, and argue that while the total solid mass captured is likely not significant, the largest captured bodies may grow to planet size via accretion of pebbles present in their host disks. This process may accelerate planet formation, or enable it in disks that have difficulty in forming their own planetesimals.

papers.title: A Unified Mass-Loading Model for ASKAP J1745-5051: Linking Long-Period Radio Transients to Magnetic Cataclysmic Variables
papers.summary: Long-period radio transients (LPTs) in white dwarf binaries require sufficiently tenuous plasma to sustain coherent radio emission, posing a challenge in systems with dense accretion flows. ASKAP J1745-5051 (J1745) combines LPT-like radio pulses recurring approximately every 82 min with magnetic accretion and X-ray modulation at a consistent period. We investigate this coexistence using a unified mass-loading framework for Roche-lobe overflow and a tenuous donor wind in the binary magnetic field. The dense stream supplies the accretion curtain and near-white-dwarf X-ray sources, while the tenuous wind feeds flux tubes of $(1-4)\times10^7\,{\rm cm^{-3}}$, satisfying the local density requirement for electron-cyclotron maser emission. A fiducial geometry places the X-ray maximum near orbital phase $0.886$ and produces a radio-visibility window at phases $0.22-0.33$, consistent with the primary observed pulse window. Geometrical modulation and curtain absorption produce stronger soft-band than hard-band X-ray variability. Long-term phase-connected radio monitoring and simultaneous X-ray observations can test this interpretation through recurring radio phase changes and correlated changes in X-ray modulation. These results extend the proposed connection between detached binary LPTs and magnetic cataclysmic variables (mCVs). J1745 may represent an evolved mCV near the orbital-period minimum, suggesting that LPT-like activity can occur at a late accreting stage.

papers.title: EMU/GAMA: Understanding the link between dust geometry and star formation rate in galaxies
papers.summary: We investigate the link between dust obscuration and star formation rate (SFR) estimators using Halpha luminosities, L_Halpha and radio luminosities, L_radio. While the Balmer Decrement (BD) is the standard tool for attenuating Halpha, it can fail to account for optically thick dust regions from which Halpha cannot escape. The ratio of SFRs estimated from radio luminosity and L_Halpha corrected for dust attenuation using the BD can be used as a probe of the degree of optically thick dust affecting Halpha. We explore this combining Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) Early Science data at 887.5MHz in the Galaxy and Mass Assembly (GAMA) G23 field with the GAMA data. We draw on dust estimates using both the BD and the dust mass, M_d, demonstrating systematic underlying dependencies with L_radio/L_Halpha. By combining the BD and M_d, we quantify how they relate to L_radio/L_Halpha and other galaxy properties. We use this approach to establish an Halpha SFR (SFR_Halpha) estimator that accounts for optically thick dust, demonstrating its consistency with conventional SFR indicators. Rather than proposing a replacement for standard correction methods, we aim to demonstrate the effectiveness of a dust geometry model that integrates both BD and M_d parameters. This H_dust parameter provides a more physically complete representation of optically thick environments that traditional methods may overlook, and can produce SFR estimates consistent with traditional techniques.

papers.title: Two Isolated Microlensing Events Near the Upper Shore of Einstein Desert
papers.summary: The Einstein desert is a deficit in the angular Einstein-radius ($\theta_{\rm E}$) distribution of isolated objects over the range $9 {\rm \mu as} < \theta_{\rm E}<26 {\rm \mu as}$. Although this interval contained no events when the desert was first identified, several subsequent detections have fallen within it, raising questions about its detailed structure and requiring a larger detection sample. In this paper, we report the observations and analyses of two microlensing events possibly caused by isolated giant planets or brown dwarfs whose $ \theta_{\rm E}$ lie near the upper shore of the desert. MOA-2021-BLG-145 has $ \theta_{\rm E} = 23.1\pm2.0 ~{\rm \mu as}$, placing it just inside the upper boundary, and KMT-2026-BLG-0357 has $ \theta_{\rm E} = 36.5\pm 3.7~{\rm \mu as}$, placing it above the desert. We also compare the $ \theta_{\rm E}$ distributions of isolated objects and bound planetary events. The bound population shows no corresponding deficit over the same range, suggesting that the Einstein desert may be associated with the formation or subsequent evolution of the isolated population. Furthermore, some FFPs may lie above the upper shore of the Einstein desert, indicating that a more complete understanding of the FFP population requires direct lens-mass measurements.

papers.title: Tracking the evolution of sub-Neptunes. I. Gyrochronology of planet hosting stars
papers.summary: Stellar age is fundamental for reconstructing planetary-system evolution but remains difficult to determine for unevolved main-sequence stars. Stellar rotation provides a sensitive age diagnostic and a temporal framework for investigating the evolution of close-in planets. This is the first paper in a series aimed at tracing the evolution of the sub-Neptune population through homogeneous ages of their host stars. We compiled rotation periods and stellar parameters for 4639 confirmed exoplanet hosts. Gyrochronological ages were inferred using a two-zone rotational evolution model and a Bayesian approach combining rotation periods, dereddened Gaia (BP-RP) colours, and literature stellar masses as Gaussian priors. Rotational tracks were extended to the terminal-age main sequence, beyond the empirical calibration range. We obtain gyrochronological constraints for 2204 host stars. Well-constrained ages have typical formal uncertainties of 10--15%, offering substantially greater precision than is generally achievable through isochrone fitting for unevolved stars. Inferred stellar masses agree with the literature priors, while model effective temperatures are consistent with independent determinations. Ages beyond the open-cluster calibration range remain model-dependent. The resulting homogeneous catalogue provides the age framework for investigating the evolution of sub-Neptune populations and the emergence of the radius valley. Stellar parameters, provenance, and gyrochronological results are publicly available through CDS.

papers.title: Cometary dust activity as a proxy for refractory organic material release
papers.summary: Cometary dust is an important reservoir of refractory organic matter and may contribute to the redistribution of carbon-rich material throughout planetary systems. We investigate whether the widely used dust-activity parameter $Af\rho$ can serve as a first-order observational proxy for the release of refractory organic material. A sample of 27 active small bodies representing active asteroids, main-belt comets, quasi-Hilda comets, quasi-Trojan objects, Jupiter-family comets, Centaurs, and long-period comets was compiled from published photometric studies. Representative near-perihelion, phase-corrected $A(0)f\rho$ values span more than three orders of magnitude, from a few centimetres for weakly active asteroids and main-belt comets to $\sim 10^4$ cm for the most active long-period comets. The large dispersion within individual dynamical classes shows that orbital classification alone does not determine the level of dust activity. Direct compositional measurements of cometary dust, including the high refractory-organic fraction measured for 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko, support the interpretation of dust activity as an indirect indicator of potential organic-material release. However, a universal conversion of $Af\rho$ into dust mass-loss rate is not possible because of uncertainties in grain-size distribution, density, porosity, velocity, and optical properties. We therefore suggest that $Af\rho$ may be used as a comparative, first-order proxy for refractory-organic material release.

papers.title: A JWST/NIRSpec Catalog of Low-Mass Candidates toward NGC 2024 from Multi-component Spectral Modeling
papers.summary: Young low-mass objects in crowded, highly obscured star-forming regions are difficult to characterize. Deriving reliable physical parameters requires separating photospheric emission from complex extinction and circumstellar emission. We apply a multi-component spectral-modeling framework to JWST/NIRSpec PRISM spectra toward NGC 2024, obtaining adopted fits for 78 sources. The framework incorporates atmospheric models, dust and ice opacities, and optional thermal emission. Most spectra favor additional large-H$_2$O-ice opacity over the baseline small-grain model, while a smaller subset requires additional gray opacity, potentially arising from large refractory grains. Some spectra also require a thermal component to reproduce the long-wavelength continuum. The parameters inferred with this framework, together with the NGC 2024 distance, yield radii and bolometric luminosities. Comparison with evolutionary models for young low-mass and substellar objects provides mass estimates and identifies 46 candidate members, 27 sources classified as background, and five uncertain sources. Candidate members show lower fitted surface gravities than likely background stars. Of the candidate members, 23 lie above the youngest available isochrones, plausibly reflecting the cluster's youth and uncertainties in model initial conditions. The resulting catalog provides a uniform characterization of the NGC 2024 sample and establishes a framework for treating complex extinction and circumstellar emission in JWST spectra of other obscured star-forming regions.

papers.title: Probing the nature of Galactic microquasars with diffuse gamma rays and neutrinos: low-mass versus high-mass X-ray binaries
papers.summary: The observations of sub-PeV gamma-ray emission have provided strong evidence for a Galactic origin of the cosmic-ray "knee" region. Meanwhile, mounting observations have ruled out most supernova remnants as sources of PeV cosmic rays, i.e., the so-called PeVatrons. Recently, a new type of PeVatron candidate, microquasars, has received much attention. Studies indicate that microquasars could be the dominant contributor to PeV cosmic rays. However, the spatial distribution of microquasars is not known. They could belong to either LMXBs or HMXBs, depending on the mass of the optical companion star. In this work, we study which type could be the dominant by means of very high energy gamma rays and neutrinos. We find that the diffuse gamma-ray distributions along the Galactic longitude are quite different due to the spatial distributions of these two kinds of sources. If the very high energy gamma rays are dominated by the distribution of LMXBs, the gamma-ray distribution would be more concentrated toward the direction of the Galactic center. Furthermore, we also find that HMXB distribution cannot account for the latest observations of Galactic diffuse neutrinos. Higher-precision measurements of the Galactic diffuse gamma-ray and neutrino fluxes with LHAASO, HAWC, IceCube, and KM3NeT will allow the spatial distribution of the microquasar population to be determined and the origin of the knee to be tested.

papers.title: The upper main sequence in h and chi Persei
papers.summary: Binary interactions play a crucial role in the evolution and eventual outcomes of massive stars. Rich young open clusters provide large coeval populations to constrain the effects of binary evolution. The Double Cluster, with a turn-off mass well above the threshold for core-collapse supernovae, is an excellent test bed for these processes. We used h and chi Persei, together with NGC 663, to constrain the evolutionary pathways of massive stars, particularly the role of binary interaction. We present spectroscopy of around 80 stars to obtain spectral types and derive stellar parameters. We combined this dataset with Gaia astrometry to evaluate their evolutionary status and possible evolutionary paths. We derived atmospheric parameters for almost 60 stars in the upper main sequence (B2V and earlier) and found broad agreement between two independent fully automated procedures. We identified the cluster turn-offs between B1 V and B1.5-2IV and differentiated this feature from the vicinity of theTAMS, where we found a population of B1-B1.5 giants, with a high fraction of Be stars. The bulk of the population in all of the massive clusters studied in the Perseus arm is consistent with single-star evolutionary models at a given age, but some B-type supergiants are much more luminous than any other cluster star. Their typical cluster kinematics and stellar parameters suggest a merger origin. Other lower-luminosity B-type supergiants seem consistent with the rest of the population. Kinematic analysis has indicated that most Be stars have not been dynamically perturbed by a supernova explosion. Those below the turn-off are likely to have been formed via case A mass transfer. papers.title: exoALMA XXV: A Statistical Analysis of Gaseous Substructure in Low-Inclination Disks
papers.summary: Protoplanetary disks exhibit complex structure in both their gas dynamics and their temperature. Characterizing it has proven challenging, owing to the mismatch between the observed complexity and the relatively simple semi-analytical models typically used to interpret it. To augment these analyses, we apply the second-order structure function to the velocity and temperature perturbations of four low-inclination sources from the exoALMA program, each measured against a noise-only null built from the data themselves. All exhibit correlated structure. Its radial correlation length is limited by the beam in every case, which excludes non-axisymmetric structure on radial scales larger than ~1.5 pressure scale heights. In three of the four disks the structure is instead resolved and elongated in azimuth, by factors of 1.6-2.3, as expected of small-scale perturbations sheared out by Keplerian rotation. We further introduce two statistics that characterize spiral structure without tracing an arm crest: a modal power spectrum, measuring the periodicity of the azimuthal structure, and a winding contrast, measuring the radial dependence of its phase. The velocity residuals of three disks are significantly wound. MWC 758 is the only source in which the winding is coherent across the disk and shared by the temperature field. Its trailing m=1 temperature structure is consistent with the illumination of a warp, while its velocity field carries small-scale, sheared structure that could redistribute angular momentum. Because neither statistic requires a crest, both extend a quantitative description of winding to the flocculent regime, where a spiral cannot be parameterized.

papers.title: Roughness-Dependent Radiative Effects on Dimorphos within Hera's Reach
papers.summary: Following the Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) impact, radiative recoil, tides, and other dissipative processes drive the dynamical evolution of the Didymos-Dimorphos binary, yet the effect of unresolved surface roughness on radiative migration remains poorly quantified. We incorporate this roughness into a binary thermophysical model coupled to planar spin-orbit dynamics. During the 6-month investigation by ESA's Hera mission, surface roughness significantly reduces the radiative contribution to the mean orbital contraction rate by 28-39% relative to smooth surfaces for two post-impact shape models of Dimorphos in synchronous principal-axis rotation. With surface roughness included, planar-libration calculations still yield centimeter-scale radiation-driven orbital contraction that increases mean motion, contributing a mean of 40-85 deg to orbital-phase advance from DART to Hera's arrival. During Hera's investigation, radiative recoil in these calculations contributes a mean orbital-phase advance of 0.7-2.0 deg, which could be detectable given Hera's projected 0.05 deg formal orbital-longitude uncertainty. In the modeled tumbling state, the net radiative contribution to the mean orbital contraction rate over the same interval is much smaller, with surface roughness reducing it by 16-18%. These results identify thermal roughness as a key factor in radiative migration estimates that, combined with Hera's orbital and rotational observations, can constrain post-impact dissipation and rubble-pile mechanical properties relevant to planetary defense. Refining the thermophysical treatment of roughness with Hera's thermal and shape measurements can improve binary YORP estimates from remote infrared observations of other synchronous binaries, helping infer tidal response from measured orbital migration to probe asteroid interiors and advance understanding of binary evolution and lifetimes.

papers.title: Mean-element Parareal: Parallel-in-Time Integration of the Solar System
papers.summary: Long-term integrations of planetary systems have long been considered inherently sequential: each time step must start from the exact state at the end of the previous one, because any error in that state, however small, is amplified by orbital shear and chaos and alters the trajectory. Because a single step of a modern Wisdom--Holman integrator takes only ~100 ns - too short to split across cores - additional cores have previously only been used to run multiple simulations in parallel. We introduce mean-element parareal (MEP), a parallel-in-time scheme that accelerates a single Solar System integration (eight planets, general relativity) at the same accuracy as the serial integrator. Combined with a latency-optimized C kernel that integrates 5 Gyr on one core in 5.8 h, MEP completes a 5 Gyr integration in 52 min on 64 cores (a parallel speed-up of 6.7x, and 10.4x faster than the previous 9.0 h single-core record) or in 1.8 h on 16 cores (3.3x parallel speed-up, 5.0x faster than the previous record). MEP succeeds because its coarse propagator uses a numerical first-order mean-element theory to remove the short-period oscillations from the semi-major axes, preventing Keplerian shear from amplifying them into growing phase errors. Standard parareal with a coarse Wisdom-Holman integrator fails for planetary orbits because no inexpensive coarse integrator can resolve these oscillations. To our knowledge, this is the first measured multicore speed-up of a single long-term planetary integration and opens a pathway towards larger-scale parallelization.

papers.title: Detection and excision of radio-frequency interference in radio arrays
papers.summary: The detection and excision of radio-frequency interference (RFI) is usually approached by asking how best to identify RFI within a given data product. I address a prior question: which data product is a given RFI emitter is most detectable in? I develop a model for the suppression of RFI in visibilities and tied-array beams by the antenna primary beam, near-field wavefront curvature, bandwidth smearing, and fringe tracking. The comparison between antenna-based and array-based detection reduces to a single quantity related to the mean per-baseline RFI coherence. Cross-correlation detection is preferred only above a coherence threshold of $(N-1)^{-1/2}$, where $N$ is the number of antennas. I evaluate this model for four array configurations (the Very Large Array A and D configurations, and the fixed MeerKAT and Deep Synoptic Array / DSA configurations) and five representative RFI emitters spanning distances of 5\,km to medium-Earth orbit. Compact, filled, arrays favor the cross-correlations for stationary terrestrial emitters, whereas extended sparse arrays do not. RFI emitters with significant motion relative to radio arrays, in particular aircraft and low- and medium-Earth-orbit satellites, favor the sum of antenna autocorrelations everywhere by one to seven orders of magnitude, because their coherence is destroyed by rapid fringe rotation. For RFI below the single-antenna noise, no phase-unknown cross-correlation statistic is more sensitive than the autocorrelation sum. Tied-array beams are the least sensitive data product of all: the array factor supplies no suppression of terrestrial RFI, so a beam sees an emitter as a single antenna does. I describe a real-time, GPU-based implementation of autocorrelation-based excision for the 110-antenna Deep Synoptic Array, and outline the design implications for upcoming arrays.

papers.title: Introducing Aurora: A New Black Hole Seeding Model With Explicit Environmental Coupling
papers.summary: We present Aurora, a black hole seeding module for the Mimic semi-analytic framework, in which the seed mass of each newly resolved halo is set by its environment. Motivated by evidence that early quiescent galaxies and overmassive black holes assemble in dense environments, Aurora replaces the fixed seed masses of conventional prescriptions with a continuous spectrum, coupling the seed mass to two environmental parameters, the local overdensity and the radial skewness of the surrounding haloes, and to the halo mass at seeding. Requiring only halo masses and positions, it applies to dark-matter-only simulations. Calibrated against Sage on the Millennium merger trees, this prescription leaves a lasting signal. Massive black holes are assembled from the seeds of many progenitors, seeds supplying 29 per cent of all black hole mass formed by $z=0$. A seed-dominated growth pathway, distinct from the accretion-dominated majority, emerges among galaxies assembled rapidly in dense, asymmetric environments. Environment-dependent seeding raises the quiescent fraction of seeded galaxies in massive haloes at $z \simeq 3.1$ by up to 70 per cent, with the excess concentrated in overdense environments, and a deficit in voids. Scrambling the seeding environments while preserving the mass spectrum erases this gradient. The two environmental couplings imprint separable signatures, broadening the scatter of the galaxy-black hole mass relation while preserving the stellar-halo mass relation and other Sage summary statistics. We discuss applying Aurora at gigaparsec scales and higher resolution, to understand the origins of massive black hole systems in contemporary deep surveys.

papers.title: Witnessing pre-processing at intermediate redshift: observational evidence of infalling groups onto a merging galaxy cluster
papers.summary: The fraction of quenched galaxies increases with local density, and part of this trend is thought to arise in groups before cluster accretion (pre-processing). In merging clusters, this is difficult to separate from star formation triggered or suppressed by the cluster merger itself. We investigate whether five high-velocity galaxies in the merging cluster SPT-CL~J0307-6225 ($z=0.579$), distributed in two candidate infalling groups, show signs of group-scale environmental processing prior to accretion. We combine MUSE integral-field spectroscopy and HST imaging to derive [\ion{O}{ii}] kinematic maps, spectral classes, and star-formation rates (SFR), to understand the properties of the galaxies. We further use the Magneticum simulations and the phase-space information to determine if these galaxies are part of two groups, and if they will be accreted onto the merging cluster. Group~1 is a morphologically disturbed interacting pair bound to the cluster, with at least one galaxy classified as dusty starburst. Group~2 is a compact triplet at $\sim$4$\sigma_v$ from the cluster, in which two galaxies share a common [\ion{O}{ii}] envelope and the dominant member, an e(b) starburst, shows an elevated ionised-gas velocity dispersion. The SFR of both starburst galaxies lie within the scatter of the field star-forming main sequence, as expected for modest, interaction-triggered bursts. Close pairs at the phase-space position of group~2 occur for $\sim$1\% of comparable-mass cluster galaxies in Magneticum, so it is not unlikely for the group to be bound. Both groups show spatially resolved signatures of galaxy--galaxy interactions alongside ongoing star formation, supporting a pre-processing scenario in the environment of a merging cluster. Such group-scale interactions may contribute to the enhanced star formation reported in merging clusters.

papers.title: Dynamically defined bulges reveal that early-type galaxies with compact bulges host more massive black holes
papers.summary: We revisit the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation for early-type galaxies by introducing a uniform bulge defined by dynamical decomposition. From the set of nearby galaxies with accurately measured black hole masses, we select 30 early-type galaxies that have been observed with wide-field integral-field unit instruments (MUSE, ATLAS3D, or PPAK). For each galaxy, we construct an orbit-superposition Schwarzschild model and obtain its stellar orbit distribution. In this framework, we define the bulge uniformly as comprising stellar orbits with circularity $\lambda_z < 0.7$ (or, in an alternative definition, $\lambda_z < 0.2$) and lying within $r < 3$ kpc. From these orbits, we reconstruct the spatial density distribution of the bulge and measure its mass ($M_{bulge}$), size ($R_{bulge}$) and surface density slope ($\gamma_{bulge}$). We find that the dynamical bulge defined by $\lambda_z < 0.7$ yields masses that are systematically consistent with the photometric bulge masses. Comparing to the bulge from photometric decomposition, using this dynamical bulge definition slightly decreases the scatter around the best-fitting from 0.56 to 0.47. More interestingly, we identify a clear trend: at a given bulge mass, galaxies hosting more compact bulges (i.e. smaller bulge sizes or steeper bulge density slopes) systematically contain more massive black holes; eight outliers show overmassive BHs together with ultra-compact bulges. We interpret this as direct observational evidence that the $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}$ relation evolves over a galaxy's merger history, with that history imprinted in bulge compactness. Incorporating compactness via an $M_{BH}-M_{bulge}-R_{e, bulge}$ (or $\gamma_{bulge}$) relation brings the outliers into agreement and reduces the overall scatter of the sample to $\sim 0.3$.

papers.title: Bayesian and frequentist constraints on dark energy parameterizations using non-CMB data
papers.summary: Data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) BAO combined with the cosmic microwave background (CMB) have provided evidence for dynamical dark energy (DDE) with a phantom crossing ($w(z) < -1$) when constraining $w_0-w_a$ parameterizations. Given the tension between BAO and CMB data within $\Lambda$CDM, we use only non-CMB data: Type Ia Supernovae (SNe) from the DES-Dovekie compilation, DESI BAO DR2, Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) and Redshift-Space-Distortion (RSD) measurements. We use the dataset combinations GRB$+$BAO, BAO$+$SNe and GRB$+$BAO$+$SNe, each with RSD. We perform both Bayesian and frequentist analyses of two quintessence-inspired thawing dark energy parameterizations: the thawing quintessence parameterization (TQD) and the Algebraic Thawing parameterization (AT), together with the Chevallier-Polarski-Linder (CPL) and the Generalized Emergent Dark Energy parameterizations (GEDE). The GRB sample, used in this work, contributes only marginally to the constraints, while SNe tighten them considerably. The CPL equation of state shows a phantom crossing at $z\sim 0.5$, while TQD and AT improve the best-fit $\chi^2$ over $\Lambda$CDM, without showing phantom crossing. When SNe are included, TQD is preferred by the Bayes factor (moderately), AIC and DIC (positively). For CPL and AT, AIC and DIC prefer the extended model positively, while the Bayes factor weakly prefers $\Lambda$CDM over CPL and is inconclusive for AT. This difference is consistent with the Occam penalty from the prior volume in the Bayes factor. GEDE, with the DE density restricted to be suppressed at high redshifts is disfavored by all three metrics. Hence, the preference for DDE depends on the parameterization, the dataset and the comparison metric used.

papers.title: foraois: Fast, Flexible Extended Press-Schechter Merger Trees with a General First-Crossing Solver
papers.summary: We present foraois (Gaelic for Forest; FAW-reesh), an open-source Python framework for generating Monte Carlo dark matter halo merger tree histories. foraois separates the description of the linear density field, the physics of halo collapse, and the algorithmic construction of halo merger histories, allowing different cosmologies, collapse prescriptions, and tree building approaches to be combined within a common framework. The package implements two approaches to the same merger-tree problem of sampling progenitor masses in the excursion-set picture: the semi-empirical algorithm of Parkinson, Cole, & Helly (2008), which applies a fitted correction to the EPS progenitor distribution, and the numerical solution of the Markovian first-crossing equation developed by Zhang & Hui (2006), which for the default real-space top-hat window is an approximation to the correlated-walk problem. Linear matter power spectra for Cold, Warm, and Fuzzy Dark Matter (CDM, WDM, and FDM) can be supplied, while the modular collapse treatment provides an extension point for alternative barrier models. The framework also supports constrained merger histories based on the Brownian-bridge construction of Nadler et al. (2023). We run extensive validation and scaling tests, and also show an illustrative example of coupling foraois to a light-weight semi-analytical model of galaxy formation.

papers.title: Physically Motivated Stellar Populations for Galaxies at Cosmic Dawn with a Temperature-Dependent IMF
papers.summary: The first few years of James Webb Space Telescope observations have identified previously undetected galaxies at $z>12$ and provided new constraints on galaxies at $z>8$. Many of these objects have stellar masses that are difficult to reconcile with $\Lambda$CDM, inferred from models not calibrated for the high-redshift Universe. This necessitates new, more astrophysically plausible stellar population models for estimating stellar masses of galaxies at cosmic dawn. We introduce a simple stellar population (SSP) library, Simple Stellar Populations with Temperature (SSPT), computed using a temperature-dependent stellar initial mass function and its implementation in the public code CIGALE. When used in a configuration designed for high-redshift galaxies that requires young stellar population ages, the new models predict stellar masses that are ~0.3-0.5 dex lower than estimates from similar CIGALE analyses using models calibrated to the local Universe, and nearly 2 dex lower than estimates from analyses using other codes and softer constraints on stellar ages. Application of these physically motivated stellar populations suggests that stellar masses of early star-forming galaxies are not in tension with $\Lambda$CDM, and that galaxy formation from virialized halos remains a reasonable hypothesis at the highest redshifts. The SSPT SSPs and their CIGALE implementation are released publicly.

papers.title: An Unusually Clumpy Ultra-Diffuse Galaxy in the Coma Cluster: A Missing Link for Globular Cluster Formation?
papers.summary: We present a study of Coma-B122, an unusually clumpy star-forming ultra-diffuse galaxy (UDG) in the Coma cluster outskirts, using deep Keck Cosmic Web Imager integral-field spectroscopy and Subaru Hyper Suprime-Cam imaging. B122 hosts $\sim10$ luminous star-forming clumps contributing $\sim25$% of its luminosity and $\sim7$% of its stellar mass, with typical clump masses of $\sim10^6\ M_\odot$ comparable to the most massive super star clusters known in nearby starbursting dwarfs. The clumps form a distinctive ring configuration $\sim2$ kpc from the center. Full-spectrum fitting shows that $\sim12.5$% of the diffuse body's stellar mass formed during an extended episode of enhanced star formation over the past $\sim300$ Myr, within which all the clumps assembled. B122 shows evidence of weak ram-pressure stripping (RPS), including a diffuse light distribution truncated on the side facing the Coma center and extended to the opposite side, along with an asymmetric H I velocity profile. Its ordered stellar and ionized-gas rotation, cold gas fraction, and phase-space position are consistent with an early stage of infall. Spatial variations in clump star formation histories and gas-phase abundances further indicate that RPS-driven metal-poor gas inflow may have triggered and sustained the recent star formation. B122 may offer a rare present-day view of how UDGs assemble their globular cluster (GC) systems during cluster infall, although it remains uncertain if the clumps could survive as GCs. Future observations with higher spatial resolution and of more analogs are important to provide a complete picture of the formation and evolution of clumpy low-surface-brightness dwarf galaxies.

papers.title: FiDeR: Denoising Astronomical Images at the Observational Resolution
papers.summary: We present Finite-iteration Deconvolution--Reconvolution Denoising (FiDeR), a method for reducing noise in astronomical images while retaining approximately the input point-spread function (PSF). We first apply a finite number of Richardson--Lucy (RL) iterations to the nonnegative source-plus-background image. We then measure the response of a calibration point source processed with the same settings and derive a reconvolution kernel matched to the observational PSF. The calibration includes the background-to-source flux ratio. We compare FiDeR with six denoisers using simulated point-source and mixed stellar--galaxy fields, and observations from the James Webb Space Telescope Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) and Mid-Infrared Instrument (MIRI). In the stellar tests, bright-source widths remain close to the input widths; faint sources show small residual offsets. For the mixed field, FiDeR reaches peak signal-to-noise ratios of 46.701 and 44.850 dB at backgrounds of 10 and 20 counts per pixel, with wing errors of 0.657 and 0.858 counts. It also gives small aperture-flux and shape errors, although block-matching and three-dimensional filtering (BM3D) gives higher structural similarity. The NIRCam data show lower core and combined-region errors, while the three-exposure MIRI test gives benefits mainly in the stellar aperture and photometry. These results support substantial noise reduction with little change in the measured PSF within the tested regimes. The denoised images can provide inputs for further reconstruction and measurement; their uncertainties must account for residual noise correlations.

papers.title: Aperture Photometric Accuracy of Point-spread-function-deconvolved Astronomical Images
papers.summary: This paper introduces an improved Richardson--Lucy (RL) framework utilizing negative backfilling (NB) and the novel filtered image deconvolution and noise backfilling (FiDNoBa) algorithm. By integrating a low-pass prefiltering stage---specifically employing a Kalman filter---with the reintegration of filtered-out noise components after RL iterations, we effectively suppress noise artifacts while maintaining rigorous flux integrity. We extensively evaluate our Kalman + RL + NB approach using both numerical simulations and real observational data. Simulations across three regimes demonstrate superior photometric accuracy, reducing the relative mean deviation (RMD) to below 1\% for isolated sources, maintaining high fidelity (RMD $\sim$0.37\%) for blended S\'{e}rsic galaxies, and achieving $\sim$5\% RMD in crowded stellar fields while significantly increasing source recovery rates compared to traditional point-spread function photometry. Crucially, we validate the practical efficacy of FiDNoBa on real space-based (JWST/NIRCam) and ground-based (Very Large Telescope Survey Telescope OmegaCAM) images. The results confirm that our method reliably handles complex instrumental signatures, such as the extended wings of the STPSF, mitigating the severe ringing artifacts typical of traditional RL deconvolution while ensuring highly stable aperture photometry in practical survey processing.

papers.title: A potential observational test to disentangle the companion of binary millisecond pulsar PSR J1928+1815
papers.summary: Recently, the binary millisecond pulsar (MSP) PSR J1928+1815 (J1928) was reported to be experiencing regular radio eclipses. To produce the radio pulse emission and regular radio eclipses, this source was proposed to be most likely an MSP with a He star companion. However, the possibility that the companion is a white dwarf (WD) cannot be completely ruled out. Considering the uncertainty of interstellar dust extinction, it is difficult to confirm the nature of the companion star in the near-infrared and optical bands. Based on the measured mass function and orbital inclination angle inferred by the radio eclipses, the gravitational radiation can produce a period derivative of $-(6.8-9.6)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$ when the companion star of J1928 is an extremely massive WD ($1.4~M_\odot$). Therefore, its companion star can be identified as a He star with a mass higher than $1.4~M_\odot$ if the measured period derivative exceeds $-9.6\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. However, the expansion of a He star could cause a transfer of angular momentum from the orbital motion to the spin of the He star through a tidal interaction. The loss of orbital angular momentum results in a negative orbital period derivative, which produces an extra-contribution to the period derivative due to gravitational radiation. If the companion of J1928 is a $1.0-1.6~M_\odot$ He star, the predicted period derivative is in the range of $-(4.9-13.5)\times10^{-13}~\rm s\,s^{-1}$. In particular, the tidal interaction could help to confirm a He star with a mass of $1.35-1.5~M_\odot$. We also constrain the maximum evaporation efficiency of spin-down luminosity to be $0.006$ when the companion star of J1928 is a He star.

papers.title: Extreme Hard X-ray Variability in the TeV Blazar Mrk 421: Insights from NuSTAR Observations
papers.summary: In this work, we investigate the hard X-ray variability of the TeV blazar Mrk 421 over both long-term and intra-day timescales to gain insights into the particle acceleration and cooling mechanisms driving its emission. Using 27 NuSTAR observations spanning 2012 to 2024, we conduct detailed spectral and timing analyses. Our findings reveal pronounced flux variability, with changes by up to a factor of 200 over the decade and a 10-fold increase within a period of 15 days during a flaring episode. The flux distribution exhibits a lognormal profile, and a linear root-mean-square (RMS)--flux relation suggests a multiplicative variability process. Spectral analysis indicates that a log-parabolic model best describes most observations, with a strong linear anti-correlation between the photon index and curvature parameter. We also identify a positive correlation between the synchrotron peak energy and flux, accompanied by a subtle ``harder-when-brighter'' trend. These results align with standard blazar emission models, supporting particle acceleration via shock fronts or magnetic reconnection in the relativistic jet.

papers.title: Deconvolved IXPE Polarization Maps of the Crab Nebula in a Maximum-a-Posteriori Framework
papers.summary: We analyze the first IXPE observation of the Crab Nebula using a polarization-resolved deconvolution method based on maximum a posteriori (MAP) estimation. The method reconstructs the polarization-resolved intensity map as a three-dimensional distribution in sky-position and polarization-angle spaces, using an instrumental response that depends on the incident direction and polarization angle of X-ray photons. We apply the method to the IXPE data in the 2-8~keV band and compare the result with that obtained using the basic analysis. Our result shows sharper spatial structure, making the jet shape more clearly identifiable than that in the basic analysis. The reconstructed image shows a statistically significant tendency for the magnetic-field orientation to be perpendicular to the intensity-gradient orientation in the jet region. Although these results are obtained by using a simplified response where systematic uncertainty remains, they demonstrate that our MAP-based deconvolution can improve the interpretability of IXPE polarization maps for nebular sources.

papers.title: Angular Momentum Transport across Accretion States around a rapidly spinning black hole
papers.summary: Accretion requires the outward transport of angular momentum, but the relative contributions of matter advection, turbulent stresses, ordered magnetic fields, winds, and black-hole spin remain uncertain in strongly magnetized flows. We use high-resolution three-dimensional GRMHD simulations around a rapidly rotating black hole ($a=0.998$) to compare SANE, intermediate-flux, and magnetically arrested disk states. In SANE and intermediate states, outward stresses are insufficient to overcome inward angular-momentum advection, and the net flux remains inward. In MAD, ordered Maxwell stresses regulate the disk and drive winds, while the Blandford-Znajek jet carries a distinct, near-constant flux extracted from the black hole, making the total angular-momentum flux outward. Magnetic-flux eruptions modulate both channels. During an eruption, an equatorial current sheet extends beyond the ergosphere, and low-density, magnetically dominated bubbles of expelled flux enter the polar region. The jet becomes asymmetric, its tilt more than doubles, and its opening angle first widens and then contracts below its pre-eruption value. Eruptions suppress the horizon accretion rate and briefly reverse the angular-momentum flux through the jet surface, while reorganizing the Maxwell stresses in the disk. As horizon-threading flux re-accumulates, the turbulent stress recovers toward its saturated MAD level. Eruption durations and lags among horizon flux, accretion rate, and jet tilt of ~40-90 $r_g/c$ correspond to milliseconds for stellar-mass black holes and tens of minutes for Sgr A*. These results distinguish disk-regulating magnetic torques from black-hole-sourced jet transport and show how flux eruptions couple disk accretion, winds, and jet morphology.

papers.title: The Agentic Observer Hackathon: Autonomous Decision-making in Simulated Astronomical Surveys
papers.summary: Astronomical surveys must allocate observing time while responding to changing conditions and competing scientific priorities. We present the Agentic Observer Hackathon (AOH), a community challenge for studying autonomous survey operations. Within a synthetic multi-object survey with prescribed exposure responses and assignment constraints, decision systems select pointings, assign targets and choose exposure configurations while responding to observing requests, instrumental faults and data loss. We evaluate systems submitted by 102 teams on campaigns reserved for evaluation and analyse target completion in a reference campaign. The leading systems combine numerical exposure planning with language models for interpreting operational information and supporting longer-term decisions. Exploratory tests show improved fault reporting with model access in several systems, while revised scientific priorities produce substantial changes in ranking. The reference campaign traces target completion and diagnoses errors in the baseline's inference of prescribed quality bands. The released simulator and reference strategies provide common survey conditions for comparing exposure allocation, target selection and recovery from interruptions.

papers.title: Effects of Competing Reactions on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ on Abundance Distributions in Type I X-Ray Bursts
papers.summary: The composition of X-ray burst ashes affects the thermal transport properties of the neutron star crust, as well as heating and cooling through weak interaction processes. Reaction-rate uncertainties can produce secondary peaks separated from the main peak in final abundance distributions. Using STARLIB reaction rates and their temperature-dependent uncertainties in the K04 one-zone post-processing model, we combine four sets of Monte Carlo calculations with XGBoost classification, SHAP analysis, and reaction-flow analysis to investigate the origins of these secondary peaks. We find that the competing $(p,\alpha)$ and $(p,\gamma)$ reaction pairs on $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ and $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ are primarily responsible for secondary peaks outside the central 68\% confidence interval in all 44 isotopes examined. Fixing both pairs at their median rates reduces the fractions of samples in the secondary-peak regions by 96\%--100\%, while the bounds of the central 68\% interval remain largely unchanged for most mass numbers. The $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}$ pair has the larger effect. Enhanced recycling limits the supply of material to heavier isotopes and accelerates proton consumption, while earlier proton exhaustion further suppresses subsequent proton captures. These changes alter the balance between isotope production and destruction, leading to high- or low-abundance secondary peaks over a broad mass range beyond the Ni--Cu and Zn--Ga cycles. These results identify $^{59}\mathrm{Cu}(p,\gamma)^{60}\mathrm{Zn}$ and the two competing channels on $^{63}\mathrm{Ga}$ as priorities for further nuclear-physics constraints to improve XRB abundance predictions.

papers.title: Tracking the evolution of sub-Neptunes. II. The radius valley on gyrochronological ages
papers.summary: The radius valley separating super-Earths from sub-Neptunes is understood as a signature of atmospheric mass loss, but the timescale over which it develops remains poorly constrained. We investigate the age evolution of the radius valley and the super-Earth population around FGK stars using gyrochronological ages. We select $746$ planets around $510$ FGK hosts with reliable gyrochronological ages between $0.1$ and $4$ Gyr. A subset of $581$ planets around $404$ hosts, for which detection and confirmation completeness can be characterised, forms the reference sample. We measure the valley morphology and its locus in the period-radius plane, and infer the intrinsic super-Earth fraction with a selection-conditioned mixture model that accounts for stellar-age uncertainties. The intrinsic super-Earth fraction increases primarily during the first $\sim2$ Gyr, with no significant subsequent evolution. An exponential approach-to-plateau model places $90\%$ of this increase within $1.9$ Gyr at $90\%$ credibility. The radius valley is consistently resolved from $\sim1.5$ Gyr onwards, with no significant evolution in its depth or width. Its minimum may shift from $\sim1.5\,R_\oplus$ before $\sim2$ Gyr to $\sim1.8\,R_\oplus$ at older ages, accompanied by a change in the shape of the super-Earth radius distribution, although these changes are only suggestive. This evolution is consistent with atmospheric loss continuing up to approximately $1$-$2$ Gyr for a fraction of planets. The tentative shift of the valley minimum towards larger radii may indicate that planets with more massive cores complete envelope loss later, although the present data do not uniquely distinguish between atmospheric-loss mechanisms.

papers.title: Simulating winds in the Galactic centre. II. Observational biases on HI clouds and a multi-wavelength comparison
papers.summary: High-velocity neutral hydrogen (HI) clouds found up to several kiloparsecs above the Galactic centre (GC) provide some of the most direct evidence for a nuclear wind in the Milky Way, yet the properties inferred for these clouds are influenced by how they are observed. Starting from a magnetohydrodynamical simulation in which supernova feedback drives a multiphase nuclear outflow, we generate mock HI observations matched to the angular resolution and sensitivity of Green Bank Telescope (GBT) surveys of the GC and analyse them in the same way as the real data. We find that observational effects substantially reshape the cloud population: beam smearing makes clouds appear larger, rounder and more diffuse, while noise erases faint clouds and strips low-density gas from the others. These effects combined, together with confusion with foreground disk emission, prevent the detection of more than 80% of the clouds (up to 95% during more quiescent phases), while those detected appear less massive, less turbulent and less elongated, with column densities underestimated by a factor of two; only their velocities are reliably recovered. Once these effects are included, the simulated clouds broadly reproduce the properties and sky distribution of the GBT population, but lack the fastest (> 250 km/s ) and highest-latitude (b > 10{\deg} ) clouds. Mock UV absorption and soft X-ray observations support this picture, with warm-ionized gas column densities at the low end of the observed range and X-ray emission measures too low at b > 10{\deg} . Our results imply that the true GC cloud population is more numerous, massive, turbulent and elongated than observed, and that fully reproducing observations may require a stronger recent starburst or additional feedback.

papers.title: Magnetized Accretion Flows with Low Angular Momentum Around Supermassive Black Holes
papers.summary: We investigate the global structure of slowly rotating accretion flows around black holes in the presence of large-scale magnetic fields. Using a steady, height-integrated transonic model with radial mass loss, we examine how magnetic pressure, tension, and torque modify the dynamics of Bondi-like and disk-like accretion. Adopting a radial magnetic-field prescription based on results from previous numerical simulations, we compare hydrodynamical and magnetized solutions across a range of plasma-$\rm \beta$ values, from weak to strong field regimes. We find that magnetic stresses substantially alter the sonic radius and change the angular momentum and mass accretion rate reaching the black hole. For sufficiently strong fields, the inner flow becomes highly sub-Keplerian and magnetically dominated ($ \beta= P_{\mathrm{gas}}/ P_{\mathrm{mag}}<1$), and magnetic stresses can drive transitions to lower angular momentum. We also show that outflows in this magnetized accretion flow can significantly alter the structure of disk-like accretion. We further perform 2D simulations of magnetized Bondi accretion and torus accretion and find that the radial structure and magnetically dominated, sub-Keplerian character of our semi-analytical solutions are qualitatively reproduced.
