papers.title: Angle-dependent emission from evolving accretion layers
papers.summary: Photon propagation through an evolving atmosphere can change the angular distribution of emerging radiation even when its integrated optical column remains constant. We quantify this effect in an irradiated, internally heated, expanding plane-parallel layer using grey, special-relativistic similarity solutions. The full angular radiation field determines both the source function and the acceleration of a pressureless flow in prompt radiative balance. We compare each evolving solution with two frozen transport calculations on the same density and velocity profiles, holding the source fixed in one and allowing it to relax in the other. Heating produces the familiar transition from limb darkening to limb brightening, while the temporal correction to the angular contrast changes sign with optical column. For an upper boundary moving at $0.04c$, an injection speed of $0.06c$, and heating four times the reference incident flux, the intensity ratio between direction cosines $0.1$ and $1$ exceeds the frozen, fixed-source result by $18.8$ per cent at column $\tau_0=0.15$, but is smaller by $2.53$ per cent at $\tau_0=0.55$. Source relaxation preserves this reversal. The corresponding direct photon flight times are one third and three per cent of the flow age in the oblique and normal directions, respectively. These solutions provide a controlled local benchmark for temporal angular transfer in evolving disc atmospheres and reprocessing layers; application to a specific accreting system requires thermal, spectral, and geometrical physics beyond the present model.

papers.title: The nucleon is not a hard sphere: screening fifth forces with Skyrmions
papers.summary: Laboratory searches for chameleon and symmetron fifth forces increasingly rely on individual nucleons as sources or probes, but model them as uniform spheres. Motivated by the Skyrme picture, we instead consider a nucleon profile with a constant-density core and an $r^{-6}$ pion tail, together with its exponential truncation at the physical pion mass. We derive analytic screening charges for the uniform sphere and the $r^{-6}$ profile, and extend the comparison to the exponential truncation at the physical pion mass using numerical solutions. Because the outer tail is too dilute to be screened at any coupling strength, the $r^{-6}$ tail produces a power-law enhancement over the sphere charge in strong screening, and the exponential tail has a weaker, logarithmic enhancement. Propagating this difference through the published analyses, nucleon-sourced exclusion regions extend systematically further into the strongly coupled regime. For example, symmetron constraints from neutron interferometry at $\mu=1\,\mathrm{keV}$ reach maximal self-couplings about $1.4$ orders of magnitude higher than for a uniform-sphere neutron ($3.0$ orders of magnitude in the chiral limit),and at the dark-energy scale the hydrogen $1s$--$2s$ chameleon bound reaches couplings $1.8$ orders of magnitude weaker than for a uniform-sphere proton ($2.4$ in the chiral limit), overtaking the muonium bound.

papers.title: Thirty years of primordial deuterium abundances: A provenance-aware statistical reanalysis
papers.summary: (ABRIDGED:) Primordial deuterium provides one of the most precise observational tests of Big Bang nucleosynthesis, yet the published literature is built on a comparatively small number of high-redshift absorption systems. We construct a provenance-aware database of 957 published primordial-D/H values from 247 publications spanning 1994--2026 and trace observational entries, wherever possible, to their underlying physical absorbers. Of the 795 observational entries, 80.1 percent represent reused individual or compilation values; only 11.4 percent correspond to new determinations of individual absorption systems. Although 52 distinct absorbers are identified overall, the eight most frequently represented systems account for 62.0 percent of all identifiable absorber mentions. An inverse Herfindahl--Hirschman measure applied to our full database gives an effective representation equivalent to only 16.28 equally represented absorbers, demonstrating that the published literature is strongly concentrated around a much smaller effective subset. Despite this strong internal dependence, the modern consensus value of $10^5({\rm D/H})\simeq2.5$ is robust to alternative absorber-level treatments and survives removal of the eight dominant systems. However, the apparent precision of literature-level compilations is more sensitive to repeated representation than a simple count of published values implies. We also identify a synchronised transition in the compilation literature around 2013--2014, associated with increasingly selective and homogeneous analyses while older individual values continued to circulate. The modern D/H consensus is therefore robust in central value, but the underlying literature is less statistically independent than its publication density suggests. This thus highlights the importance of provenance-aware analysis in precision cosmology.

papers.title: Harmonic Angular Mapping Method for Binary Microlensing Grid Search
papers.summary: Searching for binary-lens microlensing solutions is computationally demanding because of the complex parameter space and the large number of trial models required. We present an algorithm that accelerates binary-lens grid searches by expanding the angular dependence of precomputed magnification maps in Fourier modes. By contracting the observation-dependent weighted sums in Fourier space, the $\chi^2$ values for all trial source-trajectory angles can be evaluated efficiently using inverse fast Fourier transforms (FFTs), avoiding repeated calculations over individual observations. We tested the method on 200 Roman-like synthetic binary-lens events. For 166 events (83%), the recovered fits agreed with Levenberg--Marquardt fits initialized at the injected parameters to within $|\Delta\chi^2|\leq1$. The FFT map scan required an average of 5.05~min per event. For the same discrete search volume, the Fourier angular evaluation was estimated to be approximately 900 times faster than conventional magnification-map sampling. These results demonstrate that the method can efficiently identify useful initial conditions for binary-lens light-curve modeling.

papers.title: A Century-Long Archival Search and Analysis of the Rubin Observatory-Discovered Dwarf Planet Candidate 2026 ED$_{138}$
papers.summary: The trans-Neptunian object (TNO) 2026 ED$_{138}$ was discovered in early data from the NSF-DOE Vera C. Rubin Observatory, and recovered in Dark Energy Camera images back to 2016. With an absolute magnitude of $H_V = 3.11 \pm 0.05$ mag, it is one of the largest known TNOs, with a diameter of 635-1590 km for geometric albedos between 0.25 and 0.04. Its position far to the south and close to the galactic plane kept it hidden in images that recorded it for decades. Here, we present archival observations of 2026 ED$_{138}$ spanning 89 years: twelve photographic plates taken between 1954 and 2000, a marginal detection on a 1937 Harvard plate, 2010-2017 VISTA near-infrared images, 2016-2020 SkyMapper images, and ten years of ATLAS photometry. The archival positions improve the long-term ephemeris fivefold, and we predict 15 occultations of $G \leq 16.5$ mag stars in 2027-2030, six of which will occur over populated land. The line of sight from Earth has turned by $\sim87^\circ$ since 1954, yet the plate magnitudes remain consistent with the present-day phase curve. Fitted plate by plate, they exclude oblate shapes with $c/a \leq 0.6$ for at least half of all spin-axis orientations and, with a present-day light curve amplitude below $\sim0.11-0.15$ mag, a Haumea-like Jacobi ellipsoid for $\sim90\%$ of them. We find a tentative 10.4 h light curve period ($\sim20.7$ h if double-peaked). Near-infrared colors place 2026 ED$_{138}$ in the BR (intermediate red) taxonomic class, with $J-H = 0.60\pm0.15$, redder than Haumea and without evidence of similar 1.5 $\mu$m water-ice absorption, supporting the conclusion that it is not a Haumea-family member. $z$-band photometry also limits Eris-like methane to $\lesssim25\%$ of the surface. Integrations over $\pm1$ Gyr show it sticks to the 12:7 resonance with Neptune for tens of megayears at a time, but it rarely remains permanently captured.

papers.title: A Massive and Eccentric Binary Millisecond Pulsar in the Globular Cluster M10
papers.summary: We present the timing solution of the millisecond pulsar PSR J1657-0406A in the globular cluster M10, based on observations performed with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST). The timing results show that PSR J1657-0406A is in a long-period ($P_b \sim 37$ days) and eccentric ($e \sim 0.12$) orbit. We also measured the periastron advance $\dot{\omega} = 0.00090(13)$ degrees per year, which implies a total system mass of $2.5(6)$ solar masses, assuming that general relativity accurately models the orbital motion. No optical counterpart was detected within the positional uncertainty, indicating that the companion is unlikely to be a main-sequence star. Considering possible formation channels for the orbital eccentricity, we favor a helium white dwarf companion, although a massive white dwarf or neutron star cannot be completely excluded.

papers.title: Chemical abundances of a Galactic Centre ejecta discovered in DESI
papers.summary: Chemical abundances in the Galactic Centre (GC) are challenging to measure because of high extinction, crowding, and distance, and are typically limited to the brightest AGB and M giants observed in the near-infrared. In contrast, hypervelocity stars (HVSs) ejected from the GC by Sgr A* carry their natal composition into accessible regions such as the Milky Way halo, making them unique probes of GC chemistry. We present high-resolution optical Magellan/MIKE spectroscopy of DESI-312, a bound HVS candidate in the halo with super-solar metallicity ($[\mathrm{Fe/H}]=0.2\pm0.1$). This sets it apart from accreted halo populations on radial orbits and is most naturally explained by GC formation and Hills-mechanism ejection. Updated isochrone fits give an age of 7.4-11.3 Gyr; together with its metallicity and kinematics, this strengthens the case for a GC origin. Korg and Turbospectrum spectral synthesis yields $[\mathrm{X/Fe}]$ for 22 elements, plus Li from an independent line-by-line NLTE analysis. As DESI-312 is near the main sequence, its C, N, and O abundances are unaltered by dredge-up; to our knowledge, these are the first such measurements of unevolved GC material. Its abundance pattern lies where the nuclear star cluster (NSC), nuclear stellar disc (NSD), and inner-bulge sequences overlap, with a Na enhancement ($[\mathrm{Na/Fe}]=+0.16^{+0.03}_{-0.04}$) more modest than in NSC giants of similar metallicity. Chemistry alone thus cannot identify its progenitor; we nevertheless favour the NSC, given its large reservoir of old, metal-rich stars and the star's kinematics. Alongside WINERED-HVS1 and the S-star S0-6/S10, whose abundances point to different progenitors, this tentatively suggests multiple progenitor populations for the S-star cluster. DESI-312 is a test case for sampling GC chemistry with ejected dwarfs at optical wavelengths, complementing near-infrared studies of giants.

papers.title: A magnetically heated slim disc-corona model for tidal disruption events
papers.summary: Tidal disruption events (TDEs) can reach super-Eddington luminosities near their peak. While their optical/UV emission may arise from multiple processes, X-rays are more likely to be produced by the innermost accretion flow close to the black hole, analogous to super-Eddington flows in stellar-mass X-ray binaries (XRBs) and active galactic nuclei (AGNs). Super-Eddington AGNs typically show disc-dominated spectra, with weak and steep coronae, while super-Eddington XRBs show a wider variety of spectral shapes. Here we explore disc-corona coupling in TDEs by developing a super-Eddington ($\dot{m}>1$: slim) disc model in which magnetic reconnection transfers some of the accretion power from the disc into a hot Comptonizing corona. We test the model on the well-monitored X-ray TDE AT2021ehb, and can broadly fit the brightest X-ray spectra with a black-hole mass $M_{\rm BH}\sim10^6$--$10^7\,M_\odot$ at $\dot m\sim 1$, but need variable magnetic coupling to the disc to match the large observed fast changes in coronal contribution. AGN at similarly high luminosity do not show such variable coronae, but the transient XRB outbursts do, suggesting that it may be a common feature of rapidly changing, non-steady accretion flows. As the TDE declines to $\dot{m}\sim 0.01$, the source hardens, but never goes below $\Gamma\sim 2$, unlike both AGN and XRB at these luminosities. Thus the X-ray spectral evolution in this TDE does not resemble either XRB or AGN in detail, likely pointing to the very different, highly variable nature of the accretion flow in a tidal disruption event.

papers.title: An all-sky catalogue of Be transition stars from WISE and Gaia
papers.summary: We present an all-sky catalogue of classical Be stars undergoing transitions between quiescent B-type and active Be-star phases, based on Gaia DR3 astrometry and multi-epoch mid-infrared photometry from WISE and NEOWISE-R. From a Gaia-selected parent sample of 4.2 million candidate OBA stars, we identify Be transition stars through correlated variability in $W_1$ magnitude and $W_1-W_2$ colour, which traces circumstellar disk formation and dissipation. The final catalogue contains 3,300 Be transition stars, including 2,743 newly identified objects, and provides a large, homogeneous sample for studying Be outburst activity across the sky. The median durations of the measured outburst and decay phases are 459 and 478 days, respectively, consistent with previous WISE-based measurements and compatible with the long disk-evolution timescales expected in the viscous decretion disk framework. As an initial application, we use TESS photometry for 3,017 targets to identify 63 eclipsing binary systems hosting Be transition stars, including 33 Algol-type, 17 Beta Lyrae-type, and 13 W Ursae Majoris-type systems. Among the multi-epoch LAMOST spectra, two sources show candidate radial-velocity shifts exceeding 20 km s $^{-1}$; their line-profile behaviour suggests that RV variability in active Be transition stars may be influenced by outburst-related line-profile changes rather than being an unambiguous indicator of binary motion. This catalogue provides a basis for future statistical studies of Be outbursts, disk evolution, and their connection with binarity and spectroscopic variability.

papers.title: Solar Ephemeral Regions Hales and Joys laws
papers.summary: Besides the active regions and sunspots, the Sun produces many bipolar structures such as ephemeral regions,ERs, and even smaller magnetic bipoles. In this study, we investigate the smallest end of bipolar magnetic structures on the Sun, focusing on ERs using Helioseismic and Magnetic Imager full disk LOS magnetograms. We identify and track the emergence decay sequences of ERs to quantify their flux and morphological properties. Consistent with previous studies, we find that the flux distribution follows a log normal profile and the total unsigned flux emergence rate is estimated to be around 1.45 10^22 Mx/day. We find the ERs are almost uniformly distributed on the solar disc with a substantial fraction emerging outside the activity belts. A statistical analysis of ERs tilt angle reveals a weak adherence to Hales polarity law. The mixed signatures suggest that a majority of the ERs are associated with the large scale global dynamo, while the remainder most likely originate from the small scale dynamo. Overall, our findings indicate that even the small bipolar magnetic structures are statistically imprinted by the solar global dynamo. Our results bridge the scale between ERs and active regions, providing valuable constraints on how magnetic flux is structured and emerges across various spatial and temporal scales on the Sun.

papers.title: Planet-gap-induced ice lines form observable dust rings in protoplanetary disks
papers.summary: Whether volatile ice lines can produce dust rings in protoplanetary disks remains debated. Previous modelling and observational studies place ice lines using smooth, monotonic disk temperature profiles. However, in substructured disks, the midplane temperature need not be smooth: a deep, planetary gap can locally heat, shift and multiply the ice-line locations. We adopt the non-smooth temperature profile of a hot planetary gap and use dust-evolution simulations to study how CO$_2$ ice lines, which imprint radial jumps in the fragmentation velocity $V_{\rm frag}$, affect dust evolution over 10 Myr and the observational signatures. For comparison, we also run models with uniform low ($V_{\rm frag}=1$ m/s) and high ($V_{\rm frag}=10$ m/s) fragmentation velocities. In the varying-$V_{\rm frag}$ model, dust piles up with enhanced grain sizes at the two CO$_2$ ice lines along the gap edges, appearing as clear double rings in dust observations at 13 $\mu$m that persist over 10 Myr; at 1.3 mm, it shows only a modest ring-to-gap contrast of a factor of a few, consistent with the shallow, low-contrast rings in ALMA surveys. The uniform $V_{\rm frag}=10$ m/s model instead forms a single high-contrast ring at the pressure bump and suppresses the inward pebble flux to the inner disk by up to two orders of magnitude, whereas the uniform $V_{\rm frag}=1$ m/s model produces only weak substructure and strong outer-disk depletion. We propose a multi-wavelength test to distinguish these scenarios: ice-line rings stay at fixed radii from scattered light to the millimetre observation, whereas a pressure-bump trap produces a single dominant ring whose peak shifts inward at shorter wavelengths.

papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Signal from a Short GRB Relativistic MHD Jet
papers.summary: We analyze the gravitational-wave (GW) signal produced by a relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) simulation of a short GRB jet with parameters corresponding to those of GRB 170817A. The signal that is generated in the hidden central engine of the GRBs is computed by direct integration of the retarded solution of the linearized Einstein equations of an MHD simulation. Separating the GW signal into its baryonic and electromagnetic contributions, we identify the physical origin of its dominant features. The waveform is of the memory type, with $h(f) \propto 1/f$ at low frequencies and a knee at $\sim 0.5-0.5$Hz set by the energy injection time, which corresponds to the GRB duration. A pronounced early peak reflects the opening of the magnetic field lines and the equatorial kick given to the ejecta at the onset of the jet, demonstrating that the GW signal can reveal processes deep in the GRB engine that cannot be observed otherwise. The signal is strongest for observers far from the jet axis. The total radiated GW energy is only $\sim 10^{42}$ erg, about $10^{-9}$ of the jet energy; it scales as ${\cal E}^2/\tau$ with the shortest variability time $\tau$, so this is a lower limit. Comparing the predicted spectrum with the sensitivity of current and future detectors, we find that events similar to GW170817 are marginally detectable by DECIGO from up to 10 Mpc and by the Einstein Telescope from 1 Mpc. The injected Poynting flux in this simulation was smooth. An engine variable on a millisecond timescale, as predicted in some GRB models, would substantially increase the GW energy and detectability.

papers.title: The Stellar-Mass Dependence of Feedback-Driven Outflows in DESI DR1 Star-Forming Galaxies
papers.summary: Stellar feedback plays a key role in regulating star formation and shaping the evolution of star-forming galaxies. Low-mass galaxies provide one of the most powerful laboratories for testing stellar feedback and its impact on galaxy evolution. Numerical simulations predict that repeated feedback-driven gas inflows and outflows generate a "breathing mode," producing a positive correlation between mass-normalized gas velocity dispersion and recent star formation in dwarf galaxies. Whether this kinematic signature persists at higher stellar masses has remained untested. We investigate this question using $\sim1200$ star-forming galaxies with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) spectroscopy and COSMOS2020 photometry spanning $7.9<\log M_\star/M_\odot<11.5$ within $z<0.25$. Ionized-gas kinematics are measured with pPXF, and recent star formation histories are reconstructed through joint spectrophotometric fitting with Prospector. We confirm the predicted positive correlation throughout the low-mass regime with $\log M_\star/M_\odot \lesssim 9.8$, quantitatively consistent with previous observations and FIRE-2 simulations. Above $\log M_\star/M_\odot \sim 9.8$, the correlation weakens rapidly and becomes consistent with zero, providing the first empirical constraint on the stellar mass scale above which the kinematic signature of feedback-driven outflow cycles becomes negligible. Our results establish a characteristic stellar mass above which stellar feedback no longer dominates galaxy-scale gas kinematics, providing a new observational benchmark for models of feedback-regulated galaxy evolution. Future joint analyses of gas kinematics and stellar structure will test whether this transition is accompanied by the broader galaxy response predicted by the breathing mode scenario.

papers.title: Self-lensing of electromagnetic counterparts to extreme mass ratio inspirals
papers.summary: Extreme mass ratio inspirals on inclined orbits can produce recurrent electromagnetic flares by shocking gas at accretion-disk crossings. Using forward ray tracing in Kerr spacetime, we investigate how self-lensing by the central supermassive black hole (SMBH) reshapes these flares. Flares emitted behind the SMBH can be strongly magnified, whereas near-side flares remain almost unmagnified, producing strong-weak alternation even for identical intrinsic emission. As Lense-Thirring precession shifts the crossing azimuths, it generates long-term amplitude envelopes whose spacing can be used to infer the precession period. Lense-Thirring precession can also increase the cumulative geometric lensing probability over longer observing windows. Within individual flares, Keplerian motion of hotspots co-rotating with the disk produces time-dependent magnification, which can generate shoulders or double peaks and change the effective width. We also propose a spectral diagnostic to distinguish self-lensing from external lensing when their light curves are similar: self-lensing can amplify later, cooler emission and produce a softer secondary peak, whereas delayed images from a static external lens repeat the same intrinsic spectral evolution.

papers.title: See you again: an $80^\circ$ NGC~5466 stellar stream and its constraints on the Galactic dark halo mass
papers.summary: Using \textit{Gaia} Data Release 3 combined with Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument Legacy Imaging Survey Data Release 9 and Panoramic Survey Telescope and Rapid Response System Data Release 2, we apply a modified matched filter method to obtain a weighted stellar map in the surrounding of the globular cluster NGC~5466. Our results support that the tidal stream of NGC~5466 extends around $80^\circ$ on the sky, and the leading tail seemingly exhibits an upward deviation in the range of $180^\circ \lesssim \alpha \lesssim 190^\circ$, which supports previous claim that the Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) may have caused dynamical perturbations to the stream. Based on the 308 highly-weighted member candidates of the NGC~5466 stream, we try to measure the mass distribution of the Milky Way dark matter halo along with the mass of LMC. By comparing the observed stream candidate members to a series of model streams generated under different potential parameters, we obtain the posterior distributions of the parameters: the circular velocity at the solar radius $V_{\rm c} = 239.56^{+1.46}_{-1.44}\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, the density flattening of the halo $q = 1.08^{+0.07}_{-0.07}$, the scale radius of the halo density profile $r_s = 12.97^{+3.02}_{-2.18}\ \mathrm{kpc}$ and the total mass of the LMC $M_{\rm LMC} = 9.63^{+1.89}_{-2.00}\times 10^{10}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$. The enclosed mass of the Milky Way within the stream apocenter radius of $\sim$ 50 kpc is calculated as $M_{\rm MW}(<50~\mathrm{kpc}) = 4.59^{+0.48}_{-0.37} \times 10^{11}$ $\mathrm{M_\odot}$.

papers.title: Mass and angular momentum assessement of the neutron star XTEJ 1807-294 using X-ray triplets
papers.summary: The X-ray power-density spectrum of the accreting millisecond pulsar XTEJ 1807-294 contains several triplets of simultaneously observed quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs): a lower and a upper kHz QPOs and a low-frequency QPO. This fact allows us to assess the mass and the specific angular momentum of the central neutron star. We also apply an error propagation formula to obtain interval estimates of the parameters of the star. The calculations are repeated with several different models for the kHz QPOs. The degree of consistency of the bounds obtained with the different triplets may provide information for the viability of the used models.

papers.title: Hidden by Exponential Screening: The Invisibility of the Dymnikova Black Hole de Sitter Core to Accretion Observables
papers.summary: The Dymnikova spacetime replaces the Schwarzschild singularity with a de Sitter core, and its lapse deviates from Schwarzschild by a factor decaying as $e^{-r^3/(2l_{\rm cr}^2M)}$. Whether this screening renders the core invisible to accretion has remained an open quantitative question. We address it with GRHD simulations of BHL accretion onto Dymnikova BH for six values of the critical length, $0.1M\le l_{\rm cr}\le 1.1M$, the last being 97% of the extremal value. All runs share identical gas parameters and resolution, so any difference in the flow must originate from the geometry. The dynamically relevant quantity is the gravitational acceleration, whose deviation reaches 12% at the inner boundary for the most strongly corrected model, yet the flow responds only locally: the post-shock density drops by 10% in the innermost zone and the quiet-phase accretion rate by 0.12%, with no effect beyond $r\simeq2.7M$. Because runs differing by as little as $\sim 10^{-10}$ in the metric decorrelate completely once the shock-cone instability saturates, we compare models statistically using ensembles of independent realizations. The time-averaged accretion rate is then independent of $l_{\rm cr}$ to within 0.8% $(2\sigma)$ at all radii; the variability amplitude, shock-cone opening angle $(1.077\pm0.003 rad)$, and stagnation radius $(26.8\pm0.3M)$ vary only within the realization scatter; the propagation lags $(75.5\pm1.0M$ and $31.6\pm0.4M)$ agree to within 1.6%; and no power spectrum carries a detectable core signature. Accretion onto a Dymnikova BH is therefore observationally indistinguishable from accretion onto a Schwarzschild black hole: timing observations test the shock-cone mechanism, not the regular core. More broadly, ensemble-based statistical comparisons are essential before differences between simulated accretion flows in different spacetimes can be interpreted as physical.

papers.title: Two Fast Radio Burst Candidates Detected in the RATAN-600 Blind Survey
papers.summary: We report the detection of two single dispersed pulses with widths of about 6.7\,ms and 15.6\,ms and flux densities of about 0.8 and 1.7\,Jy. These were found in a blind survey of two circular regions (Dec$\;=+22^{\circ}$ and $+5^{\circ}$,RA: 0--24~h) at high radio frequencies \mbox{(4400--5000\,MHz)} using four 4-channel filter radiometers (central frequencies of 4475, 4625, 4775, and 4925\,MHz) spanning a total frequency bandwidth of 600\,MHz. The survey was carried out with the Western Sector antenna of the RATAN-600 radio telescope, which had an effective area of 1200\,m$^2$ in~2017--2025. The total area of the survey was about 1500~square degrees, and each pointing of the antenna lasted one year. We consider these to be two rare, high-frequency FRB events (MJD~58614.38257 and MJD~58659.62482), detected with estimated dispersion measures of $200\pm20$ and $266\pm10$\,pc\,cm$^{-3}$ at a final signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) level of 8--9 after additional optimal filtration. After subtraction of the estimated dispersions within the Milky Way, we estimated redshifts of approximately 0.09 and 0.13, respectively, using the traditional equation: ${\rm DM}\,[{\rm pc~cm}^{-3}] = 1000\,z$ for the intergalactic medium. The estimated isotropic energies of the FRBs are equal to $10^{40}$\,erg and $2\times 10^{40}$\,erg, respectively. To effectively detect single pulses, we applied machine learning methods using a neural network trained on synthetic FRB pulse profiles.

papers.title: The colors of protoplanetary disks - Impact of nonspherical dust particles on the polarized and total intensity colors
papers.summary: Dust properties in protoplanetary disks remain poorly understood despite their central role in planet formation. Recent studies based on analyses of scattered-light images and phase functions provide promising insights into dust characterization, but the phase function alone is insufficient to constrain dust properties. Degeneracies between dust remain a major obstacle to linking observations to realistic dust models. We investigate the behavior of the disk color as a function of dust. We used MCFOST to generate synthetic scattered-light images from the visible to the near-infrared, in total and polarized intensity. We considered compact spherical grains using, irregular particles and compact and fractal aggregates using optical properties from the AggScatVIR database. Disk colors were measured from these images. For aggregates larger than the wavelength, monomer size influences color, whereas aggregate size has little effect, especially at low fractal dimensions. Polarized color is more sensitive to dust properties than total intensity color, because it combines the wavelength dependences of scattered intensity and polarization degree. Effective medium theory is reliable only for compact aggregates with small monomers, becoming inaccurate for highly porous aggregates or larger monomers. Effective albedo helps predict disk colors, but radiative transfer is needed to account for multiple scattering. For HD 100546, red optical-to-near-infrared colors exclude compact grains and organic-rich compositions but are consistent with amorphous-carbon aggregates, compact or fractal, containing large monomers. These results show that combining color measurements with polarized scattering phase functions offers a promising way to break degeneracies between dust models. Applying this approach to larger disk samples could better constrain dust properties and evolution.

papers.title: X-ray Variability of Mrk 421 in 2025 January: A Ten-Day XPoSat XSPECT Campaign with Contemporaneous NICER Coverage
papers.summary: We present an X-ray study of the high-synchrotron-peaked blazar Mrk 421 using ten days of XPoSat/XSPECT observations (2025 January 20-29; 202 ks) and contemporaneous NICER data. The 0.8-15 keV light curve has a fractional variability amplitude of 19.6 +/- 0.3 per cent, and Bayesian blocks resolve 26 flux states spanning a factor of 2.3. The best-constrained flare has a fast rise and a slow decay, with e-folding times of about 3 h and 30 h. For typical jet parameters, the X-ray-emitting electrons cool faster than this, suggesting that the decay traces a gradual weakening of their acceleration. The count-rate distribution is best described by two lognormal components, consistent with multiplicative variability. The power spectrum is a red-noise power law with a slope of about 1.7 over timescales of 25 min to 10 d, typical of blazars. XSPECT and NICER count rates are well correlated over eight matched epochs (r = 0.941). We fitted log-parabola models to day-resolved spectra from XSPECT, NICER and both jointly, and to flux-resolved XSPECT spectra. Both show spectral hardening with brightness. In the flux-resolved spectra, the photon index at 1 keV decreases from 2.24 in the faintest state to 1.96 in the brightest, and the synchrotron peak moves from about 0.66 to 1.06 keV, while the curvature ($\beta \approx 0.7$) shows no significant change. Power-law fits to Bayesian blocks show that bright blocks at the same rate can differ in photon index by up to $6.4\sigma$, so count rate alone does not fix the spectral state.

papers.title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
papers.summary: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $\alpha_\parallel$ and $\alpha_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $\Sigma m_\nu$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title: Characterisation Methodology for Persistence and Anti-persistence in IR Detectors for the Euclid and SVOM Space Missions
papers.summary: H2RG and ALFA are the infrared detectors used in the Euclid and SVOM space missions. These types of detectors may be affected by persistence and anti-persistence, phenomena that distort pixel responses after exposure to light due to simultaneous trapping and release of charges within the pixel. These phenomena have shown to cause biases in flux measurements and potentially false detections, among other effects. This article presents a universal methodology for characterising persistence and anti-persistence using differential ramps, Savitzky--Golay filtering, and non-linearity correction. When applied to ground characterisation data, this approach reveals spatial inhomogeneities, environmental dependencies (in particular fluence, flux, temperature and wavelength), and unexpected spectral effects in ALFA. These preliminary results validate the method and pave the way for in-flight correction models capable of meeting the missions' accuracy requirements.

papers.title: An Empirical Temperature Relation for Chemical Abundances in AGN
papers.summary: We present for the very first time the empirical temperature structure of the narrow line region (NLR) clouds of active galactic nuclei (AGNs) based on a sample of [N II] and [O III] auroral line measurements. The scaling of Te([N II]) with Te([O III]), expressed as the t2-t3 relation, is key to deriving accurate chemical abundances, in AGNs and other line-emitting nebulae, particularly when only one auroral line is observed. Here, we provide the first robust empirical description of t2-t3 for AGNs: t2(10^4 K)=1.285*t3(10^4 K)+0.799. We find substantial changes in 12+log(O/H) when compared to other t2-t3 calibrations when using the direct, or Te, method with only the [O III] 4363 auroral line. We find that adopting our t2-t3 most accurately recovers the fully direct method 12+log(O/H). To interpret the physical mechanisms behind the AGN t2-t3, we compare the observed distribution of [N II] 6584/5755 and [O III] 5007/4363 flux ratios to a variety of ionization model predictions. We find evidence for power law density gradients, pressure stratification, and (sometimes significant) contributions from astrophysical shocks driving much of the dispersion on these flux ratios while metal cooling dominates the primary shape of the distribution. With more accurate t2-t3 and 12+log(O/H), the properties of the interstellar medium photoionized by AGN can be better characterized and understood across a wide range of cosmic time and may bring better context for novel observations at z>6 with JWST, with implications for understanding chemical enrichment in the earliest stages of galaxy evolution.

papers.title: Small-Scale Magnetic Fields of Hyades M Dwarfs: Evolution with Age from the Pleiades to Field Stars
papers.summary: Small-scale magnetic fields are derived for 18 M-dwarf stars in the Hyades open cluster through an analysis of Zeeman broadening in magnetically sensitive lines from the APOGEE spectra, resulting in mean magnetic fields ranging from 0.7 to 4.3 kG. Comparison with results for field stars hosting exoplanets and stars in the Pleiades open cluster from our previous works reveals distinct distributions of mean magnetic fields, reflecting differences in stellar age. Pleiades stars exhibit stronger fields ($2965\pm632$ G) and are predominantly in the saturated regime, while the roughly 500 million years older Hyades sample has weaker fields ($1925\pm1028$ G) with a larger dispersion, spanning both saturated and unsaturated regimes. Field stars show substantially weaker fields ($573\pm272$ G) and consistently occupy the unsaturated regime. Using the three samples, we derive the relationship between small-scale magnetic field strength and Rossby number, identifying saturation limits for the Rossby number ($\mathrm{Ro_{SAT}}=0.145$) and mean magnetic field ($\langle\mathrm{B}\rangle_{\rm SAT}=2452$ G). Within the Hyades sample, we find that, at a given age, cooler stars tend to have stronger magnetic fields. This trend is less apparent in the other samples, due to the broader age distribution of the field stars and magnetic saturation among the Pleiades stars. Comparisons with isochrones indicate positive correlations between mean magnetic field strength and both stellar radius inflation and photospheric spot coverage. We also find positive correlations between magnetic field strength and chromospheric and coronal activity, with stronger fields associated with larger H$\alpha$ equivalent width excess and higher X-ray-to-bolometric luminosity ratios.

papers.title: Kinematic analysis of the TNG50 Milky Way and Andromeda analogues
papers.summary: We investigate whether Ogorodnikov-Milne (O-M) parameters can serve as kinematic tracers of spiral structure in four Milky Way- and Andromeda-like disc galaxies from the TNG50-1 simulation at z=0. Stellar particles are analysed in disc-aligned reference frames, with velocities referenced to the mass-weighted mean stellar velocity within one stellar half-mass radius. Local O-M fits on a regular grid yield centroid velocities and the components of the velocity-gradient tensor, characterising local deformation and rotation. We compare their spatial distributions with stellar surface-density and relative overdensity maps and examine the influence of parameter uncertainties. The galaxies exhibit diverse coherent kinematic patterns. Features selected using the generalised Oort constants A, B, and C+K display partial correspondence with stellar overdensities, depending on the galaxy and the adopted centroid-selection criteria. For TNG50-456326, a galaxy-specific selection enables us to fit four logarithmic spiral branches and determine their geometrical parameters. Their morphology suggests two principal arms and two secondary branches. We compare the fitted spirals with stellar- and gas-mass overdensity and radial velocity maps and examine the spatial relationship between the identified stellar structures and the gas distribution. Qualitative similarities to the morphology and kinematic patterns of the Milky Way make TNG50-456326 a promising candidate for further investigation as a kinematic analogue. Our results support the use of local O-M parameters as complementary diagnostics of non-axisymmetric disc structure, while highlighting the need for galaxy-specific selection criteria.

papers.title: Cometary impacts an unlikely pathway towards the origins of life on Earth
papers.summary: An early period of cometary bombardment has long been speculated to provide an important source of prebiotic feedstock molecules, required for the origins of life on Earth. In support of this interpretation, comets boast a rich diversity of volatile organic molecules, with many thought to be limiting for prebiotic chemistry. Modelling studies suggest, however, that a significant proportion of these molecules will be destroyed during hypervelocity impact. Here, we revisit the ability of comets to deliver prebiotic feedstock molecules in the high concentrations required for prebiotic chemistry, leveraging recent advances in cometary impact simulations, comet-atmosphere interactions, and dynamical modelling of short-period comets' origin and evolution. Taken together, the rapid decline in Earth's cometary impact bombardment and the efficient destruction of fragile cometary organics indicate that the successful delivery of prebiotic feedstock molecules was an exceedingly rare event. Our results therefore challenge the long-held assumption that cometary impacts played an important role in the origins of life on Earth.

papers.title: Revealing the dusty shell of the semi-regular variable V CVn
papers.summary: The semi-regular variable (SRV) star V CVn exhibits a highly variable optical linear polarization, yet its position angle (PA) has remained remarkably stable at approximately 100 +/- 20 deg. over several decades. We present a comprehensive multi-technique study of the system covering six pulsation cycles from 2020 to 2025. This campaign includes high-cadence photopolarimetry, spectropolarimetry, and the first interferometric observations of V CVn using the CHARA Array (MIRC-X and MYSTIC) in 2024 and 2025. Our photopolarimetric data reveal a significant increase in polarization, reaching peaks of up to 6% during the 2023-2025 cycles, while the characteristic anticorrelation with brightness and the stability of the PA persisted. The interferometric observations resolve the stellar photosphere but show no evidence of large-scale asymmetric structures, such as a bow shock or isolated scattering arcs, at the scales and sensitivities probed. Based on these results, we exclude previous models based on interstellar medium (ISM) interactions or static reflection clouds as the primary drivers of the observed polarization. Instead, we propose a circumstellar disk or flattened envelope, analogous to the L2 Puppis system, as the most plausible explanation. We hypothesize that this stable geometry may be shaped or maintained by the star's high proper motion, where ram pressure from the ISM interaction favors a flattened distribution of circumstellar material. Within this stable framework, the polarization peaks are interpreted as the result of stochastic dust clumps, likely triggered by the star's long secondary period (LSP), which causes episodic increases in mass loss. This combination of an ISM-influenced disk geometry and transient, LSP-driven dust clumps naturally accounts for both the decadal stability of the position angle and the highly variable polarization amplitude of V CVn.

papers.title: Evidence of flare and coronal mass ejection-driven shock acceleration of relativistic protons on 21 November 2024
papers.summary: On 21 November 2024 at 17:55 UTC, a solar flare erupted from far-side active region (AR) 13892, with enhanced hard X-ray flux measured by Solar Orbiter (SO). It was associated with a coronal mass ejection (CME) travelling at 1436 km/s along the limb. This event produced a strong and widespread solar energetic particle (SEP) event at Earth, STEREO-A and SO, with proton energies exceeding 100 MeV. We investigate the relativistic particle acceleration during this event, focusing on separating flare- and shock-related contributions and linking spectral evolution to the CME-driven shock properties. We combine multi-spacecraft energetic-particle observations with velocity dispersion analysis (VDA), three-dimensional CME-driven shock reconstruction, and magnetic connectivity modelling. Radio observations and SEP composition provided independent diagnostics of shock- and flare-associated particle acceleration, respectively. VDA yields solar release times (SRTs) consistent with an early flare-accelerated particle population at all three observers, despite their broad range of helio-longitudes. At STEREO-A, the early release is followed immediately by magnetic connection to an efficient CME-driven shock. A 3D reconstruction of the type II radio burst location confirms a connection between Earth and an efficient shock-acceleration region several minutes later. Within the adopted models, the SO release precedes magnetic connection to the reconstructed front, disfavouring acceleration at the connected shock as the source of the earliest particles. Despite this diversity, STEREO-A and SO show similar spectral evolution, while the near-Earth spectrum extends to relativistic energies and exhibits a high-energy rollover. SEP abundances also show signatures of flare-related acceleration at all three observers. The analysis suggests multiple acceleration processes acting non-uniformly across observers.

papers.title: J-PAS: Exploring the connection between local environment and the triggering of bursty star formation in Extreme Emission Line Galaxies
papers.summary: [Abridged]Extreme Emission Line Galaxies (EELGs) are compact, low-mass systems undergoing intense bursts of star formation, whose physical conditions resemble those of galaxies in the early Universe. We characterise the local environment of EELGs identified in the J-PAS survey to determine whether their extreme properties are associated with the presence of nearby companions, as expected if galaxy-galaxy interactions were the main trigger of the burst. We analyse 917 EELGs from the J-PAS internal data release at $0.03 \lesssim z \lesssim 0.9$ over $\sim$30 deg$^2$. We use the Pair Probability Function formalism, based on the full photometric redshift probability distributions, to identify companions within projected separations up to 200 kpc and velocity differences up to 500 km s$^{-1}$. Stellar masses, star formation rates, dust attenuation, and metallicity estimates were derived for the EELGs and their companions through SED fitting with CIGALE, and Monte Carlo simulations were used to correct for projection and completeness effects. The average pair fraction of the EELGs is $f_\mathrm{pair} = 0.162^{+0.048}_{-0.033}$, indicating that only $\sim$16% of the sample has detectable companions, a value lower than the observed average for other star-forming galaxies within the adopted limits. When detected within the sensitivity and stellar-mass completeness limits of J-PAS, companions tend to be more massive and to show higher SED-based metallicity estimates than the EELGs, suggesting that the latter are typically the low-mass components of asymmetric pairs. However, lower-mass companions below these limits may remain undetected. No statistically significant correlation is found between the equivalent widths of the [OIII]$\lambda$5007, H$\beta$, and H$\alpha$ emission lines and the projected separation to the detected companions within the J-PAS limits.

papers.title: Decomposition of disk and jet optical emission: Case of PKS~1510-089 and PKS~0736+017
papers.summary: Measuring BLR size and black hole mass of jetted quasars with strong radio emission is challenging due to the contribution from non-thermal synchrotron radiation from the jet in the optical continuum. Here, we investigate the optical continuum emission in two flat-spectrum radio quasars (FSRQs), PKS~0736+017 and PKS~1510-089, by separating the thermal emission from the accretion disk and the non-thermal synchrotron emission from the jet using their distinct polarization signatures. Our analysis combines multi-epoch optical spectro-photometric and polarimetric observations from the archival optical continuum, H$\beta$ emission line light curves from earlier reverberation mapping campaigns, and 37 GHz radio data. For PKS~0736+017, we find that the disk contributes approximately 70 % ($f_d = 0.70^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$) of the total optical emission. After removing the jet component, we obtain a revised H$\beta$ lag of $84.8^{+23.2}_{-18.4}$ days. In contrast, the disk contribution in PKS~1510-089 is lower with 37.5 % ($f_d = 0.37^{+0.01}_{-0.01}$), with a corresponding H$\beta$ lag of $54.4^{+4.4}_{-5.4}$ days. Our findings highlight the need for careful decomposition of optical light curves in jet-dominated AGN.

papers.title: Are habitable-zone TESS Objects of Interest really there? Period resolution from the full archive
papers.summary: TESS Objects of Interest (TOIs) seen as single or duo transits carry a catalogue period that is undefined or equal to the separation of the two events, and their insolation and any habitable-zone label inherit it. We reanalyse all 187 TOIs catalogued with P = 0 or P >= 200 d using all public TESS data through Sector 107, with a flux-based method that weights each alias by per-epoch transit likelihoods, the transit duration and a geometric prior, and tests for coherence, data edges, contamination by other planets and instrumental artefacts. It recovers 12 published periods blindly and, in injection-recovery tests, 71 per cent of periods constrained by a new transit, with no wrong period. It resolves 28 periods and fixes 8 more by exclusion. Are habitable-zone TOIs really there? Mostly not: of the 28 duo-transits that a catalogue-period criterion places in the conservative habitable zone, about two are expected to lie there, both giants, and none of the 12 planet-sized ones; those resolved are aliases of hotter planets. Conversely, habitable-zone planets hide behind missing or wrong periods: we recover three published M-dwarf examples and validate four planets with new periods, including TOI-2298 b, a 3.0 Earth-radius sub-Neptune at 146.58 d in the conservative habitable zone of a K dwarf, and TOI-6075 b, a 1.7 Earth-radius planet at 416.5 d (833 d not excluded), the second validated transiting planet smaller than 2 Earth radii with P > 1 yr. We release alias-marginalised habitable-zone probabilities for the whole sample.

papers.title: What can strong lensing recover in edge-on disc galaxies? A mock study based on TNG50 simulations
papers.summary: Strong gravitational lensing tightly constrains the projected mass within the Einstein aperture, but what else imaging alone can recover for edge-on disc lenses remains untested against known truth. We construct HST/ACS-like mock observations of 35 edge-on TNG50 disc galaxies selected to resemble lenses from the Sloan WFC Edge-on Late-type Lens Survey (SWELLS), and fit them with a five-stage Source-Light-and-Mass workflow in PyAutoLens; the final model represents the lens mass distribution by scaling the Multi-Gaussian Expansion (MGE) foreground-light template with a global mass-to-light ratio and adding a spherical NFW halo. Decomposed fits succeed for 21 of the 35 systems; in the other 14, coherent MGE lens-light residuals prevent reliable modelling. For the successful subset, the Einstein radius and the total aperture mass are recovered with normalised median absolute deviation (NMAD) scatters of 0.3% and 0.7%. The global projected mass-weighted slope has an NMAD scatter of 10.3%, smaller than that of the mass-sheet-invariant reduced deflection curvature $\xi$ (11.4%) and well below that of the local slope (40.7%), while the stellar and dark-matter aperture masses scatter by 15.1% and 108.8%. A 35-system true-light diagnostic using the exact input light gives component-mass scatters of 0.8% and 6.3%. Under these controlled assumptions, imaging constrains Einstein-scale total mass and global radial structure more reliably than local radial structure or the stellar-dark-matter decomposition.

papers.title: GALACTIC CENTERS AS TRACERS OF GALAXY EVOLUTION: Zooming from galaxy large-scale properties into their central massive black holes
papers.summary: During the workshop ''Galactic Centers as tracers of galaxy evolution'' (Lorentz Center, Leiden), we reviewed one of the most debated questions in the field of galaxy evolution: the connection between galactic central regions and the evolution of galaxies at a global scale. We gathered different research communities to reveal the connection channels between central massive black holes (MBHs), nuclear structures, and evolutionary processes at a global scale, such as gas inflows and outflows and galaxy-galaxy interactions. Special focus was dedicated to MBH seeding, formation and growth, active galactic nuclei feedback, and the formation of nuclear stellar structures, without missing a global perspective. Participants from these different fields introduced us to the state of the art in numerical simulations, as well as cutting-edge observational techniques. In addition to achieving a deep understanding of these topics, we set up plans to exploit future facilities such as the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT). In this paper, we briefly summarize the highlights of the workshop, identify the open questions that emerged during the workshop discussions, and discuss what observations and simulations will be needed to address them.

papers.title: Molecular gas in the disks and tails of ram pressure stripped Coma galaxies
papers.summary: We present new IRAM 30 m observations of CO(1-0) and CO(2-1) emission in five Coma cluster galaxies undergoing ram pressure stripping. Molecular gas is detected in four galaxies, and CO emission is clearly detected in the stripped tails of three, extending up to $\sim50$ kpc from the stellar disks. The molecular gas masses in the tails range from a few $\times10^8\,M_\odot$ and account for up to 10-20% of the molecular gas remaining in the parent disks. Compared with field scaling relations, several galaxies exhibit elevated molecular-to-stellar gas ratios despite being H I deficient. This enhancement persists toward the lower-mass end of our sample, even in the massive Coma cluster environment, consistent with ram-pressure-induced compression of atomic gas and enhanced H I-to-H$_2$ conversion in the disks. At the same time, the total gas fractions of most galaxies remain close to those of field galaxies with similar stellar masses when the molecular gas in the tails is included, indicating that gas removal and phase transformation act simultaneously. We further investigate the relation between molecular and ionized gas by comparing CO and H$\alpha$ emission in the stripped regions. Although CO is preferentially detected in H$\alpha$-bright regions, the increased scatter compared with previous studies suggests the presence of both star-forming and diffuse CO components in the tails. Our results highlight the dual role of ram pressure stripping in dense environments: it efficiently removes gas from galaxies while also promoting molecular gas formation in both the disks and stripped material, thereby shaping short-term star formation in cluster galaxies.

papers.title: Statistical Modeling of Foreground Galactic Cirrus for Diffuse Halo Light Measurement
papers.summary: Galactic cirrus, the diffuse Milky Way starlight scattered by interstellar dust, has become a major source of systematic uncertainty in measurements of extragalactic diffuse emission at ultra-low surface brightness levels. Proper modeling and correction of this foreground is crucial to unlock the full potential of next-generation deep imaging surveys for studies of faint diffuse emission such as galactic stellar halos, ultra-diffuse galaxies, and intracluster light (ICL). We develop a statistical approach to reconstruct the 2D distribution of the Galactic cirrus while preserving the underlying diffuse extragalactic emission from stellar halos. We combine the broad dust morphology traced by far-infrared emission with multiscale structural information extracted from the optical images. The method synthesizes plausible cirrus structures through iteratively refining the foreground, the smooth diffuse light model, and the residual sky. The performance is assessed through injection--recovery experiments using Euclid VIS observations of the Abell 2390 cluster, which show substantial improvements in recovered stellar halo photometry, although residual biases depend on the local foreground structure and sky estimation. We apply the method to the central Abell 2390 field to correct for a prominent cirrus complex near its brightest cluster galaxy (BCG), revealing a smoother BCG+ICL distribution with a steeper outer light profile and reduced contamination in the integrated light. Our results demonstrate the potential of statistical modeling of Galactic cirrus to improve diffuse light photometry in deep wide-field imaging surveys.

papers.title: A Cepheid-based Distance to the Type 1 Seyfert NGC 3783
papers.summary: We present a Cepheid-based distance to the Type 1 Seyfert NGC 3783 using the Hubble Space Telescope. Images were obtained over 15 visits using nonredundant time spacing, with ten observations in the F350LP filter and eight observations each in the F555W and F814W filters. We found 1541 unique point sources across all observations, and we fit Cepheid templates to analyze these light curves. From these data, we determined a full sample of seven Cepheid candidates. Of these seven candidates, four are the most convincing and comprise our "strong" sample of Cepheid candidates. We fit the period$-$luminosity relationship to the total sample and to our "strong" sample using the LMC calibration by Riess et al. (2019). Adopting an independent distance constraint to the LMC given by Pietrzynski et al. (2019), and correcting for the potential effects of metallicity, we determine a distance modulus of $\mu = 33.118 \pm 0.154$ mag using our strong sample. This value is formally consistent with the value derived using our full sample and corresponds to a distance of $D = 42.03 \pm 2.98$ Mpc. NGC 3783 is therefore among the farthest galaxies with a Cepheid-based distance measurement.

papers.title: SHAPE: Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions A machine learning approach to solar flare forecasting
papers.summary: Solar flares are the most energetic impulsive events in the solar system, and reliable operational forecasting of the rarest and most destructive M- and X-class events remains an open problem. We present Solar Heliospherical Analysis and Prediction of Eruptions (SHAPE), a two-phase deep-learning pipeline that bypasses sunspot proxies in favour of direct soft X-ray observations from the GOES X-ray Sensor (XRS). Phase 1 forecasts monthly flare counts, aggregated to annual totals, with a hybrid model: a cycle-shape curve anchored to published solar-cycle minima fixes the timing and mean profile, and a compact gated-recurrent-unit network with Monte Carlo dropout models the residual variability. Trained on the science-quality NOAA GOES Flare Report for 1995--2020 and validated on 2021--2025, it achieves a mean absolute error of 204 flares yr$^{-1}$, although it underestimates the 2024 solar maximum. Phase 2 forecasts the next day's strongest flare class (C, M or X) with a shared-trunk, dual-head LSTM operating on a 12-day rolling window of five intensity features, with an optional blend against an active-region physics score and a decision threshold tuned to favour recall of M-or-above (M+) events. On a 100-day chronological backtest, the classifier attains a true skill statistic of 0.351, a Heidke skill score of 0.335 for M+ events, a Brier skill score of 0.163 relative to climatology, and an expected calibration error of 0.023. A day-to-day persistence baseline is, however, competitive on both skill scores, showing that much short-term predictability in flare class is autocorrelation rather than learned structure. SHAPE shows that competitive flare forecasting is achievable with compact architectures that retain in minutes on standard hardware, without sunspot proxy inputs.

papers.title: A GeV PWN Candidate in the PSR J1135--6055/G293.8+0.6 Field
papers.summary: We present a \textit{Fermi} Large Area Telescope (LAT) study of PSR~J1135--6055 and the composite supernova remnant (SNR) G293.8+0.6. MeerKAT radio observations reveal a bright central plerion within the faint SNR shell, while Chandra observations detect a compact nebula around the pulsar. Together, these observations establish the presence of a PWN within G293.8+0.6. Our analysis of the 20~GeV--1~TeV LAT data yields a point-like excess with $\mathrm{TS}=26.30$ and photon index $\Gamma=1.63\pm0.33$. Its best-fit position is consistent with the pulsar within the 95\% statistical localization region, and neither the uniform-disk nor Gaussian model is favored, providing no evidence for significant extension. A one-zone leptonic model, together with an independent jet component, reproduces the multiwavelength observations. In this model, the GeV photons are produced mainly by inverse-Compton scattering from relativistic electrons and positrons. Given its positional agreement with the pulsar/PWN and broadband interpretation, we regard the LAT point source as a GeV PWN candidate.

papers.title: White dwarf pollution in wide binaries: the role of planetary mass
papers.summary: Atmospheric pollution in white dwarfs is interpreted as evidence for the accretion of rocky material from remnant planetary systems. In wide binaries, these reservoirs can be influenced by planetary perturbers. Here, we investigate how planetary mass affects the survival and delivery of planetesimals onto an evolving white dwarf. We perform N-body simulations incorporating time-dependent stellar evolution and a stellar companion, varying planetary masses and following the evolution of a planetesimal disc. We find that lower-mass planets perturb the planetesimal reservoir less efficiently, allowing more planetesimals to survive longer. Consequently, delivery onto the white dwarf can persist into the cool white dwarf phase, whereas high-mass planets deplete the reservoir earlier, preventing sustained pollution at late stages. Our results show that planetary mass regulates the timescale over which rocky material remains available for accretion, while the planet's location has minor impact. Pollution is more frequent in binaries with lower inclinations and eccentricities.

papers.title: Stellar wind variability in OB stars and its effect on mass-loss determinations
papers.summary: Virtually all stellar winds of OB stars exhibit variability in one spectral diagnostic or another. This review focuses primarily on UV spectroscopic signatures of this variability and on studies that have exploited it to reveal the presence of large-scale velocity and density structures in the winds. The review includes demonstrations that the physical structures responsible for the variations appear to be large, spatially coherent and rooted in the stellar photospheres. Furthermore, evidence is summarised that these structures can be optically thick to resonance line radiation and are dense enough to modulate the X-ray fluxes that originate in the wind. Also discussed, is how the structures can affect wind line formation and, as a result, the precision by which mass-loss rates can be determined. The potential of millimetre and radio continuum observations to constrain the radial stratification of wind clumping is highlighted, as a future path to reliable empirical determinations of massive star mass-loss rates.

papers.title: Milliarcsecond-scale jet reorientations in GRS 1915+105 pointing towards a warped accretion disc
papers.summary: The black hole X-ray binary GRS 1915+105 was persistently X-ray bright for over 26 years before entering a prolonged low X-ray flux state in 2018, while remaining bright at radio wavelengths. Multi-wavelength observations suggest this state results from a complex layer of absorbing material of unknown nature. Radio jet observations provide an unobstructed view of the physical changes during this phase, and recent Very Large Array and East Asian VLBI Network observations revealed substantial changes in the jet position angle (PA). We use higher-resolution VLBI observations to investigate the connection between the obscuration event and the jet behaviour close to the launch region. We observed GRS 1915+105 with the Very Long Baseline Array and European VLBI Network at four epochs during the early obscuration phase (2019-2021), sampling a diverse range of jet and accretion behaviours. We study the milliarcsecond jet morphology and PA changes and relate these to the reported X-ray behaviour. Many post-2018 PAs are significantly offset from the pre-obscuration jet axis, which has a weighted mean of $142^\circ \pm 7^\circ$ on milliarcsecond scales. We measure a maximum offset of $57^\circ \pm 8^\circ$, the largest reported for GRS 1915+105 to date. Our epochs reveal a variety of jet behaviour, ranging from a stable, compact source with a large PA offset, to a bright, flaring source with a similar offset, to an extended jet with a PA closer to the pre-obscuration axis, and a non-detection. The lack of measurable PA changes within individual 8-hour epochs rules out rapid Lense-Thirring precession of the inner disc as the direct driver of the jet reorientation. Instead, the timescales involved, the system geometry, and the apparent connection to the X-ray obscuration favour a radiation-driven warped accretion disc, a configuration that could naturally explain the persistent obscuration.

papers.title: HCN detection in the Kreutz sungrazing comet C/2026 A1 (MAPS) shortly before its disruption
papers.summary: Context. Kreutz sungrazing comets are characterised by extremely small perihelion distances (q < 3.45 R). These objects are of particular interest because their intense activity and fragmentation can expose material from deeper within the nucleus, providing unique access to their bulk chemical composition rather than merely their surface layers. Aims. The discovery of C/2026 A1 (MAPS) three months before its perihelion offered a rare opportunity to investigate the composition and activity of a Kreutz sungrazing comet. We present the first millimetre wavelength study of this type of comet. Methods. We observed C/2026 A1 (MAPS) with the IRAM 30-m telescope from April 1 to April 3 2026 at heliocentric distances rh = 0.10-0.23 au, the three days preceding its perihelion and full disintegration. We analysed the molecular emissions using non-local thermodynamic equilibrium radiative transfer models to derive molecular production rates. Results. We report the first HCN detection in a Kreutz sungrazer through its (3-2) transition at 265.886 GHz, enabling us to characterise the variability of its activity. We witnessed two outbursts, on April 1 and April 3. The second one, occurring the day before the disintegration of C/2026 A1 (MAPS), led to the release of 0.4% to 1.2% of the total cometary mass, thus suggesting a pre-disruption before entering the Roche limit region. We also obtained upper limits for HNC, CS, H2CO, CO, OCS and CH3OH

papers.title: A Physics Informed Neural Network Approach to Decipher Environmental Confinement of Molecular Clouds in the Third Galactic Quadrant
papers.summary: Recent high-sensitivity and high-resolution surveys of the Third Galactic Quadrant [$219.75 \leq l \leq 229.75$ and $-5.25 \leq b \leq 5.25$], such as the Milky Way Imaging Scroll Painting ( MWISP) survey, have revealed a significant population of molecular clouds (MCs) that appear virially unbound ($\alpha_{vir} > 2$) according to traditional isolated MC models. However, these apparently unstable cloud structures are actually found long-lived and actively undertaking star formation. This inconsistency presents a Virial Paradox. In the present work, we employ a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) to address this discrepancy by re-evaluating the stability of 2,091 MCs . Unlike traditional machine learning, our PINN model embeds the complete Eulerian Virial Theorem including external surface pressure support ($P_{ext}$) directly into the network's loss function. This model autonomously discovers a global Galactic pressure field that scales inversely with vertical height ($|z|$) and Galactocentric radius ($R_{GC}$), consistent with the properties of the Galactic Flare. By incorporating this AI-derived pressure support, we demonstrate a dramatic shift in the stability census: 99.9\% of previously thought unbound clouds are found to be in a state of pressure confined equilibrium ($\alpha_{AI} \leq 2$). Furthermore, we find a robust log-log correlation ($R = 0.64$) between our corrected stability parameter and the star formation rate (SFR). This correlation provides independent physical validation that environmental confinement is a primary regulator of star forming efficiency in the outer Galaxy.

papers.title: Multiprobe strategies for Kinematic Lensing with the Roman Space Telescope High Latitude Wide Area Survey
papers.summary: In its latest design, the High Latitude Wide Area Survey (HLWAS) Medium Tier comprises overlapping photometric and spectroscopic data across 2,300 square degrees. This dataset enables Kinematic Lensing (KL), a Weak Lensing (WL) technique that exploits galaxy kinematics to control for shape noise, the dominant statistical limitation of traditional WL. We present several simulated analyses quantifying the expected cosmological science return of a Roman KL analysis with the latest design of the HLWAS: We explore KL prospects with early Roman data from the Deep Tier fields and from the early Medium Tier fields; we demonstrate the impact of different roll-angle choices on the KL performance; we benchmark KL against traditional WL; we introduce a KL-based multiprobe analysis that jointly models KL, galaxy clustering, and galaxy-galaxy lensing. In these analyses, we consider systematics, including photometric uncertainties, shear calibration bias, galaxy bias, and baryonic feedback. Our results show that KL alone achieves a dark energy figure of merit (FoM) of 22.54, which is more than a factor of two improvement over a corresponding WL analysis. The KL multiprobe approach improves the full-survey FoM to 34.58, even assuming conservative scale cuts in the clustering and galaxy-galaxy lensing. For the HLWAS roll-angle strategy, we find that the current plan of 4 passes with rotations of approximately 0, 10, 170, 180 degrees are near optimal for KL.

papers.title: Baryonic feedback and intrinsic alignments in profile: a frequentist view of DES Y3 cosmic shear
papers.summary: Current cosmic shear surveys primarily constrain $S_8$ and $\Omega_\mathrm{m}$, while most other model parameters remain dominated by priors. Consequently, marginal posteriors are vulnerable to prior-volume effects, particularly through degeneracies among $S_8$, baryonic feedback, and intrinsic alignment (IA) model parameters. To isolate data-driven constraints from prior volume effects, we compare profile likelihoods with Bayesian posteriors for DES Y3 cosmic shear under the DES Y3+KiDS-1000 Hybrid model. For cosmic shear alone, the profile global best fit and the marginal posterior mean agree in $S_8$, but the profile likelihood reveals a strong degeneracy between feedback strength and $S_8$, leaving the upper $1\sigma$ limit on $S_8$ determined by the assumed feedback range. External CMB information on parameters other than $\Omega_\mathrm{m}$ and $S_8$ breaks this degeneracy, suppressing prior-volume effects and reconciling the profiles with the posteriors. With CMB data included, small-scale cosmic shear data prefers moderate baryonic feedback strengths consistent with hydrodynamical simulations calibrated to observed gas fractions. Furthermore, additional unconstrained parameters in the tidal alignment and tidal torquing (TATT) model result in weaker constraints, shifting and broadening the $S_8$ profile relative to the nonlinear linear alignment (NLA) model. Adding DES Y3 shear ratios mitigates this degeneracy, bringing profile likelihood and marginal posteriors into close agreement.

papers.title: VLITE Observations of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field
papers.summary: We present 136 hr of 340 MHz observations of the Hubble Ultra Deep Field (HUDF) conducted with the VLA Low-band Ionosphere and Transient Experiment (VLITE), collected commensally with higher-frequency Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array (VLA) observations. Our deepest image combines 20 hr of data, covers 4 square degrees, and achieves an angular resolution of 8.8 arcsec x 3.8 arcsec with an rms sensitivity of 158 microJy per beam at the field center. We catalog 671 radio sources detected above 5 sigma significance. Correcting for incompleteness using injection-recovery simulations with a model radio continuum population, we show that our source counts recover the sub-mJy star-forming galaxy population at abundances consistent with other deep fields at comparable frequencies. The data span 45 observing days across two VLA A-configuration semesters separated by 1.3 years, providing a search for variability on ~1-year timescales at sub-mJy flux densities. We identify eleven variable sources with flux densities of 1-100 mJy and modulation indices of 6-40%, six of which exhibit peaked radio spectra consistent with compact AGN. Their variability amplitudes are consistent with refractive interstellar scintillation (RISS) predicted for this line of sight, though three sources with modulation indices exceeding 30% likely require an intrinsic contribution. One source, subsequently confirmed as a compact symmetric object through VLBA follow-up observations, demonstrates the potential of VLITE for identifying populations of young radio AGN through commensal low-frequency variability searches.

papers.title: Toward the one- and two-loop EFTofLSS for Simons Observatory CMB lensing
papers.summary: Cosmic microwave background (CMB) lensing observations are becoming sensitive to non-linear structure formation and baryonic feedback scenarios. The effective field theory of large-scale structure (EFTofLSS) provides a systematic description of matter clustering in the mildly non-linear regime, accounting for baryonic effects through counterterms and offering a consistent framework for cross-correlations with other observables. We perform a Fisher forecast for the joint Simons Observatory temperature, polarization, and CMB lensing likelihood using noiseless data vectors with different baryonic feedback scenarios, modelling non-linear structure formation using the one- and two-loop EFTofLSS. We find that, with a single additional parameter, obtained through a principal-component analysis of the EFTofLSS counterterms, both the one- and two-loop EFTofLSS provide a good fit across the baryonic feedback scenarios considered. This parameter is closely aligned with the effective AGN heating temperature $T_{\rm AGN}$. Both loop orders reduce cosmological parameter biases, with only a small loss in marginalized precision at fixed scale cuts. We find that the one-loop EFTofLSS yields unbiased estimates over a range of scales similar to the dark-matter-only model, while the two-loop EFTofLSS extends this range to smaller scales and accommodates different feedback scenarios more robustly. When each model is evaluated at the smallest scales for which its cosmological parameter estimates remain unbiased, the two-loop EFTofLSS yields stronger constraints than the dark-matter-only model.

papers.title: Episodic Protostellar Outflows: A Proper Motion Study in Serpens South
papers.summary: Serpens South is a notable protostellar cluster with signatures of recent star formation, including a high protostellar fraction. Within the region, several protostars provide important mechanical feedback via outflows. We investigate the molecular outflow driven by the Class 0 protostar known as CARMA-7, which is located in the central hub of Serpens South. Two epochs of observations with the Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array (ALMA) with sub-arcsecond resolution capture the well-collimated, episodic outflow with distinct ejecta knots. This outflow, traced with 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7, appears to be mostly blueshifted to the south and redshifted to the north, with radial velocities up to at least 25 km/s. We present the first proper motion study of this outflow by comparing observations taken in 2017 and 2021. The measured proper motions trace the ejection history and refine the inferred outflow morphology. We find that proper motions of the 12CO J = 3-2 and SiO J = 8-7 knots range between 10 - 40 mas/yr, corresponding to 30-90 km/s. Using radial velocities and proper motions, we determined that the inclinations of the outflow lobes are ~60 -80 degrees relative to the line of sight. Finally, we measure ejection timescales as recent as ~10 to ~120 years, and we discuss this in the context of other known protostars with recent ejecta events.

papers.title: Detection of the Galaxy--Galaxy--Temperature Skewed Bispectrum
papers.summary: We present the first measurement of the galaxy--galaxy--temperature skewed bispectrum, obtained by cross-correlating the squared, filtered unWISE galaxy overdensity with \textit{Planck} maps at 100, 143, 217, and 353~GHz. The signal is detected with high significance in all four channels. Its frequency dependence reveals contributions from hot gas through the thermal Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (tSZ) effect and from dust through the cosmic infrared background (CIB). With the galaxy occupation fixed, our halo-model fits favor higher integrated pressure and peak star-formation efficiency for the galaxy--temperature cross-spectra than for the skewed bispectrum. Comparisons with component-separated tSZ and CIB maps from the same \textit{Planck} observations indicate that this mismatch is not confined to the frequency-map fits. This difference motivates testing more flexible descriptions of gas pressure, CIB emission, and galaxy occupation. In particular, it could point to a mass dependence of the gas-pressure profile that our model does not fully capture. By giving greater weight to massive halos that host many galaxy pairs, the skewed bispectrum provides a complementary test of these descriptions, using information beyond two-point statistics at a comparable computational cost.
