papers.title: A Tightly Coupled Magnetic-Inertial SLAM System for Field Robots
papers.summary: Field robots operating in mines, tunnels, and disaster areas require reliable localization despite GNSS denial and degraded camera and LiDAR measurements caused by dust, smoke, or poor illumination. Missions involving both ground and aerial robots further motivate complementary sensing modalities that do not depend on visibility, preinstalled infrastructure, or wheel contact. This letter presents MISLAM, a tightly coupled magnetic-inertial simultaneous localization and mapping system using an IMU and a nine-magnetometer array, without relying on external odometry or platform-specific motion assumptions. The system combines the inertial navigation model with local polynomial magnetic-field models for short-term motion estimation and a global Gaussian process model for drift correction using an error-state Kalman filter. Offline evaluation on three indoor datasets collected with a handheld rig shows reductions in total endpoint closure error of 45.7% - 78.0% relative to magnetic-inertial odometry. Under poor illumination, MISLAM maintains tracking after visual-inertial odometry fails, achieving a horizontal closure error of 0.332 m, although vertical drift remains a limitation. These results support magnetic-inertial SLAM as a complementary localization modality for robotic sensor suites operating under degraded visual conditions.

papers.title: Harnessing Mutual Coupling in Cell-Free mMIMO
papers.summary: This letter investigates a cell-free massive MIMO system with $L$ access points (APs), each employing a small fixed-form-factor, uniform linear array of $N$ potentially closely spaced antennas. Utilizing multiport communication theory, we analyze the impact of mutual coupling on uplink and downlink spectral efficiency (SE) under various impedance-matching strategies. We compare two deployment regimes: ($i$) increasing $N$ while $L$ is kept fixed, and ($ii$) increasing $N$ while fixing the total antenna count $M = NL$. Numerical results show that, with a full matching network, mutual coupling itself becomes beneficial when an AP serves several user equipments, which is the typical operating regime of user-centric cell-free networks. Furthermore, with full matching, antenna densification can enhance SE or allow for a reduction in the number of APs without performance loss. Since full matching networks remain of manageable size in the small arrays of distributed APs, unlike in large centralized arrays, cell-free networks offer a natural setting for exploiting mutual coupling.

papers.title: Safe-Ballbot: Tilt-Consistent MPC with Control Barrier Functions for Ballbot Navigation
papers.summary: Ball-balancing robots (ballbots) must lean to accelerate, and the lean is limited by the wheel torques and by safety. Planners that use the full robot model are expensive, while planners that ignore the balance dynamics produce references that cannot be followed. This paper presents a two-layer navigation scheme for a three-omni-wheel ballbot. The upper layer is a model predictive controller on a \emph{jerk model} of the ball position, with discrete-time control barrier functions for static, moving, rotating and concave obstacles. The lower layer is a hierarchical sliding mode controller with an extended state observer and a robust exponential control barrier function on the tilt (HSMC-ESO-ECBF). The layers are linked by an acceleration bound derived in closed form from the largest steady tilt that the barrier function admits, so that the plan never asks for a lean the tracker refuses. For obstacles whose motion is only predicted, the obstacles are inflated by conformal prediction radii that bound the prediction error with a prescribed probability. In MuJoCo, with omni-wheel roller contacts and torque saturation, the scheme keeps at least $10$\,cm of clearance, tracks the plan within $2$\,cm RMS, keeps the tilt below the limit and plans in $9$--$12$\,ms, $10$--$15$ times faster than a full-model nonlinear MPC that enters the inflated obstacles; with predicted obstacles, the conformal inflation removes the collisions of a constant-velocity predictor in $30$ random crossing scenarios and reduces them in an endless run on a closed path.The source code and video illustrations are available at https://safe-ballbot.github.io

papers.title: Non-Coherent Over-the-Air Distributed Consensus: Algorithm Design and Power Control Optimization
papers.summary: Non-coherent over-the-air (NCOTA) aggregation offers a scalable and communication-efficient approach to distributed average consensus in wireless networks, without requiring instantaneous channel state information (CSI) or phase alignment. However, persistent aggregation errors pose fundamental challenges in achieving exact average consensus under nominal distributed averaging protocols. In this paper, we develop an NCOTA consensus framework that accommodates row-stochastic mixing, without requiring the conventional average-preservation property of doubly stochastic mixing matrices. Building on a distributed optimization formulation of average consensus, we propose a decentralized projected gradient descent with row-stochastic mixing (DPGD-RS) algorithm and establish its mean-square convergence to the exact average of the agents' initial states. We further derive a closed-form upper bound on the mean-square consensus error, characterizing the effects of aggregation uncertainty, network connectivity, and mixing imbalance. Guided by this analysis, we propose a spectral-reshaping power control (SR-PC) scheme that jointly optimizes transmit powers and receive-scaling factors to accelerate convergence by balancing aggregation accuracy and network mixing. Numerical results validate the theoretical convergence guarantees and demonstrate that the proposed power control scheme significantly accelerates convergence compared with full-power transmission and spectral-radius-minimization benchmarks.

papers.title: Beyond GNSS: Leveraging LEO Satellite Signals of Opportunity for Doppler Positioning
papers.summary: Large constellations of low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites provide ubiquitous global connectivity; yet, their rapid motion introduces significant Doppler shift effects. While challenging for communication, these effects can be leveraged for precise user terminal (UT) positioning, particularly in GNSS-denied environments where traditional satellite-based navigation struggles. Unlike GNSS, most LEO satellites lack dedicated navigation signals, motivating signals-of-opportunity (SOPs) approaches that repurpose existing LEO signals and use publicly available two-line element (TLE) files for orbital information, although ephemeris errors can limit accuracy. This article explores the fundamental principles, challenges, and enabling technologies for LEO-based Doppler shift positioning, highlighting its advantages over conventional non-Doppler methods, and discussing future research directions. Furthermore, to facilitate realistic and reproducible performance evaluation beyond stochastic modeling, we propose SionnaNTN-RT, a ray tracing framework for non-terrestrial network (NTN) built upon Sionna, enabling end-to-end simulation of Doppler-based positioning. Simulation results demonstrate that Doppler-based positioning can achieve high positioning accuracy in both urban and open-sky environments, highlighting its promise for next-generation positioning systems.

papers.title: Delay-Certified Readiness Barriers for Overactuated Multirotor Allocation Without Lipschitz Constants
papers.summary: Overactuated multirotors can produce the same wrench with many rotor-speed combinations, some of which leave the vehicle unable to change its wrench quickly, e.g., to reject a gust. Readiness barriers keep this ability, the readiness, above a floor, but only in continuous time; with sampled commands and varying speed-controller delays, the available robustness bound covers less than one millisecond. We remove this limit by exploiting the structure of the problem: each rotor responds monotonically and in closed form to its own torque, so the speeds reachable under uncertain switching times lie in a cheaply computed box, and the lowest readiness over that box sits at a corner known in advance. This yields a Lipschitz-free test that a command keeps the readiness above its floor until the next sample, plus a fallback torque that keeps the vehicle on a certified plan. In hexarotor simulations with 2--40~ms delays and $\pm2$~ms jitter, the filter never violated the floor. At $10\pm2$~ms, it matched a delay-compensating predictor within the design envelope and cost 2--30\% more tracking error beyond it, where the predictor alone violated the floor in 2 to 16 of 16 missions.

papers.title: Dynamical Unbalanced Optimal Transport: Duality, Reachability, and Computation
papers.summary: We study dynamical unbalanced optimal transport for nonlinear control-affine systems in which the control input affects both the transportation of mass and its growth or decay. This phenomenon arises naturally in controlled transport-reaction systems such as cancer treatment, and distinguishes the problem from standard unbalanced optimal transport, where transport and mass variation are typically independent. To address this problem, we combine classical relaxed-control theory with a weighted superposition principle to obtain an infinite-dimensional linear programming reformulation over weighted trajectories. Under suitable convexity and compactness assumptions, we show that this relaxation is tight. Based on the relaxation, we derive a Kantorovich dual formulation in terms of Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman inequalities, and establish strong duality over smooth subsolutions. We then utilize the dual formulation to characterize reachability of the system, namely, when a given terminal measure is reachable from a given initial measure. In addition, tractable sufficient conditions for reachability are provided. Finally, we develop an augmented-Lagrangian algorithm based on the dual formulation for numerical computation of the optimal transport plan. The framework is illustrated on a phenotype-structured cancer treatment problem in which therapy simultaneously drives phenotypic adaptation and population growth or death.

papers.title: Dynamic State-Feedback Control for LPV Systems: Ensuring Stability and LQR Performance
papers.summary: In this paper, we propose a novel dynamic state-feedback controller for polytopic linear parameter-varying (LPV) systems with constant input matrix. The controller employs a projected gradient flow method to continuously improve its control law and, under established conditions, converges to the optimal feedback gain of the corresponding linear quadratic regulator (LQR) problem associated with constant parameter trajectories. We derive conditions for quadratic stability, which can be verified via convex optimization, to ensure exponential stability of the LPV system even under arbitrarily fast parameter variations. Additionally, we provide sufficient conditions to guarantee the boundedness of the trajectories of the dynamic controller for any parameter trajectory and the convergence of its feedback gains to the optimal LQR gains for constant parameter trajectories. Furthermore, we show that incorporating the plant state into the controller dynamics renders the closed-loop system is asymptotically stable for constant parameter trajectories under these conditions. Simulation results demonstrate that the controller maintains stability and improves transient performance.

papers.title: HoloTrace: a Location Privacy-Preserving Framework for mmWave MIMO-OFDM Systems
papers.summary: High-resolution radio localization is becoming increasingly important for next-generation vehicular and mobile networks, enabling infrastructure-assisted positioning for connected and automated mobility. However, the same mmWave multiple-input multiple-output (MIMO)-orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) links used for communication may allow a serving base station (BS) to infer the location of a vehicle-mounted or mobile user equipment (UE) from routine uplink pilot transmissions, even without an explicit positioning request. This paper introduces HoloTrace, a signal-level location-privacy framework for single-BS localization in mmWave MIMO-OFDM systems. HoloTrace modifies user-side pilot symbols while keeping the analog precoder fixed to bias localization-relevant channel features, including angle of arrival (AoA), angle of departure (AoD), and time difference of arrival (TDoA), toward a prescribed fictitious geometry. We formulate pilot-level spoofing as a subspace projection-based signal design problem and derive closed-form oracle designs assuming UE-side channel-gain knowledge. We further develop blind designs that operate without complex path-gain information, while relying on geometric side information, and explicitly characterize their limitations in multipath scenarios. Simulation results with a two-path single-anchor geometry show that oracle HoloTrace can steer the inferred position toward a desired spoofed location, whereas blind variants mainly provide obfuscation or approximate spoofing due to angle-delay pairing ambiguities. The communication impact is geometry-dependent rather than intrinsic to the proposed method: selecting a spoofed location compatible with the serving beams can preserve channel-rate quality while providing effective location privacy.

papers.title: Joint Communications, Sensing, and Positioning in 6G Multi-Functional Satellite Systems: Survey and Open Challenges
papers.summary: Satellite systems are expected to be a cornerstone of sixth-generation (6G) networks, supporting communications, sensing, and positioning, navigation, and timing (PNT) with global coverage. This survey develops a framework for multi-functional satellite systems (MFSS), which combine at least two of these services through shared or jointly designed payload resources. A two-dimensional taxonomy distinguishes the functional configuration---joint communications and sensing (JCAS), joint communications and PNT (JCAP), joint sensing and PNT (JSAP), or joint communications, sensing, and PNT (JCSAP)---from the integration depth---cooperative, integrated, or joint. After consolidating the communication, sensing, and PNT fundamentals and payload architectures into a single background section, the survey examines the three integration levels and then devotes a dedicated section to each configuration, covering its architecture, classification, state of the art, advantages, key challenges, and research directions. The achievable performance of each configuration is illustrated with representative trade-off results from the literature and compared across configurations, the differences between terrestrial multi-functional networks and satellite MFSS are made explicit, and a life-cycle techno-economic framework balances hardware, spectrum, launch, and operational reuse against engineering, qualification, verification, and common-mode risks. The analysis shows that deeper integration can improve resource utilization and functional synergy, but is not automatically the technical or economic optimum for every mission.

papers.title: Distributed Adaptive Estimation with ISS Guarantees for Sensor Networks with Partially Unknown Source Dynamics
papers.summary: This paper studies distributed adaptive estimation over sensor networks with partially unknown source dynamics. We present parallel continuous-time and discrete-time designs in which each node runs a local adaptive observer and exchanges information over a directed graph. For both time scales, we establish stability of the network coupling operators, prove boundedness of all internal signals, and show convergence of each node's estimate to the source despite model uncertainty and disturbances. We further derive input-to-state stability (ISS) bounds that quantify robustness to bounded process noise. A key distinction is that the discrete-time design uses constant adaptive gains and per-step regressor normalization to handle sampling effects, whereas the continuous-time design does not. A unified Lyapunov framework links local observer dynamics with graph topology. Simulations on star, cyclic, and path networks corroborate the analysis, demonstrating accurate tracking, robustness, and scalability with the number of sensing nodes.

papers.title: The Iberian Blackout: A Black Swan or a Gray Rhino? A Protection-Aware Dynamic Voltage Security Assessment
papers.summary: On 28 April 2025, the Iberian power system collapsed after a rapid voltage rise that led to widespread generation disconnections and loss of synchronism. The final report of the ENTSO-E Expert Panel attributes the blackout to several interacting factors including ineffective voltage control, fixed power factor operation, misaligned protection settings, manual shunt reactor switching, and limited observability. These factors raise a general question: given the current state, can the next trip, ramp, topology action, or shunt switching raise the voltages measured by overvoltage relays above their settings before voltage controls respond? We answer it with a protection-aware dynamic voltage security assessment. For each candidate event, the method computes the voltage at every overvoltage relay over the relay time window from a dynamic model of the network, its controls, and its relays. It predicts which relays trip after a first trip, identifies assets whose relay or measurement data are insufficient for a safety conclusion, and, when one exists, computes a minimum-cost fast reactive power action that keeps all relay voltages below their settings. Case studies on four benchmark systems and a 2000-bus system that reproduces the mechanism of the Iberian blackout show that the method flagged every event that caused a secondary trip within the relay window, never declared safe a plant that tripped within that window, and, on the benchmarks, found fast reactive power actions that prevented the trips within the relay window whenever it judged such actions feasible. These results were validated with nonlinear time-domain simulations. The code is publicly available.

papers.title: Log-linear Dynamic Inversion for Thrusting Spacecraft on SE2(3)
papers.summary: Body-fixed spacecraft thrust couples attitude tracking error to translational motion because the applied inertial acceleration depends on spacecraft attitude. In this work, we formulate the dynamics of a continuously thrusting spacecraft on $\mathrm{SE}_2(3)$ to make this coupling explicit while retaining a structured form suitable for analysis. We represent attitude, velocity, and position within a single Lie-group state and derive the logarithmic dynamics of a left-invariant tracking error with position-dependent gravity. The resulting dynamics show explicitly how attitude error affects translational velocity through the applied acceleration and separate the structured linear dynamics from nonlinear contributions due to body-frame input mismatch and position-dependent gravity difference. We specialize the gravity contribution to the two-body model and derive an analytical bound in terms of the reference orbital radius, logarithmic position error, and attitude error. Numerical simulations of a continuous-thrust maneuver in a highly elliptical Molniya-like orbit show agreement between the derived logarithmic error dynamics and errors reconstructed from independent nonlinear state propagation.

papers.title: A Data-Driven Krasovskii-Based Approach for Safety Controller Design of Time-Delayed Uncertain Polynomial Systems
papers.summary: We develop a data-driven framework for the synthesis of robust Krasovskii control barrier certificates (RK-CBC) and corresponding robust safety controllers (R-SC) for discrete-time input-affine uncertain polynomial systems with (partially) unknown dynamics, while explicitly accounting for unknown-but-bounded disturbances and time-invariant delays using only observed input-state data. Although control barrier certificates have been extensively studied for safety analysis of control systems, existing work on unknown systems with time delays, particularly in the presence of disturbances, remains limited. The challenge of safety synthesis for such systems stems from two main factors: first, the system's mathematical model is unavailable; and second, the safety conditions should explicitly incorporate the effects of time delays on system evolution during the synthesis process, while remaining robust to unknown disturbances. To address these challenges, we develop a data-driven framework based on RK-CBC, extending the classical CBC formulation for delay-free systems to explicitly account for time delays by aggregating delayed components within the barrier construction. The proposed framework relies solely on input-state data collected over a finite time horizon, enabling the direct synthesis of RK-CBC and R-SC from observed trajectories without requiring an explicit system model. The synthesis is cast as a data-driven sum-of-squares (SOS) feasibility program, yielding a structured design methodology. As a result, robust safety is guaranteed in the presence of unknown disturbances and time delays as long as the closed-loop trajectories remain within the state set. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through three case studies, including two physical systems.

papers.title: Cramer-Rao Bounds for Target Parameter Estimation in a Bi-Static IRS-Assisted Radar Configuration
papers.summary: The use of Intelligent Reflective Surfaces (IRS) to assist communication and sensing has proven cost-effective in challenging scenarios. For sensing, IRS is shown to sense non-line-of-sight (NLOS) and stealth targets, albeit with significant loss due to the four-hop path model. Amongst the available IRS-assisted configurations, we consider a three-hop model in which the IRS redirects the scattered target response towards the mono-static radar. With the IRS spatially displaced from the radar, this configuration mimics a bi-static radar. While target detection has been studied in this configuration, parameter estimation has not been investigated to date. To this end, we first develop the signal model for this configuration and derive the Cramer Rao Bounds (CRB) for target parameters. The dependence of CRB on system parameters such as SNR, number of snapshots, number of IRS elements and their weights is brought forward through extensive simulations. This study can enable a designer to customize the system parameters to meet the requirements. It also serves as a benchmark for parameter estimation techniques developed for this configuration.

papers.title: A Survey on Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces: Fundamentals, Recent Advances, and Challenges
papers.summary: Stacked intelligent metasurfaces (SIMs) cascade several closely spaced programmable metasurface layers so that an electromagnetic wave undergoes repeated modulation-propagation interactions before leaving the stack. The stack thereby implements, at the speed of propagation and with few radio-frequency chains, high-dimensional analog transformations that would otherwise require digital precoding, combining, spatial filtering, focusing, or inference. Since 2023, SIM research has produced more than two hundred articles, a dedicated magazine special issue, and two survey-level overviews organized around applications and wave-domain computing. This article complements them with a model-to-hardware perspective. First, we present the electromagnetic modeling hierarchy of SIMs, making explicit the assumptions under which the models coincide, their validity regimes, and their computational complexity, with a common notation for hardware non-idealities and power consumption. Second, we present a methodology-first taxonomy (SIM-aware channel acquisition, model-based optimization, statistical-CSI design, learning-based control, and hardware-aware robust design), compare the families in terms of CSI requirements, complexity, convergence, and hardware constraints, and reconcile conflicting findings in the literature. Third, we synthesize applications by the physical role of the SIM. Fourth, we quantitatively compare experimentally demonstrated multilayer prototypes, separate validated from conceptual architectures, and discuss thermal, tolerance, and calibration issues. Fifth, we provide a tutorial-style performance and trade-off analysis anchored in reported results. Finally, we map evidence-based challenges to research directions with measurable targets. Lessons learned are summarized at the end of every section.

papers.title: Coupling Europe's Capacity Markets
papers.summary: European Member States are increasingly introducing national capacity mechanisms (CMs) to manage growing adequacy risks. However, isolated national CMs are inefficient in highly interconnected electricity systems, such as the European system. While progress has been made in facilitating cross-border participation by generation capacity in CMs, existing arrangements are prone to under- or over-investment and do not properly value the contribution of interconnection capacity to Member States' adequacy targets. We argue that national capacity markets, offering long-term contracts, need a second tier: an annual capacity auction coupled across zones, which sets zonal prices for firm, deliverable capacity. We design such an auction by extending the logic of flow-based market coupling to capacity markets. In a comparative analysis of different market design scenarios in an illustrative multi-zone case study, using a bespoke long-run equilibrium problem, we show that the proposed auction removes the circular dependency between imports and available capacity in current cross-border participation schemes, locates investment where it is cheapest while keeping it deliverable under network constraints in defined scarcity situations, and makes the value of additional interconnection capacity explicit.

papers.title: Reusable Neural Reachability via Local Refinement
papers.summary: This paper studies obstacle avoidance under translation invariant dynamics using an avoid-side travel cost Hamilton Jacobi formulation. For running costs that are zero outside an obstacle and strictly negative inside it, we prove that the value function is non-positive everywhere, equals zero exactly outside the avoid set, and is strictly negative exactly on it. Under translation invariance, this yields a reuse principle: the value of any translated obstacle is obtained by translating a single template value function. We show that the pointwise minimum of translated template values exactly characterizes the union of the translated single-obstacle avoid sets and provides a conservative inner certificate of unavoidable collision in clutter. To reduce conservatism, we introduce a blockwise composition framework in which subsets of obstacles are merged and solved jointly. This yields a hierarchy of conservative certificates from singleton reuse to the exact clutter value, together with monotonicity under block merging and an exactness criterion based on the existence of a common clutter avoiding control. The framework is illustrated on a Dubins car example in a repeated clutter field.

papers.title: Energy-Efficient Velocity Profile Optimization for Movable Antenna-Enabled Sensing Systems
papers.summary: Movable antennas (MAs) enable the reconfiguration of array geometry within a bounded region to exploit sub-wavelength spatial degrees of freedom in wireless communication and sensing systems. However, most prior research has predominantly focused on the communication and sensing performance, overlooking the mechanical power consumption inherent in antenna movement. To bridge this gap, this paper investigates a velocity profile optimization framework for MA-assisted direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation, explicitly balancing sensing accuracy with mechanical energy consumption of MAs. We first establish a Newtonian-based mechanical energy model, and formulate a functional optimization problem for sensing energy efficiency (EE) maximization. By applying the calculus of variations, this formulation is transformed into an infinite-dimensional problem defined by the Euler-Lagrange equation. To solve it, we propose a spectral discretization framework based on the Galerkin method, which expands the velocity profile over a sinusoidal basis. In the regime where energy consumption is dominated by linear damping, we prove that the optimal velocity profile follows a closed-form sinusoidal shape. For more general scenarios involving strong nonlinear aerodynamic drag, we leverage the Markov-Luk\'{a}cs theorem to transform the kinematic constraints into strictly convex sum-of-squares (SOS) conditions. Consequently, the infinite-dimensional problem is reformulated as a tractable finite-dimensional nonlinear algebraic system, which is solved by a two-layer algorithm combining Dinkelbach's method with successive convex approximation (SCA). Numerical results demonstrate that our optimized velocity profile significantly outperforms baselines in terms of EE across various system configurations. Insights into the optimized velocity profiles and practical design guidelines are also provided.

papers.title: Feedforward Density-Driven Optimal Control (D2OC) for Tracking Time-Varying Distributions
papers.summary: Tracking a time-varying spatial distribution poses a fundamental challenge for multi-agent systems, as agents often lag behind a moving target when reacting solely to the current target configuration. This paper develops a feedforward extension of Density-Driven Optimal Control (D$^2$OC) for dynamic distribution tracking with general discrete-time linear time-invariant agents. The proposed framework predicts reference sample trajectories along a known velocity field and incorporates these anticipated locations into the finite-horizon control problem. A scalar factor explicitly adjusts the feedforward action to account for predicted reference displacement. We establish an explicit receding-horizon control policy and provide a formal performance analysis that quantifies the tracking impact of prediction limitations. Furthermore, under a nominal stability condition, we derive explicit ultimate bounds on agent tracking errors and local Wasserstein distances in the presence of bounded reference drift, discretization errors, and transport perturbations. Monte Carlo simulations with linearized quadrotor dynamics demonstrate that incorporating feedforward compensation significantly mitigates tracking lag and enhances spatial distribution matching. These results offer formal analytical guarantees for predictive distribution tracking while preserving the computational efficiency and local optimization structure of D$^2$OC.

papers.title: Energy Efficiency Maximization for Discrete Activation based NOMA-assisted Pinching-Antenna Systems
papers.summary: Pinching-antenna systems are a promising architecture for flexible wireless communications, but energy efficiency (EE) maximization remains largely unexplored, as limited existing studies mainly focus on transmit power minimization. This paper investigates EE maximization in a downlink non-orthogonal multiple access (NOMA)-assisted PASS by explicitly modeling the pinching antenna (PA) activation power and jointly optimizing discrete PA activation and power allocation under both quality-of-service and transmit power constraints. To tackle the resulting mixed-integer nonlinear programming problem, a two-layer iterative algorithm is proposed with an EE-oriented matching-based PA activation and a Dinkelbach-based power allocation with closed-form updates. Numerical results demonstrate that the proposed solution achieves substantial EE gains over the considered benchmark schemes, while exhibiting fast convergence. The impact of activation power has been analyzed and the significance of accounting it in EE maximization problem is also demonstrated.

papers.title: Valuing Static Synchronous Series Compensators in the U.S. Grid: Planning with Transmission Feedback
papers.summary: Flexible AC Transmission Systems, particularly Static Synchronous Series Compensators (SSSCs), can increase the transfer capability of existing networks and complement constrained transmission expansion, but their value, optimal scale, and best locations in U.S. power system planning remain unquantified. This paper develops a capacity expansion model of the contiguous U.S. power system for 2050, incorporating SSSC-modified power flow equations. Expanding a line by adding parallel circuits lowers its equivalent impedance and, for a given SSSC rating, the series voltage the SSSC can inject. Through this transmission feedback, line flows depend nonlinearly on capacity decisions, making the planning problem nonconvex. We solve it by sequential linear programming (SLP) with adaptive proximal regularization. We prove the convergence to a Karush-Kuhn-Tucker point, which does not hold for the conventional fixed-impedance iteration. We also demonstrate that SLP converges faster to lower-cost plans. In the baseline scenario, the least-cost plan deploys 291 GVAr of SSSCs across the contiguous U.S. SSSCs reduce annualized system cost by $6.75 billion (2.1%) with an overall benefit-cost ratio (BCR) of 6.4 and lower the average wholesale electricity price by 5.1%. Alternatively, SSSCs could avoid about 75% of the transmission expansion without increasing system cost. Most of the economic value of SSSCs could be delivered by deployment in high-value locations: the highest-value 1 GVAr, located mainly near Eastern U.S. load centers, yields a BCR above 100, and one-tenth of the optimal SSSC capacity captures half of the savings. The overall BCR of SSSCs ranges from 4.1 to 9.1 across the demand, decarbonization, and device cost scenarios considered.

papers.title: Residual-Corrected Equivalent-Circuit Model with Universal Differential Equations for Robust Battery Voltage Prediction under Operating-Condition Shift
papers.summary: Accurate terminal-voltage prediction underpins model-based battery management, yet low-order equivalent-circuit models (\ecm{}) lack expressiveness under transient conditions, whereas purely data-driven predictors sacrifice interpretability and may degrade under operating-condition shift. This paper introduces a residual-corrected hybrid formulation in which a first-order Thevenin \ecm{} (\ecmrc{}) provides the dominant voltage structure, and a compact neural network embedded as a universal differential equation (\ude{}) corrects only the latent polarization mismatch. The \ecmrc{} parameters identified by nonlinear least squares warm-start the hybrid model so that the learned component operates in a low-residual regime. Experiments on a public Panasonic 18650PF dataset compare the proposed \ecmude{} with standalone \ecmrc{} and Long Short-Term Memory (\lstm{}) baselines across four axes: matched-condition prediction on UDDS at \SI{25}{\celsius}, inference-time perturbation of the supplied state-of-charge (\SOC{}, denoted $z$) input, zero-shot temperature transfer (\SI{25}{\celsius} to \SI{-20}{\celsius}), and zero-shot drive-cycle transfer to US06, LA92, and HWFET. The proposed \ecmude{} achieves the lowest voltage error in every setting, reducing mean absolute error (\mae{}) by 48\% relative to the \lstm{} under matched conditions and showing an order-of-magnitude lower inter-seed variability (coefficient of variation: 0.44\% vs.\ 6.20\%). Substantial gains persist under challenging distribution shifts, indicating that the physical model anchors prediction where a purely learned model is most vulnerable. These results position residual-corrected \ecmude{} as a lightweight and interpretable enhancement of low-order circuit models for voltage prediction in battery management systems (\bms{}).

papers.title: Octree-Context Gaussian Splatting with Multi-Order Propagation for Channel Knowledge Maps
papers.summary: Channel knowledge maps (CKMs) can support environment-aware wireless communications by providing site-specific channel knowledge as a function of the transmitter position, the receiver position or both. Existing Gaussian splatting CKM methods can reduce the high training and inference costs of implicit neural methods yet represent all multipath interactions by one wireless radiance field. We propose octree-context Gaussian splatting (OctCGS), which anchors Gaussian primitives on an octree as virtual scattering nodes and decomposes multi-bounce propagation into orders by the number of node-level interactions along each path. Shared tree attention gives each node local context from neighboring octree cells and room-wide context from ancestor cells at a cost linear in the number of cells, and the order-wise scattering of each node is predicted from this context. The order-wise contributions of the power transported between the nodes are summed in power with a line-of-sight (LoS) term to give the channel gain and the spatial spectrum. OctCGS raises the spatial-spectrum structural similarity (SSIM) by 0.13 to 0.23 and lowers the mean absolute error (MAE) of the channel gain by 0.9 to 3.8 dB on five indoor ray-tracing scenes, relative to the best baseline per scene and metric.

papers.title: Orion: Enabling Self-adaptive Memory Management for On-device Online Continual Learning
papers.summary: Online continual learning (OCL) enables real-time adaptation to new data, making it crucial for dynamic robotic applications. However, its practical deployment is hindered by memory constraints in resource-limited systems, which affect key trade-offs in training latency, plasticity, and stability. Unlike offline parameter tuning, which cannot account for the dynamic shift in memory pressure and workload complexity as OCL progresses, an online and self-adaptive approach is essential for robust on-device deployment. This paper proposes Orion, a holistic framework designed to co-optimize training latency, plasticity, and stability of state-of-the-art OCL models under strict memory constraints, enabling feasible on-device deployment. At its core, Orion leverages URGE, a unified runtime indicator grounded in the ``Buckets effect'' principle that system performance is bounded by its scarcest resource, to dynamically reallocate memory across OCL components by jointly coordinating batch processing, replay buffers, and optimization strategies at both the OS and application level. Furthermore, Orion introduces system-level data prefetching techniques to maximize efficiency. A system prototype of Orion has been implemented using the widely adopted \texttt{Avalanche-lib} and thoroughly evaluated across a diverse range of OCL algorithms, benchmarks, and hardware platforms commonly used in autonomous robotic applications. To further demonstrate its practical utility, Orion is integrated into a realistic autonomous navigational robot powered by OCL. The results show that Orion achieves significant training speedups while maintaining balanced performance and effectively adapting to various scenarios, all with minimal runtime, memory, and energy overhead, making Orion a practical solution for on-device continual learning.

papers.title: When Can Phasor-Domain Device Models Be Trusted for Electromechanical Stability Analysis of Grid-Forming Converter-Dominated Microgrids?
papers.summary: Grid-forming (GFM) converter-dominated microgrids are often analyzed using reduced-order phasor-domain electromechanical GFM models, but the validity of these models is often taken for granted. Assuming ideal inner-loop tracking (IILT) of terminal-voltage references, these models neglect the inner-loop and filter dynamics at the electromagnetic-transient (EMT) timescale to simplify stability analysis. This paper argues that such neglected dynamics can destabilize the system, invalidating the stability conclusions drawn from the IILT model. To address this cross-timescale stability issue, we formulate the validity of the IILT stability conclusion as a robust-stability certification problem. The EMT-induced model mismatch between the reduced-order converter model and the actual converter model is represented as a structured uncertainty embedded around the IILT feedback loop. This yields a frequency-resolved interaction index and a structured singular-value sufficient certificate for determining when the stability conclusion of the IILT model can be certified with respect to a prescribed EMT uncertainty weight. The uncertainty weight can be obtained from detailed EMT models or terminal reference-response measurements. Case studies confirm that the proposed certificate correctly certifies model validity and identifies the loss of trustworthiness. We also demonstrate that the measurement-based uncertainty weights closely match the model-based ones, which enables deployment without accessing inner-loop models.

papers.title: Differentially Private Consensus for Time-Delay Multi-agent Systems
papers.summary: This paper is concerned with the differentially private consensus problem for discrete-time multi-agent systems with communication delays. The purpose of the paper is to achieve differentially private consensus for such systems while protecting the entire delayed initial histories of all agents. A novel adjacency relation for delayed histories is introduced, and a Laplace-noise-based privacy mechanism is developed, where the noise variance is allowed to vary with time and even increase. By using the difference resolvent function method, decay estimates for the fundamental solutions of the delayed difference equations are derived. Based on these estimates and a backstepping technique, mean square weak consensus, mean square strong consensus, and almost sure strong consensus are established. The estimates for the fundamental solutions are also used to derive an explicit sensitivity bound. Furthermore, a constructive parameter design is provided to achieve a prescribed infinite-horizon $\epsilon^\star$-differential privacy level. Numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical results.

papers.title: Beyond Speaker Independence: Evaluating Cross-Lingual Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion Across Finnish and Russian
papers.summary: Acoustic-to-articulatory inversion (AAI) remains challenging under domain shifts where changes in speaker attributes and cross-language conditions often degrade performance. We conduct a systematic evaluation under such shifts and establish baseline benchmarks on FROST-EMA, a Finnish-Russian bilingual EMA corpus. FROST-EMA addresses the English bias and limited speaker diversity of existing resources. We benchmark (i) articulatory targets (raw EMA coordinates vs tract variables), (ii) acoustic front-ends (MFCC vs SSL features), and (iii) inversion back-ends (BiLSTM vs a lightweight attention-based sequence model). We further define evaluation protocols for cross-gender transfer (within language) and cross-language transfer (within gender). The results indicate that cross-gender mismatch introduces moderate Pearson correlation declines (approximately 0.05 to 0.10) relative to the in-domain baseline, whereas cross-language mismatch causes larger drops (approximately 0.10 to 0.20).

papers.title: Predictive Beam Tracking for Sea-Air Communication under Wave-Induced Disturbances
papers.summary: In the sea-air communications system consisting of an uncrewed aerial vehicle (UAV) and an uncrewed surface vehicle (USV), the six-degree-of-freedom (6-DoF) motion of the USV under wave-induced disturbances may lead to severe misalignment of communication beams. In this paper, we develop a wide- and narrow-beam switching scheme based on an extended Kalman filter (EKF) algorithm. Specifically, in the wide-beam mode, the UAV transmits an integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) signal to provide full USV coverage and estimate the position of the communication receiver (CR) mounted on the USV. In the narrow-beam mode, the UAV forms a highly directional beam based on the position estimates of the CR for high-rate communication. In the EKF framework, we derive a state evolution model for the CR by incorporating wave-induced disturbance loads into the surge, sway, and yaw dynamics of the USV. In addition, we further analyze the impacts of sea clutter and sea state on the measurement equation, which is constructed using observations from multiple scatterers arising from the extended-target characteristics of the USV. Finally, we formulate a time allocation optimization problem to balance the time durations of the wide- and narrow-beam modes under different sea states, considering both robust USV state sensing and high-rate communication. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed scheme achieves consistently good tracking performance compared with conventional and neural-network-based methods.

papers.title: On the Comparison of Reinforcement Learning and Adaptive Control for Linear Systems under Packet Loss and Uncertainty
papers.summary: This paper presents a comparative study between Adaptive Quantized Control (AQC) and Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) reinforcement learning for uncertain linear systems with input quantization over communication channels subject to packet loss. The considered setting also includes dynamic switching from a nominal unstable system to a more unstable one during operation. The AQC is designed for unknown system dynamics using acknowledgment messages to compensate for packet losses, whereas the DDPG controller is trained using the nominal system model without acknowledgment messages. Numerical results show that the DDPG controller achieves faster transient responses and improved damping within its training environment. However, under model uncertainty, packet loss, and dynamic switching, the AQC consistently demonstrates superior robustness owing to its rigorous Lyapunov stability guarantees. These results highlight the trade-off between data-driven performance and model-based robustness, and provide insight into the applicability of reinforcement learning and adaptive control for networked uncertain systems.

papers.title: Shadow Pricing of Static Voltage Stability Services within Unit Commitment for Inverter-Dominated Power Systems
papers.summary: Modern power systems are increasingly dominated by Inverter-Based Resources (IBR), most of which work in Grid-following (GFL) mode. This implies that they do not directly control their terminal voltage, so the static voltage stability at these buses may be compromised, especially under constant-power-factor operation that lacks voltage-adaptive reactive support. In addition, weather-driven IBR are often installed in electrically remote areas with low Short-Circuit Ratio (SCR), further exacerbating voltage issues. To address this challenge, grid-forming control can be utilized to enhance low-SCR buses, while GFL-IBR could be explicitly required to provide voltage support through grid codes. As an alternative, a market mechanism could be devised that incentivizes relevant generators to proactively adjust their operating points as a service to maintain voltage stability, while the theoretical framework for such a market has not been developed. To fill this gap, this work adopts a second-order cone-based static voltage stability constraint for GFL-IBR buses within a unit commitment problem, and proposes a mechanism to assign shadow prices to this ancillary service. To determine appropriate price values under non-convex conditions, different pricing schemes are assessed. Using a modified IEEE 30-bus system, we demonstrate that both the dispatchable and restricted pricing methods can yield revenue-adequate service prices, though the former may deliver less efficient price signals and the latter may require well-defined uplift payments. This implies that, given differentiated pricing mechanisms and price signals, operators need to select a suitable pricing method in accordance with actual system conditions and market rules.

papers.title: Vertical Pinching Antenna Systems (V-PAS) Aided UAV Communications
papers.summary: To address the limitation that existing horizontal pinching antenna systems (H-PAS) are primarily designed for ground users and confined to two-dimensional (2D) coverage, this paper proposes deploying a pinching antenna (PA) along the facade of urban buildings to construct a vertical pinching antenna system (V-PAS) for ultra-low-altitude unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) communications. The proposed architecture employs a dielectric waveguide continuously deployed along the full height of buildings, extending the considered user service region of PAS from a 2D ground plane to a three-dimensional (3D) low-altitude airspace, enabling stable line-of-sight (LoS) links for "last meter" UAV communications. We define the concept of pinching multiplicative path loss (PMPL) to characterize the cascaded multiplicative attenuation of the waveguide and free-space path losses. It is found that PMPL is insensitive to vertical distance, rendering V-PAS highly adaptive to building heights. Furthermore, accurate and asymptotic closed-form expressions for outage probability and ergodic rate under lossy waveguide conditions are derived, respectively. The optimal access point (AP) height and PA position are further characterized, providing deployment insights for practical V-PAS. The results show that V-PAS achieves performance advantages over H-PAS and the benchmark without PA in most ultra-low-altitude UAV communication scenarios. Only under extremely high transmission power and large UAV operational area may the outage probability of V-PAS with a lossy waveguide be inferior to that of the benchmark without PA, but the ergodic rate of V-PAS still maintains an advantage. By contrast, V-PAS with a lossless waveguide outperforms the benchmark without PA in UAV communications, representing the theoretical performance upper bound of V-PAS.

papers.title: SPIRAL-PO: Symbolic Identification of Partially Observed Nonlinear Dynamics with Application to Rotating Machinery
papers.summary: Many engineering systems contain states that cannot be measured directly, yet these hidden states act on the measured outputs. We present SPIRAL-PO (Symbolic Physics-Informed Residual Augmentation Loop - Partially Observed), a framework for identifying an interpretable observable-space closure: a model, written in the measured coordinates, of how the unmeasured states act on the measured dynamics. A physics seed is augmented by candidate terms from a mechanism-labeled library; terms are selected by statistical tests designed for numerically differentiated, serially correlated data, using a weak (integral) formulation, and are checked on independent records. For an idealized regression we give sufficient conditions for recovering the closure coefficients, a rank condition under which no estimator can recover them, and a per-term detection bound; these results apply only to systems that admit an instantaneous observable closure. On a simulated four-degree-of-freedom vertical rotor with cubic bearing stiffness, in which only the lateral displacements are measured, the method recovers the gyroscopic and cubic-stiffness signatures of the hidden tilt dynamics in every noise realization at 2% noise; with a mechanism removed it never admits the cubic term and admits the gyroscopic term in 15-25% of realizations, above the nominal level, because the closure is only partly instantaneous. A residual network and a quasi-random projection stage add no measurable benefit, and pointwise tests that ignore the serial correlation of differentiated data admit absent mechanisms more often. On a laboratory rotor with simultaneous x,y measurement and an order-tracked speed, the method detects only a speed-dependent stiffening; gyroscopic and cubic terms obtained with an assumed constant-deceleration speed are consistent with the speed error, which produces such terms in simulation.

papers.title: Critical Inertia Estimation for the Three U.S. Interconnections
papers.summary: The rapid integration of inverter-based resources (IBRs) is reducing system inertia across U.S. power grids, raising concerns about frequency stability following large contingencies. This paper presents a simulation-based assessment of critical inertia--the minimum system inertia required to prevent first-stage under-frequency load shedding (UFLS) after the largest credible contingency--across the three major U.S. interconnections: Eastern Interconnection (EI), WECC, and ERCOT. Reduced-inertia scenarios are created by progressively replacing synchronous generators with IBRs, and dynamic simulations are performed using full-scale PSS(R)E and PowerWorld models. The results show that ERCOT reaches critical inertia at approximately 20% IBR penetration under the strict first-stage UFLS criterion--or approximately 58% if only the final UFLS stage must be avoided--compared with above 90% for EI and approximately 67%-68% for WECC. IBR shares in 2024 in the U.S. portions of EI, WECC, and ERCOT were 16%, 33%, and 44%, respectively, indicating varying proximity to critical inertia thresholds. These findings highlight the importance of full dynamic simulations to accurately estimate critical inertia and guide transmission planning under high renewable penetration scenarios.

papers.title: Antenna Positioning and Beamforming Optimization in MA Enabled Secure ISAC Systems: A Gradient-Based Meta Learning Approach
papers.summary: Integrated sensing and communications (ISAC) significantly improves spectral efficiency but introduces security risks regarding the interception of embedded communication signals. This paper proposes an movable antenna (MA)-enabled secure ISAC system that utilizes the spatial degrees of freedom of MA to mitigate these risks. Then, a problem is formulated to maximize the system secrecy rate by jointly optimizing antenna positioning, transmit beamforming, and artificial noise. However, the principal challenge arises from the non-convexity of the optimization problem and the strong coupling of the optimization variables. Generally, traditional optimization methods for this problem suffer from complex mathematical derivations, while existing deep learning approaches rely heavily on the training data distribution. To address these issues, we introduce a gradient-based meta learning (GML) algorithm, which works without pre-training and demonstrates favorable performance. Specifically, the algorithm establishes a neural network for each optimization variable, where the gradient of the objective function with respect to the variable serves as the input, and the output of the network determines the variable's update step. By handling the constraints and constructing penalty terms, the global loss function is used to guide the optimization process. Extensive numerical simulations confirm that the proposed algorithm achieves satisfactory performance in terms of both communication security and sensing capabilities.

papers.title: Multimodal Deep Learning for Uncertainty-Aware Radiation Pneumonitis Risk Prediction
papers.summary: Radiation pneumonitis (RP) is a potentially serious complication of thoracic radiotherapy, making reliable risk prediction important for identifying high-risk patients and guiding effective toxicity management. Although deep learning models can predict RP risk, uncertainty quantification remains underdeveloped in radiation toxicity assessment. We developed a Multimodal Bayesian Diffusion Transformer (MM-DiT) that integrates pretreatment computed tomography (CT) and three-dimensional planning dose distributions for RP risk prediction and uncertainty quantification. MM-DiT combines self-supervised multimodal representation learning with Bayesian classification to estimate individual risk and characterize aleatoric, epistemic, and label uncertainty. In independent Mount Sinai Health System (MSHS) and RTOG cohorts, MM-DiT achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUCs) of $0.89$ and $0.86$, respectively, with expected calibration errors of $0.02$ and $0.03$. Incorporating post-treatment CT increased AUC to $0.95$ in MSHS and reduced aleatoric and epistemic uncertainty by approximately $40-45\%$ and $40\%$, respectively. These findings establish a framework for uncertainty-aware radiation toxicity prediction that complements risk estimates with information about predictive reliability. By integrating multimodal learning and uncertainty quantification, MM-DiT may advance more interpretable and trustworthy AI-assisted toxicity assessment and support individualized radiotherapy planning.

papers.title: Utility-Aware Adaptive Downlink DM-RS Allocation from Uplink CSI for Lightweight O-DU dApps
papers.summary: Adaptive demodulation reference signal (DM-RS) placement in 5G New Radio (NR) trades pilot overhead against channel-tracking robustness, making a single static density suboptimal across heterogeneous mobility and propagation regimes. This paper studies a lightweight per-UE controller intended for O-DU-side distributed application (dApp) execution. The controller consumes eleven deployable uplink-CSI statistics and selects among six standards-derived PDSCH DM-RS configurations. Rather than optimize oracle-class accuracy, we train an 11-128-64-32-6 multilayer perceptron with a utility-aware objective that preserves the throughput structure of all candidate actions. In a large-scale trajectory-disjoint evaluation covering 294 channel/speed/SNR conditions and 7,056 observations, the proposed U-SoftCE policy significantly improves throughput over a training-selected best fixed pattern by 1.30, 0.86, and 1.13 percentage points on in-distribution, CDL channel-OOD, and 300-km/h mobility-OOD splits, respectively; paired 95% bootstrap intervals exclude zero in all three cases. An independent bit-accurate Sionna NR LDPC validation over 36 held-out conditions and 50 transport blocks per candidate retains a +1.21-point gain with a 95% cluster-bootstrap interval of [0.27, 2.13]. A native C++ implementation uses 12,070 dense parameters and requires 5.59 microseconds mean inference time, while a FlexRIC-based emulated O-DU prototype demonstrates sub-10-ms closed-loop operation. These results support utility-aware objectives for compact adaptive PHY controllers while exposing the limits of exact class-accuracy optimization.

papers.title: Reduced Order Observers for Monocular Visual Inertial Odometry
papers.summary: This work develops a reduced order observer framework of monocular visual-inertial odometry (VIO). The key idea consists in considering the gravity vector in the body-frame as an additional state and constructing an appropriate output that relates the monocular bearing measurements and their time derivatives to the body-frame velocity. This eliminates the need for the estimation of the landmark positions, leading to a six-dimensional linear time-varying (LTV) observer for the body-frame velocity and gravity, endowed with uniform global exponential stability guarantees. These estimates are subsequently used to recover the orientation almost globally, up to an unknown constant yaw offset, and the position up to an unknown constant translation. The mixed-bearing framework is further extended to account for the inertial measurement unit (IMU) biases, yielding a twelve-dimensional LTV observer endowed with local exponential stability guarantees. Numerical simulations are provided to illustrate the effectiveness of the proposed observers.

papers.title: Two-impulse Rendezvous Planning about Thrusting Spacecraft on SE2(3)
papers.summary: The classical Hill--Clohessy--Wiltshire equations assume an unforced Keplerian reference trajectory, an assumption that is violated by missions requiring continuous thrust. We formulate spacecraft relative motion on the $\mathrm{SE}_2(3)$ Lie group, which encodes position, velocity, and attitude in a single geometric state, linearize the gravity and body-frame control mismatches between the two vehicles, and derive analytic bounds on every neglected term. Under circular coasting Keplerian assumptions the framework recovers the Hill--Clohessy--Wiltshire equations exactly. For thrusting references the state transition matrix acquires thrust-induced attitude--translation coupling blocks that, when the two vehicles share body-frame inputs, are exact in log coordinates and independent of the attitude error, and a mismatch between the vehicles' inputs re-centers the linearization at their mean. A two-impulse rendezvous planner follows directly. A scalar coupling ratio, computable before planning, separates two regimes. Where it exceeds unity, the planner reduces the terminal error of coupling-blind planners by more than an order of magnitude, and somewhat above unity it is also more accurate than a Cartesian planner of the same computational structure; well below unity, simpler planners are adequate or better. Simulations confirm the recovery to machine precision and validate every bound along the transfer.

papers.title: AVSG: Accelerated Vectorized Sparse Gather for Efficient KV Cache Offload in Sparse-Attention LLM Serving
papers.summary: Dynamic sparse attention reduces long-context attention computation by selecting only a subset of tokens, but still requires access to the full KV cache, leaving serving memory-bound. Offloading the KV cache to host memory reduces device memory pressure but places H2D transfers on the decoding critical path. In DSA, substantial overlap in selected KV entries across decoding steps creates an opportunity for device-resident reuse. Exploiting this reuse efficiently, however, presents three critical challenges: costly matching of selected tokens against entries retained in the HBM buffer, uneven distribution of the remaining H2D transfers across accelerator cores, and retaining frequently accessed KV entries within limited HBM capacity. We present AVSG, an operator that addresses these challenges for DSA while preserving its exact token selections. AVSG uses vectorized hash matching to identify reusable HBM-buffer slots and reserve slots for entries requiring transfer, then evenly partitions these H2D transfers across accelerator cores. Lifetime-based buffer management retains frequently accessed KV entries in the device buffer across decoding steps, and shared slot reservations extend reuse across tokens within a multi-token prediction iteration. On a single NPU, vectorized hash matching is 2.80x faster than scalar dual-pointer matching, miss-only transfer raises effective H2D bandwidth by up to 34.44x over request-level assignment, and an 8K-entry buffer reaches a 94.83% hit rate on real requests. These gains translate into end-to-end improvement: on a serving stack processing a real-world production dataset, AVSG reduces time per output token by 39% and increases output throughput by 1.27x relative to the same KV offload layout without HBM-buffer reuse. The code of AVSG is released at https://gitcode.com/cann/cann-recipes-infer.

papers.title: Safe Unicycle Navigation Among Multiple Obstacles Under Bounded Disturbances: A Learning-Augmented CLF-CBF Approach (Extended Version)
papers.summary: This paper presents a robust control framework for safe navigation of a unicycle robot to a goal among multiple static obstacles under an unknown, time-varying disturbance. The controller solves a single real-time quadratic program (QP) that combines a goal-reaching term with one safety term per obstacle. The goal-reaching term is a cross-track control Lyapunov function built from body-frame tracking errors rather than a bearing angle, which keeps its Lie derivatives bounded everywhere, including the goal. Safety is encoded using robust control barrier functions, one per obstacle, each tightened by a closed-form, state-dependent disturbance bound. When stabilization and safety conflict, a slack variable relaxes only the convergence requirement, so that the safety constraints remain strictly enforced. Whenever the QP is feasible, the robust barrier constraints guarantee forward invariance of every obstacle's safe set under all admissible disturbances. Complementing this safety guarantee, a Lyapunov analysis yields an explicit ultimate bound on the distance to the goal. A learning-augmented variant replaces the fixed objective with a reinforcement-learning reference, which accelerates convergence when multiple constraints are simultaneously active. We further derive the obstacle separation below which the gap between two obstacles becomes too narrow to pass through under the robust constraints. For such gaps, a learned virtual goal for the Lyapunov function steers the robot around the obstacles without compromising safety. Simulations, a Monte Carlo study, and a comparison against a sampled-data robust baseline support the theoretical results.

papers.title: Global Parameter Identification and Uncertainty Quantification of reduced-order ADM1 using Maximum Likelihood Estimation and Bayesian Inference
papers.summary: Anaerobic digestion (AD) models can be challenging to calibrate against real data due to limited practical identifiability, data scarcity, and model complexity. Weighted least squares objective functions and gradient-based solvers using finite differences are often used in literature, but result in suboptimal parameter estimates and large uncertainty bands. This paper identifies the parameters of a reduced-order ADM1 by comparing the frameworks of maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) and Bayesian inference (BI), and quantifies uncertainties of parameters and outputs. Multirate experimental data are taken from a lab-scale AD reactor fed with agricultural substrates and operated at organic loading rates of 3$\,$g VS $\mathrm{m^{-3}d^{-1}}$. Global optima are found via global and gradient-based local search algorithms using forward sensitivities. Enhanced scatter search provides the best global search results. These are refined by the Gauss-Newton algorithm as the best local search, which delivers $R^2$ values of 0.95 for acetic acid and 0.77 for biogas production. BI yields substantially narrower uncertainty bands than MLE and avoids the need for a global search by incorporating prior knowledge about parameter distributions. The search space is captured efficiently by log10 scaling of parameters. Algorithmic details on its implications are provided. Despite a high-resolution lab-scale dataset, the ADM1-specific inhibition parameter $K_\mathrm{I,nh3}$ is practically not identifiable with MLE, and shows a low output sensitivity, whereas a parameter for the effective ion concentration shows superb practical identifiabilty at high confidence with both MLE and BI. The present work lays a scalable base for calibration of nonlinear AD models by providing reliable simulations. It thus advances model-based monitoring and control applications of multirate processes such as agricultural AD plants.

papers.title: Per-Bundle, Pre-Reconstruction Inversion for Temporal CT: Flux-Compensation Design and Training-Free Empirical-Bayes Estimation
papers.summary: In Temporal computed tomography (TCT) each detector reading sums the photons of up to three rays. Earlier work set the resulting per-bundle limits and tested a learned prior on one patient at one incident count $N_0$; this paper lifts both. N$_0$FC ($N_0$ flux compensation), a bow-tie and tube-current-modulation co-design, equalizes each bundle's detected flux. SNN2 is a per-bundle Poisson maximum-likelihood estimator. V8c is a neural-network corrector trained on 19 patients stratified by water-equivalent diameter (WED). T2bp, a training-free empirical-Bayes post-processor, combines per-bundle Poisson likelihoods with a prior built from the patient's own bundles. Results use that work's Dose Inflation Factor (DIF), charging bias as error. On 23 non-test volumes, N$_0$FC lowers the per-volume median middle-path Cramer-Rao floor, as a DIF, from 23-48 under a flat-fluence (no bow-tie) baseline to 3.3-6.3 at 35-62% of its incident photons, near the equal-attenuation value 13/3 and 1.4-1.7 times below conventional bow-ties; the bow-tie alone achieves this median, and tube-current modulation trims the tail. For bundles with $X_2<6$ (83%), SNN2 attains this floor (median mean-squared-error ratio 1.02); training-free T2bp$\circ$SNN2 lowers the ratio to 0.89 (0.74-1.26). It is best or tied on three of four N$_0$FC test cells (WED 207-342 mm) and trails T2bp$\circ$V8c by 3% on the fourth. V8c beats SNN2 in distribution under baseline acquisition, gains at most 9% under N$_0$FC (losing 14% on the largest in-distribution test patient), and fails on a patient acquired below its training count level. Acquisition co-design removes most of the attenuation-contrast penalty, and training-free estimation attains the resulting limit. The remaining three- to six-fold gap to single-source CT at equal fluence, and the high-attenuation tail, are targets for inter-bundle priors.

papers.title: Keep Pace to Learn: Movable-Antenna Compensation of Channel Aging in Over-the-Air Split Learning
papers.summary: Split learning (SL) trains a neural network across devices by exchanging intermediate activations and gradients. In over-the-air SL, the wireless channel serves as an inter-layer linear map, and when the forward and backward channels match, reciprocity and conjugation supply the backward product without channel estimation at the base station (BS). Passive user motion, which the learning link does not control, breaks this match. Movable antennas let the antenna move relative to the user device, and we use this freedom to compensate the displacement. For a stationary BS and a propagation environment quasi-static within each exchange, returning the antenna to its forward-transmission position restores the channel and yields a conditionally unbiased gradient estimate. We also derive when discrete positioning or mechanical movement can achieve this in time. A residual displacement below a quarter wavelength keeps the real part of the channel correlation positive for any angular spectrum. At zero effective offset, independent Gaussian jitter attenuates this correlation without reversing its sign, whereas a persistent offset can reverse it, and in arrays the tolerance depends on the receive-combining direction. These effects enter a nonconvex convergence bound, and a local analysis shows that partial mechanical compensation saves cycle time to first order at only a second-order loss in correlation. In CIFAR-10 experiments, a user terminal without channel state information stays at chance level under uncompensated walking motion, while discrete positioning stays within about 0.3 percentage points of exact restoration, including at a speed beyond the modeled actuator's limit.

papers.title: Geometry-Conditioned Target Speaker Extraction based on spatial features incorporating acoustic propagation principles
papers.summary: Recently, spatially selective non-linear filter (SSF) was proposed for target speaker extraction, utilizing the direction-of-arrival (DOA) of the target speaker as a spatial cue. To overcome its dependency on a fixed microphone array geometry, geometry-conditioned SSF (GCSSF) was proposed, which maps the target DOA and the microphone positions into abstract high-dimensional embeddings using positional encoding. As an alternative to these high-dimensional embeddings, in this paper we propose utilizing two spatial features incorporating acoustic propagation principles for geometry conditioning: 1) the steering vector of the target speaker, which captures inter-microphone phase differences, and 2) a spatial mask based on GCC-PHAT, which quantifies presence of the target speaker per time-frequency bin. These features are used as input to a geometry-conditioning encoder and integrated via a FiLM layer into the GCSSF system. Experimental results on circular and random arrays demonstrate that conditioning with spatial features improves target extraction performance compared to abstract high-dimensional embeddings, maintaining a clear performance advantage across a wide range of target DOA errors.

papers.title: Pilot Decontamination via Data-aided Channel Tracking in Cell-free Massive MIMO
papers.summary: As cell-free massive MIMO emerges as a promising technology for future wireless networks, robust channel estimation becomes increasingly important. Channel estimation relies on pilot transmissions, and with increasing number of users, pilot reuse inevitably introduces contamination that degrades channel estimation and symbol detection. This limitation is compounded by rapidly evolving channels, which render the estimates obsolete over time. To address both the problems, viz. pilot contamination and channel aging without additional pilot overhead, we propose a Kalman filter-based data-aided channel tracking strategy. By leveraging the symbol estimates as virtual pilots, the proposed approach successively refines the channel estimates over time. Unlike the conventional Kalman filter model, here, the observation model depends on symbol estimates, introducing symbol uncertainty that gets coupled with channel uncertainty. This requires a careful calculation of the innovation covariance matrices. Additionally, we discuss a stochastic-gradient-descent based tracking approach with low computational complexity. Extensive simulations are used to demonstrate that successive refinement progressively decontaminates the channel estimate, achieving lower channel estimation error and improved spectral efficiency.

papers.title: Constrained Sparsest Input Selection for Structural Controllability is NP-Hard
papers.summary: We study the problem of selecting the fewest admissible input--state links that make a structured linear system structurally controllable. This objective counts nonzero entries from prescribed positions of the input matrix and is different from minimizing its number of nonzero columns. Prior work gives polynomial-time algorithms for several restricted cases, including single or dedicated inputs and prescribed input patterns satisfying additional graph-theoretic conditions. We give a polynomial-time reduction from perfect three-dimensional matching, establishing for the first time that the decision problem is NP-complete and the optimization problem is NP-hard. A refinement of the reduction yields an exact optimum relation and shows that the problem is APX-hard. An example also exhibits a strict integrality gap for the natural linear programming relaxation.

papers.title: Reducing 6G Energy Consumption: TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation for Power Amplifiers
papers.summary: The Power Amplifier (PA) of a base station operates inefficiently at partial load, where back-off from the peak output power wastes supply headroom. Adapting the PA drain voltage to the instantaneous signal recovers this loss but requires frequent switching, increasing hardware cost. We propose TDD-Aligned Drain Voltage Modulation (TDD-DVM), a drain voltage modulation scheme that instead selects the drain voltage level once per Time-Division Duplex (TDD) period based on the downlink resource load and switches the voltage during the uplink window. This is enabled by the authors' previous work on POLITE link adaptation, which spreads the transmit power over resources left unused at partial load and moves the PA into a regime where a lower drain voltage suffices. In a 3GPP Urban Macro system-level simulation across traffic loads, we compare TDD-DVM against baseline approaches under conventional and POLITE link adaptation. At equal delivered throughput, TDD-DVM with POLITE keeps the packet failure ratio of the full drain voltage while consuming up to 35% less power than it under conventional link adaptation and up to 7% less than it under POLITE, capturing most of the gain of an idealized reference at moderate loads and roughly half at the highest load.

papers.title: Weak and Strong Data Informativity with Structural Priors for System Analysis
papers.summary: When measurement data are insufficient for unique system identification, data informativity evaluates whether a dataset determines a property across all systems consistent with the data. This paper introduces a unified framework distinguishing between weak and strong data informativity under prior structural knowledge described by affine constraints: data are weakly informative if at least one system consistent with the data and prior knowledge possesses the target property, and strongly informative if every consistent system satisfies it. The latter is consistent with the notion of data informativity in the existing literature. By explicitly parameterizing all consistent systems as affine functions of free parameters via the Moore-Penrose pseudoinverse, we characterize these notions for fundamental system properties-including controllability, stabilizability, and stability. This formulation establishes that verifying weak and strong informativity, when tractable, reduces to rank tests of matrix pencils constructed from the data and prior knowledge. Our findings show that structural priors can lower data-excitation requirements and enable reliable analysis even when data fail to be strongly informative. Finally, the framework is extended to a class of noisy data.

papers.title: Sensing Fast and Distant Targets in Fractional Overspread Channels with Zak-OTFS and Modular Arithmetic
papers.summary: Delay-Doppler (DD) modulations, such as Zak-transform-based orthogonal time frequency space (Zak-OTFS) modulation, represent the channel as a sparse set of delay and Doppler shifts, which makes them well suited for radar sensing. Sensing with a single DD frame, however, is unambiguous only when the channel spread factor, i.e., the product of the delay and Doppler spreads, is less then one. Long-range mobility scenarios, including drones, airplanes, low Earth orbit (LEO) satellites, and underwater acoustic links, typically violate this crystallization condition, so that a single frame aliases the target delays, Doppler shifts, or both. Existing methods add a time-frequency pilot to a conventional DD frame, resolve the aliasing in only one dimension, and assume integer delays and Doppler shifts. We propose a frame design that combines multiple DD bases with different delay and Doppler periods, which together cover an overspread channel with fractional delays and Doppler shifts, using the same bandwidth and frame size. We show that modular arithmetic on the peak positions uniquely recovers each target by pairing the peaks through their common projection and their gains, and we derive the condition under which this pairing is ambiguous. We implement the design with two superimposed Zak-OTFS frames and propose two receivers: dual-frame sensing (DS), which performs the joint detection directly, and DS with cross-pilot cancellation (DS-XC), which additionally cancels the cross-pilot interference, re-estimates the gains by joint least squares, and removes ghost targets. Both receivers maintain a detection rate close to one as the spread factor grows, and DS-XC also achieves the lowest false-alarm rate and channel estimation error among all the compared systems. In a 100 km drone scenario, DS-XC outperforms all baselines, with a complexity that grows near-linearly with the time-bandwidth product.
